## File: src/1/chat-content.md
`````markdown
  1: # Chat Content Integration
  2: 
  3: ## Problem Identified
  4: 
  5: The system is not properly including page content in prompts:
  6: ```javascript
  7: // Current output shows content issue
  8: Chat component content type: string
  9: Chat component content length: 15
 10: Chat component content preview: [object Object]
 11: ```
 12: 
 13: ## Solution
 14: 
 15: ### 1. Content Processing in Text.astro
 16: ```typescript
 17: // Get the raw content
 18: const { frontmatter, content } = Astro.props;
 19: 
 20: // Process content properly
 21: const rawContent = typeof content === 'object' 
 22:   ? content.toString()
 23:   : content;
 24: 
 25: // Clean content
 26: const cleanContent = rawContent
 27:   .replace(/^---[\s\S]*?---/, '') // Remove frontmatter
 28:   .trim();
 29: 
 30: // Pass to Chat component
 31: <Chat 
 32:   chatConfig={chatConfig} 
 33:   content={cleanContent}
 34: />
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: ### 2. Update Chat Component
 38: ```typescript
 39: // src/components/Chat.tsx
 40: interface ChatProps {
 41:   chatConfig: ChatConfig;
 42:   content: string;
 43: }
 44: 
 45: // Log content properly
 46: console.log('Content:', {
 47:   type: typeof content,
 48:   length: content.length,
 49:   preview: content.substring(0, 100)
 50: });
 51: 
 52: // Add content to system prompt
 53: const systemPrompt = [
 54:   chatConfig.systemPrompt,
 55:   chatConfig.includeContent && {
 56:     type: 'text' as const,
 57:     text: `${chatConfig.contentPrefix || 'Content:'}\n${content}`
 58:   }
 59: ].filter(Boolean);
 60: ```
 61: 
 62: ### 3. API Integration
 63: ```typescript
 64: // src/pages/api/chatsimple.ts
 65: const messages = [
 66:   {
 67:     role: 'system',
 68:     content: [
 69:       ...systemPrompt,
 70:       {
 71:         type: 'text',
 72:         text: config.includeContent 
 73:           ? `${config.contentPrefix || 'Content:'}\n${config.content}`
 74:           : ''
 75:       }
 76:     ].filter(text => text)
 77:   }
 78: ];
 79: ```
 80: 
 81: ## Implementation Steps
 82: 
 83: 1. **Process Content First**
 84:    - Convert content object to string
 85:    - Remove frontmatter
 86:    - Clean whitespace
 87:    - Truncate if needed
 88: 
 89: 2. **Update System Prompt**
 90:    - Include base prompts (1.md, business.md)
 91:    - Add page-specific prompt
 92:    - Append cleaned content
 93: 
 94: 3. **Send to API**
 95:    - Combine all prompt parts
 96:    - Include content section
 97:    - Maintain proper structure
 98: 
 99: ## Example Usage
100: 
101: ```yaml
102: ---
103: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
104: title: Documentation
105: includeContent: true
106: contentPrefix: "Reference Material:"
107: systemPrompt: |
108:   You are a documentation expert.
109:   Use the following content to answer questions:
110: ---
111: 
112: # Documentation Content
113: 
114: This content should be included in the prompt...
115: ```
116: 
117: ## Expected Output
118: 
119: ```javascript
120: // Content logs should show:
121: Chat component content type: string
122: Chat component content length: 42
123: Chat component content preview: "# Documentation Content\n\nThis content should..."
124: 
125: // Final system message:
126: {
127:   role: 'system',
128:   content: [
129:     { type: 'text', text: '1.md content...' },
130:     { type: 'text', text: 'business.md content...' },
131:     { type: 'text', text: 'System prompt...' },
132:     { type: 'text', text: 'Reference Material:\n# Documentation Content...' }
133:   ]
134: }
135: ```
136: 
137: ## Debug Checklist
138: 
139: 1. Check content object conversion
140: 2. Verify frontmatter removal
141: 3. Confirm content cleaning
142: 4. Test prompt assembly
143: 5. Validate API message structure
`````

## File: src/1/chat-schema.md
`````markdown
  1: # Chat Schema with Content Support
  2: 
  3: ## Base Schema
  4: 
  5: ```typescript
  6: const BaseChatSchema = {
  7:   // Existing fields from current schema
  8:   layout: string().optional(),
  9:   title: string().optional(),
 10:   // ... other existing fields ...
 11: 
 12:   // New content handling fields
 13:   includeContent: boolean().default(true),
 14:   contentPrefix: string().default("Context:"),
 15:   contentMaxLength: number().default(2000)
 16: }
 17: ```
 18: 
 19: ## Prompt Assembly
 20: 
 21: The system combines prompts in this order:
 22: 
 23: 1. Base system prompt from `1.md` (if `addSystemPrompt: true`)
 24:    ```typescript
 25:    if (config.addSystemPrompt) {
 26:      prompts.push(loadPromptContent('src/1/1.md'));
 27:    }
 28:    ```
 29: 
 30: 2. Business context from `business.md` (if `addBusinessPrompt: true`)
 31:    ```typescript
 32:    if (config.addBusinessPrompt) {
 33:      prompts.push(loadPromptContent('src/1/business.md'));
 34:    }
 35:    ```
 36: 
 37: 3. Page-specific system prompt (if provided)
 38:    ```typescript
 39:    if (config.systemPrompt) {
 40:      prompts.push(config.systemPrompt);
 41:    }
 42:    ```
 43: 
 44: 4. Page content (if `includeContent: true`)
 45:    ```typescript
 46:    if (config.includeContent && config.content) {
 47:      prompts.push(
 48:        `${config.contentPrefix}\n${
 49:          truncate(config.content, config.contentMaxLength)
 50:        }`
 51:      );
 52:    }
 53:    ```
 54: 
 55: ## Content Handling
 56: 
 57: Content is processed before being added to the prompt:
 58: 
 59: ```typescript
 60: function processContent(content: string, maxLength: number): string {
 61:   // Remove frontmatter
 62:   const cleanContent = content.replace(/^---[\s\S]*?---/, '');
 63:   
 64:   // Clean and normalize
 65:   const normalized = cleanContent
 66:     .trim()
 67:     .replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n');
 68:     
 69:   // Truncate if needed
 70:   return truncate(normalized, maxLength);
 71: }
 72: ```
 73: 
 74: ## Example Usage
 75: 
 76: ```yaml
 77: ---
 78: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
 79: title: Documentation Page
 80: includeContent: true
 81: contentPrefix: "Page Content:"
 82: contentMaxLength: 1500
 83: systemPrompt: "Answer questions about this documentation..."
 84: ---
 85: 
 86: # Page Content
 87: 
 88: This content will be included in the system prompt...
 89: ```
 90: 
 91: ## Benefits
 92: 
 93: 1. **Context Awareness**
 94:    - AI has access to page content
 95:    - Can reference specific details
 96:    - More accurate responses
 97: 
 98: 2. **Configurability**
 99:    - Enable/disable per page
100:    - Custom prefix
101:    - Length control
102: 
103: 3. **Performance**
104:    - Content truncation prevents token limits
105:    - Clean content processing
106:    - Efficient prompt assembly
`````

## File: src/1/content-guide.md
`````markdown
  1: # Content-Aware Chat System Guide
  2: 
  3: ## Overview
  4: 
  5: The content-aware chat system allows the AI to understand and reference page-specific content while maintaining its general knowledge capabilities. This creates a more contextual and accurate chat experience.
  6: 
  7: ## Implementation Approaches
  8: 
  9: ### 1. Basic Content Inclusion
 10: 
 11: ```yaml
 12: ---
 13: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
 14: title: Simple Page
 15: includeContent: true
 16: systemPrompt: "Reference the content when answering questions."
 17: ---
 18: 
 19: Your page content here...
 20: ```
 21: 
 22: ### 2. Documentation Assistant
 23: 
 24: ```yaml
 25: ---
 26: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
 27: title: API Documentation
 28: includeContent: true
 29: contentPrefix: "### API Documentation:"
 30: systemPrompt: "You are a technical documentation expert. Explain concepts from the documentation clearly and accurately."
 31: suggestions:
 32:   - "What are the key endpoints?"
 33:   - "How do I authenticate?"
 34:   - "Show me example usage"
 35: ---
 36: 
 37: API documentation content...
 38: ```
 39: 
 40: ### 3. Learning Assistant
 41: 
 42: ```yaml
 43: ---
 44: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
 45: title: Tutorial
 46: includeContent: true
 47: contentPrefix: "### Tutorial Content:"
 48: systemPrompt: "You are a patient teacher. Help users understand concepts from the tutorial. Provide examples and explanations based on the tutorial content."
 49: suggestions:
 50:   - "Explain this concept"
 51:   - "Show me an example"
 52:   - "What's next?"
 53: ---
 54: 
 55: Tutorial content...
 56: ```
 57: 
 58: ## Content Processing
 59: 
 60: The system automatically:
 61: 1. Strips frontmatter
 62: 2. Cleans formatting
 63: 3. Truncates if needed
 64: 4. Adds to system prompt
 65: 
 66: ## Best Practices
 67: 
 68: ### Content Structure
 69: - Use clear headings
 70: - Keep sections focused
 71: - Include important details
 72: - Use consistent formatting
 73: 
 74: ### Configuration
 75: - Set appropriate content length limits
 76: - Customize prefix for content type
 77: - Craft specific system prompts
 78: - Add relevant suggestions
 79: 
 80: ### System Prompt Design
 81: - Tell AI to reference content
 82: - Define its role clearly
 83: - Specify how to handle missing info
 84: - Include citation instructions
 85: 
 86: ## Common Patterns
 87: 
 88: 1. **Documentation Helper**
 89:    ```yaml
 90:    systemPrompt: "Explain documentation concepts. Always cite sections."
 91:    ```
 92: 
 93: 2. **Tutorial Guide**
 94:    ```yaml
 95:    systemPrompt: "Walk through concepts step by step using tutorial content."
 96:    ```
 97: 
 98: 3. **Content Summarizer**
 99:    ```yaml
100:    systemPrompt: "Summarize and explain key points from the content."
101:    ```
102: 
103: ## Advanced Usage
104: 
105: ### Combining Knowledge Sources
106: 
107: ```yaml
108: addSystemPrompt: true      # Include core knowledge
109: addBusinessPrompt: true    # Include business context
110: includeContent: true       # Include page content
111: ```
112: 
113: ### Content Processing Control
114: 
115: ```yaml
116: contentMaxLength: 2000     # Limit content length
117: contentPrefix: "custom:"   # Custom prefix
118: ```
119: 
120: ### Response Styling
121: 
122: ```yaml
123: systemPrompt: |
124:   When answering:
125:   1. Quote relevant sections
126:   2. Provide examples
127:   3. Link related concepts
128: ```
129: 
130: ## Benefits
131: 
132: 1. **Accuracy**
133:    - Responses based on actual content
134:    - Verifiable references
135:    - Clear source attribution
136: 
137: 2. **Flexibility**
138:    - Works with any content type
139:    - Customizable per page
140:    - Adaptable to different uses
141: 
142: 3. **User Experience**
143:    - Contextual responses
144:    - Relevant suggestions
145:    - Immediate access to content
146: 
147: 4. **Maintenance**
148:    - Content updates automatically reflected
149:    - No manual syncing needed
150:    - Easy to modify behavior
`````

## File: src/1/content-handling.md
`````markdown
 1: # Content Handling in Chat System
 2: 
 3: ## Current Structure in ai.md
 4: ```yaml
 5: ---
 6: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
 7: title: ONE License
 8: # ... other frontmatter ...
 9: ---
10: # This is some contnet
11: the secret is xoxoxo
12: ```
13: 
14: ## Required Changes in schema/chat.ts
15: 
16: 1. **Content Inclusion**
17: ```typescript
18: function combinePrompts(config: BaseChat, content?: string): ContentPart[] {
19:   const prompts: string[] = [];
20: 
21:   // Add base prompts
22:   if (config.addSystemPrompt) {
23:     const systemPrompt = loadPromptContent('src/1/1.md');
24:     if (systemPrompt) prompts.push(systemPrompt);
25:   }
26: 
27:   if (config.addBusinessPrompt) {
28:     const businessPrompt = loadPromptContent('src/1/business.md');
29:     if (businessPrompt) prompts.push(businessPrompt);
30:   }
31: 
32:   // Add page specific prompt
33:   if (config.systemPrompt) {
34:     prompts.push(typeof config.systemPrompt === 'string' 
35:       ? config.systemPrompt 
36:       : config.systemPrompt.map(p => p.text).join('\n\n')
37:     );
38:   }
39: 
40:   // Add page content
41:   if (content) {
42:     prompts.push(`Page Content:\n${content}`);
43:   }
44: 
45:   return prompts.map(text => ({
46:     type: 'text' as const,
47:     text: text.trim()
48:   }));
49: }
`````

`````markdown
 1: # Content Prompt System
 2: 
 3: ## Overview
 4: 
 5: A simple system to include page content in chat system prompts.
 6: 
 7: ## Implementation Plan
 8: 
 9: 1. **Content Extraction**
10:    - Get raw content from markdown file
11:    - Strip frontmatter
12:    - Clean any special characters/formatting
13: 
14: 2. **Configuration Options**
15:    ```yaml
16:    includeContent: true            # Enable/disable content inclusion
17:    contentPrefix: "Context:"       # Prefix for content section
18:    contentMaxLength: 2000         # Maximum content length
19:    ```
20: 
21: 3. **Prompt Assembly Order**
22:    1. System prompt (if addSystemPrompt: true)
23:    2. Business prompt (if addBusinessPrompt: true)
24:    3. Page specific prompt (if systemPrompt exists)
25:    4. Content section (if includeContent: true)
26:       ```
27:       Context:
28:       [Cleaned page content here]
29:       ```
30: 
31: 4. **Usage in Frontmatter**
32:    ```yaml
33:    ---
34:    layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
35:    title: Some Page
36:    description: Description
37:    includeContent: true
38:    contentPrefix: "Reference Material:"
39:    systemPrompt: "You are a helpful assistant..."
40:    ---
41:    ```
42: 
43: ## Components to Update
44: 
45: 1. `src/schema/chat.ts`
46:    - Add content handling options to schema
47:    - Update prompt assembly logic
48: 
49: 2. `src/layouts/Text.astro`
50:    - Pass cleaned content to chat component
51:    - Handle content truncation
52: 
53: 3. `src/components/Chat.tsx`
54:    - Use assembled prompt including content
55:    - Handle content updates
56: 
57: ## Benefits
58: - Simple opt-in content inclusion
59: - Configurable per page
60: - Clear separation of concerns
61: - Easy to extend
`````

335: ## 2. Zod as Single Source of Truth
336: 
337: I use Zod as the single source of truth for all data validation and typing in my projects. This ensures:
338: 
339: 1. **Schema Definition:**
340:    ```typescript
341:    import { z } from 'zod';
342:    
343:    // Define schema once, use everywhere
344:    const configSchema = z.object({
345:      title: z.string(),
346:      version: z.number(),
347:      features: z.array(z.string()),
348:      settings: z.object({
349:        theme: z.enum(['light', 'dark']),
350:        language: z.string(),
351:      }),
352:    });
353:    
354:    // TypeScript type is automatically inferred
355:    type Config = z.infer<typeof configSchema>;
356:    ```
357: 
358: 2. **Runtime Validation:**
359:    ```typescript
360:    // Validate data at runtime
361:    const validateConfig = (data: unknown) => {
362:      return configSchema.parse(data);
363:    };
364:    ```
365: 
366: 3. **Type Safety:**
367:    ```typescript
368:    // TypeScript knows the exact shape
369:    const config: Config = validateConfig(data);
370:    ```
371: 
372: **Key Benefits:**
373: - Single schema definition for both runtime validation and TypeScript types
374: - Automatic type inference eliminates type duplication
375: - Runtime type checking catches invalid data early
376: - Excellent IDE support and type hints
377: - Composable and reusable schemas
378: 
379: **Best Practices:**
380: - Define schemas in dedicated type files (src/types/*)
381: - Use schema composition for complex types
382: - Leverage Zod's rich validation features
383: - Export both schema and inferred type
384: - Add JSDoc comments for better documentation
385: 
386: ## 3. Step by Step
387: 
388: I use Zod as a single source of truth in my Astro project enhances both type safety and data validation. Astro utilizes Zod to define content schemas, ensuring that each file's data within a collection is validated and automatically typed in TypeScript. 
389: 
390: 
391: 1. **Define Your Schema with Zod:**
392:    Begin by creating a Zod schema that outlines the structure and validation rules for your content.
393: 
394:    ```typescript
395:    import { z } from 'zod';
396: 
397:    const blogPostSchema = z.object({
398:      title: z.string(),
399:      date: z.string().transform((str) => new Date(str)),
400:      tags: z.array(z.string()),
401:      content: z.string(),
402:    });
403:    ```
404: 
405: 2. **Infer TypeScript Types:**
406:    Leverage Zod's type inference to generate corresponding TypeScript types, ensuring consistency between your schema and types.
407: 
408:    ```typescript
409:    type BlogPost = z.infer<typeof blogPostSchema>;
410:    ```
411: 
412: 3. **Validate Content Data:**
413:    When loading or processing content, use the schema to validate the data, catching any discrepancies at runtime.
414: 
415:    ```typescript
416:    import blogPostData from './post.json';
417: 
418:    const parsedPost = blogPostSchema.parse(blogPostData);
419:    ```
420: 
421: **Benefits of Using Zod in Astro:**
422: 
423: - **Single Source of Truth:** By defining your data structures with Zod schemas, you maintain a single source of truth for both validation and TypeScript types, reducing redundancy and potential inconsistencies. 
424: 
425: - **Enhanced Type Safety:** Zod's integration ensures that your content adheres to the defined schemas, providing automatic TypeScript types and minimizing runtime errors. 
426: 
427: - **Runtime Validation:** Zod performs runtime checks, ensuring that external data sources, such as user inputs or API responses, conform to expected formats.

 1: import { completeJsxTag } from "@/lib/jsx-utils";

 5: interface JsxRendererProps extends React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> {
 6: 	jsx: string;
 7: 	fixIncompleteJsx?: boolean;
 8: 	components: Record<string, React.ComponentType>;
 9: }
10: 
11: const JsxRenderer = React.forwardRef<JsxParser, JsxRendererProps>(
12: 	({ className, jsx, fixIncompleteJsx = true, components }, ref) => {

17: 		return (
18: 			<JsxParser
19: 				ref={ref}
20: 				className={className}
21: 				jsx={processedJsx}
22: 				components={components}
23: 			/>
24: 		);
25: 	},
26: );

32:   useEffect(() => {
33:     const canvas = canvasRef.current;
34:     if (!canvas) return;
35: 
36:     try {
37:       window.TagCanvas.Start(canvas.id, `tags-${id}`, {
38:         dragControl,
39:         textColour: null,
40:         dragThreshold: 4,
41:         initial: [0.1, -0.1],
42:         maxSpeed: 0.04,
43:         minSpeed: 0.02,
44:         decel: 0.95,
45:         reverse: true,
46:         ...options,
47:       });
48:     } catch (error) {
49:       console.error("Error initializing TagCanvas:", error);
50:     }
51: 
52:     return () => {
53:       try {
54:         window.TagCanvas.Delete(canvas.id);
55:       } catch (error) {
56:         console.error("Error cleaning up TagCanvas:", error);
57:       }
58:     };
59:   }, [dragControl, id, options]);
60: 
61:   return (
62:     <div {...props}>
63:       <canvas
64:         id={`canvas-${id}`}
65:         ref={canvasRef}
66:         width={600}
67:         height={600}
68:         {...canvasProps}
69:       />
70:       <div id={`tags-${id}`} className="hidden">
71:         {children}
72:       </div>
73:     </div>
74:   );
75: }
`````

## File: src/components/magicui/icon-cloud.tsx
`````typescript
 1: "use client";
 2: 
 3: import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
 4: import { Icon } from "@iconify/react";
 5: 
 6: interface IconCloudProps {
 7:   iconSlugs: string[];
 8: }
 9: 
10: export default function IconCloud({ iconSlugs }: IconCloudProps) {
11:   const [isLoaded, setIsLoaded] = useState(false);
12:   const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
13: 
14:   useEffect(() => {
15:     if (!containerRef.current) return;
16:     setIsLoaded(true);
17: 
18:     const icons = containerRef.current.getElementsByClassName("icon-item");
19:     Array.from(icons).forEach((icon, index) => {
20: 
21:       const phi = Math.acos(-1 + (2 * index) / icons.length);
22:       const theta = Math.sqrt(icons.length * Math.PI) * phi;
23: 
24: 
25:       const radius = Math.min(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight) * 0.4;
26:       const x = Math.cos(theta) * Math.sin(phi);
27:       const y = Math.sin(theta) * Math.sin(phi);
28:       const z = Math.cos(phi);
29: 
30: 
31:       const el = icon as HTMLElement;
32:       el.style.setProperty("--x", `${x * radius}px`);
33:       el.style.setProperty("--y", `${y * radius}px`);
34:       el.style.setProperty("--z", `${z * radius}px`);
35:       el.style.setProperty("--delay", `${index * 100}ms`);
36:     });
37:   }, []);
38: 
39:   return (
40:     <div
41:       ref={containerRef}
42:       className={`fixed inset-0 transition-opacity duration-1000 ${
43:         isLoaded ? "opacity-100" : "opacity-0"
44:       }`}
45:     >
46:       <div className="absolute left-1/2 top-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 animate-spin-slow">
47:         {iconSlugs.map((slug) => (
48:           <div
49:             key={slug}
50:             className="icon-item absolute left-1/2 top-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2"
51:             style={{
52:               animation: "orbit 30s linear infinite",
53:               animationDelay: `var(--delay)`,
54:               transform: "translate3d(var(--x), var(--y), var(--z))",
55:             }}
56:           >
57:             <Icon
58:               icon={slug}
59:               className="h-8 w-8 md:h-12 md:w-12 transition-all duration-300 hover:scale-150"
60:               style={{
61:                 filter: "drop-shadow(0 0 12px rgba(var(--primary-rgb), 0.3))",
62:               }}
63:             />
64:           </div>
65:         ))}
66:       </div>
67:     </div>
68:   );
69: }
`````

## File: src/components/magicui/render-simple-icon.tsx
`````typescript
 1: "use client";
 2: 
 3: import type { HTMLAttributes } from "react";
 4: import { getContrastRatio, hexToRgb } from "./utils";
 5: 
 6: export interface Icon {
 7:   title: string;
 8:   slug: string;
 9:   svg: string;
10:   hex: string;
11:   source: string;
12: }
13: 
14: interface RenderSimpleIconProps {
15:   icon: Icon;
16:   bgHex?: string;
17:   fallbackHex?: string;
18:   minContrastRatio?: number;
19:   size?: number;
20:   aProps?: HTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement>;
21:   imgProps?: HTMLAttributes<HTMLImageElement>;
22: }
23: 
24: export function renderSimpleIcon({
25:   icon,
26:   bgHex = "#fff",
27:   fallbackHex = "#000",
28:   minContrastRatio = 1,
29:   size = 42,
30:   aProps,
31:   imgProps,
32: }: RenderSimpleIconProps) {
33:   const iconColor = `#${icon.hex}`;
34:   const iconRgb = hexToRgb(iconColor);
35:   if (!iconRgb) {
36:     return fallbackHex;
37:   }
38: 
39:   const bgRgb = hexToRgb(bgHex);
40:   if (!bgRgb) {
41:     return fallbackHex;
42:   }
43: 
44:   const contrast = getContrastRatio(iconRgb, bgRgb);
45:   const color = contrast >= minContrastRatio ? iconColor : fallbackHex;
46: 
47:   return (
48:     <a
49:       key={icon.slug}
50:       href={icon.source}
51:       target="_blank"
52:       rel="noopener noreferrer"
53:       {...aProps}
54:     >
55:       <img
56:         src={`data:image/svg+xml;utf8,${encodeURIComponent(
57:           icon.svg.replace(/currentColor/g, color)
58:         )}`}
59:         alt={icon.title}
60:         width={size}
61:         height={size}
62:         loading="lazy"
63:         {...imgProps}
64:       />
65:     </a>
66:   );
67: }
`````

## File: src/components/magicui/utils.ts
`````typescript
 1: export interface RGB {
 2:   r: number;
 3:   g: number;
 4:   b: number;
 5: }
 6: 
 7: export function hexToRgb(hex: string): RGB | null {
 8:   const result = /^#?([a-f\d]{2})([a-f\d]{2})([a-f\d]{2})$/i.exec(hex);
 9:   if (!result) return null;
10: 
11:   return {
12:     r: parseInt(result[1] || '0', 16),
13:     g: parseInt(result[2] || '0', 16),
14:     b: parseInt(result[3] || '0', 16),
15:   };
16: }
17: 
18: export function getLuminance({ r, g, b }: RGB): number {
19:   const rs = r / 255;
20:   const gs = g / 255;
21:   const bs = b / 255;
22: 
23:   return 0.2126 * rs + 0.7152 * gs + 0.0722 * bs;
24: }
25: 
26: export function getContrastRatio(foreground: RGB, background: RGB): number {
27:   const l1 = getLuminance(foreground) + 0.05;
28:   const l2 = getLuminance(background) + 0.05;
29:   return Math.max(l1, l2) / Math.min(l1, l2);
30: }
`````

133: 
134:     const [item] = payload
135:     const key = `${labelKey || item?.dataKey || item?.name || "value"}`
136:     const itemConfig = getPayloadConfigFromPayload(config, item, key)
137:     const value =
138:       !labelKey && typeof label === "string"
139:         ? config[label as keyof typeof config]?.label || label
140:         : itemConfig?.label
141: 
142:     if (labelFormatter) {
143:       return (
144:         <div className={cn("font-medium", labelClassName)}>
145:           {labelFormatter(value, payload)}
146:         </div>
147:       )
148:     }
149: 
150:     if (!value) {
151:       return null
152:     }
153: 
154:     return <div className={cn("font-medium", labelClassName)}>{value}</div>
155:   }, [
156:     label,
157:     labelFormatter,
158:     payload,
159:     hideLabel,
160:     labelClassName,
161:     config,
162:     labelKey,
163:   ])
164: 
165:   if (!active || !payload?.length) {
166:     return null
167:   }
168: 
169:   const nestLabel = payload.length === 1 && indicator !== "dot"
170: 
171:   return (
172:     <div
173:       className={cn(
174:         "border-border/50 bg-background grid min-w-[8rem] items-start gap-1.5 rounded-lg border px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs shadow-xl",
175:         className
176:       )}
177:     >
178:       {!nestLabel ? tooltipLabel : null}
179:       <div className="grid gap-1.5">
180:         {payload.map((item, index) => {
181:           const key = `${nameKey || item.name || item.dataKey || "value"}`
182:           const itemConfig = getPayloadConfigFromPayload(config, item, key)
183:           const indicatorColor = color || item.payload.fill || item.color
184: 
185:           return (
186:             <div
187:               key={item.dataKey}
188:               className={cn(
189:                 "[&>svg]:text-muted-foreground flex w-full flex-wrap items-stretch gap-2 [&>svg]:h-2.5 [&>svg]:w-2.5",
190:                 indicator === "dot" && "items-center"
191:               )}
192:             >
193:               {formatter && item?.value !== undefined && item.name ? (
194:                 formatter(item.value, item.name, item, index, item.payload)
195:               ) : (
196:                 <>
197:                   {itemConfig?.icon ? (
198:                     <itemConfig.icon />
199:                   ) : (
200:                     !hideIndicator && (
201:                       <div
202:                         className={cn(
203:                           "shrink-0 rounded-[2px] border-(--color-border) bg-(--color-bg)",
204:                           {
205:                             "h-2.5 w-2.5": indicator === "dot",
206:                             "w-1": indicator === "line",
207:                             "w-0 border-[1.5px] border-dashed bg-transparent":
208:                               indicator === "dashed",
209:                             "my-0.5": nestLabel && indicator === "dashed",
210:                           }
211:                         )}
212:                         style={
213:                           {
214:                             "--color-bg": indicatorColor,
215:                             "--color-border": indicatorColor,
216:                           } as React.CSSProperties
217:                         }
218:                       />
219:                     )
220:                   )}
221:                   <div
222:                     className={cn(
223:                       "flex flex-1 justify-between leading-none",
224:                       nestLabel ? "items-end" : "items-center"
225:                     )}
226:                   >
227:                     <div className="grid gap-1.5">
228:                       {nestLabel ? tooltipLabel : null}
229:                       <span className="text-muted-foreground">
230:                         {itemConfig?.label || item.name}
231:                       </span>
232:                     </div>
233:                     {item.value && (
234:                       <span className="text-foreground font-mono font-medium tabular-nums">
235:                         {item.value.toLocaleString()}
236:                       </span>
237:                     )}
238:                   </div>
239:                 </>
240:               )}
241:             </div>
242:           )
243:         })}
244:       </div>
245:     </div>
246:   )
247: }
248: 
249: const ChartLegend = RechartsPrimitive.Legend
250: 
251: function ChartLegendContent({
252:   className,
253:   hideIcon = false,
254:   payload,
255:   verticalAlign = "bottom",
256:   nameKey,
257: }: React.ComponentProps<"div"> &
258:   Pick<RechartsPrimitive.LegendProps, "payload" | "verticalAlign"> & {
259:     hideIcon?: boolean
260:     nameKey?: string
261:   }) {
262:   const { config } = useChart()
263: 
264:   if (!payload?.length) {
265:     return null
266:   }
267: 
268:   return (
269:     <div
270:       className={cn(
271:         "flex items-center justify-center gap-4",
272:         verticalAlign === "top" ? "pb-3" : "pt-3",
273:         className
274:       )}
275:     >
276:       {payload.map((item) => {
277:         const key = `${nameKey || item.dataKey || "value"}`
278:         const itemConfig = getPayloadConfigFromPayload(config, item, key)
279: 
280:         return (
281:           <div
282:             key={item.value}
283:             className={cn(
284:               "[&>svg]:text-muted-foreground flex items-center gap-1.5 [&>svg]:h-3 [&>svg]:w-3"
285:             )}
286:           >
287:             {itemConfig?.icon && !hideIcon ? (
288:               <itemConfig.icon />
289:             ) : (
290:               <div
291:                 className="h-2 w-2 shrink-0 rounded-[2px]"
292:                 style={{
293:                   backgroundColor: item.color,
294:                 }}
295:               />
296:             )}
297:             {itemConfig?.label}
298:           </div>
299:         )
300:       })}
301:     </div>
302:   )
303: }
304: 
305: 
306: function getPayloadConfigFromPayload(
307:   config: ChartConfig,
308:   payload: unknown,
309:   key: string
310: ) {
311:   if (typeof payload !== "object" || payload === null) {
312:     return undefined
313:   }
314: 
315:   const payloadPayload =
316:     "payload" in payload &&
317:     typeof payload.payload === "object" &&
318:     payload.payload !== null
319:       ? payload.payload
320:       : undefined
321: 
322:   let configLabelKey: string = key
323: 
324:   if (
325:     key in payload &&
326:     typeof payload[key as keyof typeof payload] === "string"
327:   ) {
328:     configLabelKey = payload[key as keyof typeof payload] as string
329:   } else if (
330:     payloadPayload &&
331:     key in payloadPayload &&
332:     typeof payloadPayload[key as keyof typeof payloadPayload] === "string"
333:   ) {
334:     configLabelKey = payloadPayload[
335:       key as keyof typeof payloadPayload
336:     ] as string
337:   }
338: 
339:   return configLabelKey in config
340:     ? config[configLabelKey]
341:     : config[key as keyof typeof config]
342: }
343: 
344: export {
345:   ChartContainer,
346:   ChartTooltip,
347:   ChartTooltipContent,
348:   ChartLegend,
349:   ChartLegendContent,
350:   ChartStyle,
351: }
`````

152:     </p>
153:   )
154: }

 1: import * as React from "react";

 3: 
 4: interface LinkProps extends React.AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement> {
 5:   href: string;
 6:   children: React.ReactNode;
 7:   className?: string;
 8: }
 9: 
10: export function Link({ href, children, className, ...props }: LinkProps) {
11:   return (

13:       href={href}

20:       {children}
21:     </a>
22:   );
23: }
24: 
25: export function useLocation() {
26:   const [pathname, setPathname] = React.useState("/");
27: 
28:   React.useEffect(() => {
29:     setPathname(window.location.pathname);
30: 
31:     const handleRouteChange = () => {
32:       setPathname(window.location.pathname);
33:     };
34: 
35:     window.addEventListener('popstate', handleRouteChange);
36:     document.addEventListener('astro:page-load', handleRouteChange);
37: 
38:     return () => {
39:       window.removeEventListener('popstate', handleRouteChange);
40:       document.removeEventListener('astro:page-load', handleRouteChange);
41:     };
42:   }, []);
43: 
44:   return { pathname };
45: }
`````

## File: src/components/ui/squares-background.tsx
`````typescript
  1: import { useRef, useEffect, useState } from "react"
  2: 
  3: interface SquaresProps {
  4:   direction?: "right" | "left" | "up" | "down" | "diagonal"
  5:   speed?: number
  6:   borderColor?: string
  7:   squareSize?: number
  8:   hoverFillColor?: string
  9:   className?: string
 10:   glowIntensity?: number
 11:   fadeEdges?: boolean
 12:   pulseEffect?: boolean
 13:   height?: string | number
 14: }
 15: 
 16: export function Squares({
 17:   direction = "right",
 18:   speed = 1,
 19:   borderColor = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2)",
 20:   squareSize = 40,
 21:   hoverFillColor = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1)",
 22:   className = "",
 23:   glowIntensity = 0.8,
 24:   fadeEdges = true,
 25:   pulseEffect = true,
 26:   height = "500px",
 27: }: SquaresProps) {
 28:   const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(null)
 29:   const requestRef = useRef<number>(0)
 30:   const numSquaresX = useRef<number>(0)
 31:   const numSquaresY = useRef<number>(0)
 32:   const gridOffset = useRef({ x: 0, y: 0 })
 33:   const pulsePhase = useRef<number>(0)
 34:   const [hoveredSquare, setHoveredSquare] = useState<{
 35:     x: number
 36:     y: number
 37:   } | null>(null)
 38: 
 39:   useEffect(() => {
 40:     const canvas = canvasRef.current
 41:     if (!canvas) return
 42: 
 43:     const ctx = canvas.getContext("2d")
 44:     if (!ctx) return
 45: 
 46:     canvas.style.background = "transparent"
 47: 
 48:     const resizeCanvas = () => {
 49:       const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1
 50:       canvas.width = canvas.offsetWidth * dpr
 51:       canvas.height = canvas.offsetHeight * dpr
 52:       ctx.scale(dpr, dpr)
 53:       canvas.style.width = `${canvas.offsetWidth}px`
 54:       canvas.style.height = `${canvas.offsetHeight}px`
 55:       numSquaresX.current = Math.ceil(canvas.width / squareSize) + 1
 56:       numSquaresY.current = Math.ceil(canvas.height / squareSize) + 1
 57:     }
 58: 
 59:     window.addEventListener("resize", resizeCanvas)
 60:     resizeCanvas()
 61: 
 62:     const drawGrid = () => {
 63:       ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
 64: 
 65:       const startX = Math.floor(gridOffset.current.x / squareSize) * squareSize
 66:       const startY = Math.floor(gridOffset.current.y / squareSize) * squareSize
 67: 
 68:       if (pulseEffect) {
 69:         pulsePhase.current = (pulsePhase.current + 0.02) % (Math.PI * 2)
 70:       }
 71: 
 72:       for (let x = startX; x < canvas.width + squareSize; x += squareSize) {
 73:         for (let y = startY; y < canvas.height + squareSize; y += squareSize) {
 74:           const squareX = x - (gridOffset.current.x % squareSize)
 75:           const squareY = y - (gridOffset.current.y % squareSize)
 76: 
 77:           const centerX = canvas.width / 2
 78:           const centerY = canvas.height / 2
 79:           const distanceFromCenter = Math.sqrt(
 80:             Math.pow((squareX - centerX) / centerX, 2) +
 81:             Math.pow((squareY - centerY) / centerY, 2)
 82:           )
 83: 
 84:           let opacity = pulseEffect
 85:             ? 0.5 + 0.3 * Math.sin(pulsePhase.current + distanceFromCenter * 2)
 86:             : 0.7
 87:           opacity *= Math.max(0.3, 1 - distanceFromCenter)
 88: 
 89:           if (
 90:             hoveredSquare &&
 91:             Math.floor((x - startX) / squareSize) === hoveredSquare.x &&
 92:             Math.floor((y - startY) / squareSize) === hoveredSquare.y
 93:           ) {
 94:             ctx.fillStyle = hoverFillColor
 95:             ctx.fillRect(squareX, squareY, squareSize, squareSize)
 96: 
 97:             ctx.shadowColor = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.5)"
 98:             ctx.shadowBlur = 20 * glowIntensity
 99:           } else {
100:             ctx.shadowColor = "transparent"
101:             ctx.shadowBlur = 0
102:           }
103: 
104:           ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(255, 255, 255, ${opacity})`
105:           ctx.lineWidth = 1
106:           ctx.strokeRect(squareX, squareY, squareSize, squareSize)
107:         }
108:       }
109: 
110:       if (fadeEdges) {
111:         const gradient = ctx.createRadialGradient(
112:           canvas.width / 2,
113:           canvas.height / 2,
114:           0,
115:           canvas.width / 2,
116:           canvas.height / 2,
117:           Math.max(canvas.width, canvas.height) / 1.5
118:         )
119:         gradient.addColorStop(0, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)")
120:         gradient.addColorStop(1, "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.7)")
121: 
122:         ctx.fillStyle = gradient
123:         ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height)
124:       }
125:     }
126: 
127:     const updateAnimation = () => {
128:       const effectiveSpeed = Math.max(speed, 0.1)
129:       const time = Date.now() * 0.001
130: 
131:       const waveOffset = Math.sin(time) * 0.5
132: 
133:       switch (direction) {
134:         case "right":
135:           gridOffset.current.x =
136:             (gridOffset.current.x - effectiveSpeed + waveOffset + squareSize) % squareSize
137:           break
138:         case "left":
139:           gridOffset.current.x =
140:             (gridOffset.current.x + effectiveSpeed + waveOffset + squareSize) % squareSize
141:           break
142:         case "up":
143:           gridOffset.current.y =
144:             (gridOffset.current.y + effectiveSpeed + waveOffset + squareSize) % squareSize
145:           break
146:         case "down":
147:           gridOffset.current.y =
148:             (gridOffset.current.y - effectiveSpeed + waveOffset + squareSize) % squareSize
149:           break
150:         case "diagonal":
151:           gridOffset.current.x =
152:             (gridOffset.current.x - effectiveSpeed + waveOffset + squareSize) % squareSize
153:           gridOffset.current.y =
154:             (gridOffset.current.y - effectiveSpeed + waveOffset + squareSize) % squareSize
155:           break
156:       }
157: 
158:       drawGrid()
159:       requestRef.current = requestAnimationFrame(updateAnimation)
160:     }
161: 
162:     const handleMouseMove = (event: MouseEvent) => {
163:       const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect()
164:       const mouseX = event.clientX - rect.left
165:       const mouseY = event.clientY - rect.top
166: 
167:       const startX = Math.floor(gridOffset.current.x / squareSize) * squareSize
168:       const startY = Math.floor(gridOffset.current.y / squareSize) * squareSize
169: 
170:       const hoveredSquareX = Math.floor(
171:         (mouseX + gridOffset.current.x - startX) / squareSize,
172:       )
173:       const hoveredSquareY = Math.floor(
174:         (mouseY + gridOffset.current.y - startY) / squareSize,
175:       )
176: 
177:       setHoveredSquare({ x: hoveredSquareX, y: hoveredSquareY })
178:     }
179: 
180:     const handleMouseLeave = () => {
181:       setHoveredSquare(null)
182:     }
183: 
184:     window.addEventListener("resize", resizeCanvas)
185:     canvas.addEventListener("mousemove", handleMouseMove)
186:     canvas.addEventListener("mouseleave", handleMouseLeave)
187: 
188:     resizeCanvas()
189:     requestRef.current = requestAnimationFrame(updateAnimation)
190: 
191:     return () => {
192:       window.removeEventListener("resize", resizeCanvas)
193:       canvas.removeEventListener("mousemove", handleMouseMove)
194:       canvas.removeEventListener("mouseleave", handleMouseLeave)
195:       if (requestRef.current) {
196:         cancelAnimationFrame(requestRef.current)
197:       }
198:     }
199:   }, [direction, speed, borderColor, hoverFillColor, hoveredSquare, squareSize, glowIntensity, fadeEdges, pulseEffect])
200: 
201:   return (
202:     <canvas
203:       ref={canvasRef}
204:       style={{ height: typeof height === 'number' ? `${height}px` : height }}
205:       className={`w-full border-none block bg-transparent ${className}`}
206:     />
207:   )
208: }
`````

115: const chartConfig = {
116:     views: {
117:         label: "Page Views",
118:     },
119:     desktop: {
120:         label: "Desktop",
121:         color: "hsl(var(--chart-1))",
122:     },
123:     mobile: {
124:         label: "Mobile",
125:         color: "hsl(var(--chart-2))",
126:     },
127: } satisfies ChartConfig
128: 
129: export function Chart() {
130:     const [activeChart, setActiveChart] =
131:         React.useState<keyof typeof chartConfig>("desktop")
132: 
133:     const total = React.useMemo(
134:         () => ({
135:             desktop: chartData.reduce((acc, curr) => acc + curr.desktop, 0),
136:             mobile: chartData.reduce((acc, curr) => acc + curr.mobile, 0),
137:         }),
138:         []
139:     )
140: 
141:     return (
142:         <Card>
143:             <CardHeader className="flex flex-col items-stretch space-y-0 border-b p-0 sm:flex-row">
144:                 <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col justify-center gap-1 px-6 py-5 sm:py-6">
145:                     <CardTitle>Bar Chart - Interactive</CardTitle>
146:                     <CardDescription>
147:                         Showing total visitors for the last 3 months
148:                     </CardDescription>
149:                 </div>
150:                 <div className="flex">
151:                     {["desktop", "mobile"].map((key) => {
152:                         const chart = key as keyof typeof chartConfig
153:                         return (
154:                             <button
155:                                 key={chart}
156:                                 data-active={activeChart === chart}
157:                                 className="relative z-30 flex flex-1 flex-col justify-center gap-1 border-t px-6 py-4 text-left even:border-l data-[active=true]:bg-muted/50 sm:border-l sm:border-t-0 sm:px-8 sm:py-6"
158:                                 onClick={() => setActiveChart(chart)}
159:                             >
160:                                 <span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
161:                                     {chartConfig[chart].label}
162:                                 </span>
163:                                 <span className="text-lg font-bold leading-none sm:text-3xl">
164:                                     {total[key as keyof typeof total].toLocaleString()}
165:                                 </span>
166:                             </button>
167:                         )
168:                     })}
169:                 </div>
170:             </CardHeader>
171:             <CardContent className="px-2 sm:p-6">
172:                 <ChartContainer
173:                     config={chartConfig}
174:                     className="aspect-auto h-[250px] w-full"
175:                 >
176:                     <BarChart
177:                         accessibilityLayer
178:                         data={chartData}
179:                         margin={{
180:                             left: 12,
181:                             right: 12,
182:                         }}
183:                     >
184:                         <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
185:                         <XAxis
186:                             dataKey="date"
187:                             tickLine={false}
188:                             axisLine={false}
189:                             tickMargin={8}
190:                             minTickGap={32}
191:                             tickFormatter={(value) => {
192:                                 const date = new Date(value)
193:                                 return date.toLocaleDateString("en-US", {
194:                                     month: "short",
195:                                     day: "numeric",
196:                                 })
197:                             }}
198:                         />
199:                         <ChartTooltip
200:                             content={
201:                                 <ChartTooltipContent
202:                                     className="w-[150px]"
203:                                     nameKey="views"
204:                                     labelFormatter={(value) => {
205:                                         return new Date(value).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {
206:                                             month: "short",
207:                                             day: "numeric",
208:                                             year: "numeric",
209:                                         })
210:                                     }}
211:                                 />
212:                             }
213:                         />
214:                         <Bar dataKey={activeChart} fill={`var(--color-${activeChart})`} />
215:                     </BarChart>
216:                 </ChartContainer>
217:             </CardContent>
218:         </Card>
219:     )
220: }
`````

 81:       try {
 82:         const response = await fetch('https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids=bitcoin,ethereum,solana&vs_currencies=usd');
 83:         const data = await response.json();
 84: 
 85:         const newPrices: CryptoPrices = {
 86:           BTC: data.bitcoin.usd,
 87:           ETH: data.ethereum.usd,
 88:           SOL: data.solana.usd
 89:         };
 90: 
 91:         setPrices(newPrices);
 92:         const cryptoPrice = newPrices[selectedCrypto];
 93:         setCryptoAmount((amount / cryptoPrice).toFixed(8));
 94:       } catch (err) {

 96:         console.error('Price fetch error:', err);

156:       >

158:           <SelectValue placeholder="Select cryptocurrency" />
159:         </SelectTrigger>
160:         <SelectContent>
161:           {Object.entries(CRYPTO_CONFIG).map(([key, config]) => (
162:             <SelectItem key={key} value={key}>
163:               <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
164:                 <img src={config.icon} alt={key} className="w-5 h-5" />
165:                 {key}
166:               </div>
167:             </SelectItem>
168:           ))}
169:         </SelectContent>
170:       </Select>
171: 
172:       {prices && (

174:           <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-2">
175:             <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Amount Due:</span>
176:             <span className="font-bold">${amount} {currency}</span>
177:           </div>
178:           <div className="flex justify-between items-center">
179:             <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Crypto Amount:</span>
180:             <span className="font-bold">{cryptoAmount} {selectedCrypto}</span>
181:           </div>
182:         </div>
183:       )}
184: 
185:       <div className="text-center mb-6">
186:         {showQR ? (
187:           <div className="p-4 bg-white rounded-lg inline-block">
188:             <QRCode
189:               value={`${CRYPTO_CONFIG[selectedCrypto].qrPrefix}${CRYPTO_CONFIG[selectedCrypto].address}?amount=${cryptoAmount}`}
190:               size={200}
191:             />
192:           </div>

197:             className="w-full"
198:           >

200:             Show QR Code

217:             >

219:             </Button>

222:

## File: src/components/ModeToggle.tsx
`````typescript
 1: import * as React from "react"
 2: import { Moon, Sun } from "lucide-react"
 3: import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
 4: 
 5: export function ModeToggle() {
 6:     const [theme, setThemeState] = React.useState<"theme-light" | "dark">("dark")
 7: 
 8:     React.useEffect(() => {
 9:         const isDarkMode = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")
10:         if (!isDarkMode) {
11:             document.documentElement.classList.add("dark")
12:         }
13:         setThemeState(isDarkMode ? "dark" : "theme-light")
14:     }, [])
15: 
16:     React.useEffect(() => {
17:         const isDark = theme === "dark"
18:         document.documentElement.classList[isDark ? "add" : "remove"]("dark")
19:     }, [theme])
20: 
21:     return (
22:         <Button
23:             variant="ghost"
24:             size="icon"
25:             className="h-[50px] w-[50px]"
26:             onClick={() => setThemeState(theme === "dark" ? "theme-light" : "dark")}
27:             aria-label="Toggle theme"
28:         >
29:             <Sun className="h-6 w-6 rotate-0 scale-100 transition-all dark:-rotate-90 dark:scale-0" />
30:             <Moon className="absolute h-6 w-6 rotate-90 scale-0 transition-all dark:rotate-0 dark:scale-100" />
31:         </Button>
32:     )
33: }
`````

333:   const [visibleStaff, setVisibleStaff] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set());
334: 
335:   return (
336:     <div className="container mx-auto px-4 py-8 sm:py-12">
337:       <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-8 sm:gap-12 relative">
338:         {/* Managing Director Card */}
339:         <motion.div
340:           key="director"
341:           className="mb-8 sm:mb-12 max-w-2xl mx-auto w-full"
342:           initial={{ opacity: 0, y: -20 }}
343:           animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
344:           transition={{ duration: 0.5 }}
345:         >
346:           <Card
347:             className={`p-6 sm:p-8 cursor-pointer transition-all duration-300 transform hover:scale-105 ${activeDepartment === 'director' ? 'bg-primary/15 shadow-lg ring-2 ring-primary/20' : 'hover:bg-primary/5 hover:shadow-md'}`}
348:             onClick={() => {
349:               if (activeDepartment === 'director') {
350:                 setActiveDepartment('');
351:                 setVisibleStaff(new Set());
352:               } else {
353:                 setActiveDepartment('director');
354:               }
355:             }}
356:           >
357:             <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-4 sm:gap-6 relative">
358: 
359:               <div className={`p-3 sm:p-4 rounded-full transition-all duration-300 transform ${activeDepartment === 'director' ? 'bg-primary/20 scale-110' : 'bg-primary/10 hover:scale-105'}`}>
360:                 <Brain className={`w-8 h-8 sm:w-12 sm:h-12 transition-colors duration-300 ${activeDepartment === 'director' ? 'text-primary' : 'text-primary/70'}`} />
361:               </div>
362:               <div className="text-center">
363:                 <h3 className="font-bold text-xl sm:text-2xl mb-2 text-primary">Managing Director</h3>
364:                 <p className="text-sm sm:text-base text-muted-foreground">Build your AI Director to orchestrate company vision and assemble a team of AI Directors</p>
365:               </div>
366:             </div>
367:           </Card>
368:         </motion.div>
369: 
370:         {/* Department Grid */}
371:         <div className="grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-4 sm:gap-6 lg:gap-8 relative">
372:         {departments.map((dept, index) => (
373:           <motion.div
374:             key={dept.id}
375:             initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
376:             animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
377:             transition={{ duration: 0.5, delay: index * 0.1 }}
378:           >
379:             <Card
380:               className={`p-4 sm:p-6 cursor-pointer transition-all duration-300 transform hover:scale-105 ${activeDepartment === dept.id ? 'bg-primary/15 shadow-lg ring-2 ring-primary/20' : 'hover:bg-primary/5 hover:shadow-md'}`}
381:               onClick={() => {
382:                 if (activeDepartment === dept.id) {
383:                   setActiveDepartment('');
384:                   setVisibleStaff(new Set());
385:                 } else {
386:                   setActiveDepartment(dept.id);
387:                   setVisibleStaff(new Set(dept.team.map((_, i) => `${dept.id}-${i}`)));
388:                 }
389:               }}
390:             >
391:               <div className="flex items-center gap-3 sm:gap-4 relative">
392: 
393:                 <div className={`p-2 sm:p-3 rounded-full transition-all duration-300 transform ${activeDepartment === dept.id ? 'bg-primary/20 scale-110' : 'bg-primary/10 hover:scale-105'}`}>
394:                   <dept.icon className={`w-5 h-5 sm:w-6 sm:h-6 transition-colors duration-300 ${activeDepartment === dept.id ? 'text-primary' : 'text-primary/70'}`} />
395:                 </div>
396:                 <div>
397:                   <h3 className="font-semibold text-base sm:text-lg text-primary">{dept.title}</h3>

399:                 </div>
400:               </div>
401:             </Card>
402:             <div className="mt-3 sm:mt-4">
403:               {dept.team.map((member, mIndex) => {

406: 
407:                 return (

409:                     key={staffId}
410:                     initial={{ opacity: 0, x: -20 }}

412:                       opacity: isVisible ? 1 : 0,

423:                           <member.icon className={`w-4 h-4 sm:w-5 sm:h-5 transition-colors duration-300 ${activeDepartment === dept.id ? 'text-primary' : 'text-primary/70'}`} />
424:                         </div>
425:                         <div>
426:                           <h5 className="font-medium text-sm sm:text-base">{member.title}</h5>
427:                           <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">{member.description}</p>
428:                         </div>
429:                       </div>
430:                     </Card>
431:                   </motion.div>
432:                 );
433:               })}
434:             </div>
435:           </motion.div>
436:         ))}
437:         </div>
438:       </div>
439:     </div>
440:   );
441: }

`````typescript
  1: import { useEffect, useState, type ReactElement } from "react";
  2: import { PanelRightClose, PanelRightOpen } from "lucide-react";
  3: 
  4: interface Heading {
  5:   depth: number;
  6:   text: string;
  7:   slug: string;
  8: }
  9: 
 10: interface HeadingNode extends Heading {
 11:   children: HeadingNode[];
 12: }
 13: 
 14: interface Props {
 15:   headings?: Heading[];
 16:   onVisibilityChange?: (isVisible: boolean) => void;
 17:   "client:load"?: boolean;
 18:   "client:visible"?: boolean;
 19:   "client:media"?: string;
 20:   "client:only"?: boolean;
 21:   "client:idle"?: boolean;
 22: }
 23: 
 24: export default function TableOfContents({ headings = [], onVisibilityChange }: Props): ReactElement | null {
 25:   const [activeId, setActiveId] = useState<string>("");
 26:   const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(true);
 27: 
 28:   const toggleVisibility = () => {
 29:     const newVisibility = !isVisible;
 30:     setIsVisible(newVisibility);
 31:     onVisibilityChange?.(newVisibility);
 32:     (window as any).handleTocVisibility?.(newVisibility);
 33:   };
 34: 
 35:   useEffect(() => {
 36:     const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
 37:       (entries) => {
 38:         entries.forEach((entry) => {
 39:           if (entry.isIntersecting) {
 40:             setActiveId(entry.target.id);
 41:           }
 42:         });
 43:       },
 44:       { rootMargin: "0% 0% -80% 0%" }
 45:     );
 46: 
 47:     headings.forEach((heading) => {
 48:       const element = document.getElementById(heading.slug);
 49:       if (element) observer.observe(element);
 50:     });
 51: 
 52:     return () => {
 53:       headings.forEach((heading) => {
 54:         const element = document.getElementById(heading.slug);
 55:         if (element) observer.unobserve(element);
 56:       });
 57:     };
 58:   }, [headings]);
 59: 
 60:   const buildToc = (headings: Heading[]): HeadingNode[] => {
 61:     const toc: HeadingNode[] = [];
 62:     const parentHeadings = new Map<number, HeadingNode>();
 63: 
 64:     headings.forEach((heading) => {
 65:       const node: HeadingNode = { ...heading, children: [] };
 66: 
 67:       if (heading.depth === 2) {
 68:         toc.push(node);
 69:         parentHeadings.set(heading.depth, node);
 70:       } else {
 71:         const parentDepth = heading.depth - 1;
 72:         const parent = parentHeadings.get(parentDepth);
 73:         if (parent) {
 74:           parent.children.push(node);
 75:           parentHeadings.set(heading.depth, node);
 76:         }
 77:       }
 78:     });
 79: 
 80:     return toc;
 81:   };
 82: 
 83:   const renderTocItem = ({ text, slug, children }: HeadingNode): ReactElement => {
 84:     const isActive = activeId === slug;
 85: 
 86:     return (
 87:       <li key={slug} className="my-2">
 88:         <a
 89:           href={`#${slug}`}
 90:           className={`block py-1.5 px-4 text-sm rounded-md transition-all duration-200 ${
 91:             isActive
 92:               ? "bg-primary/10 text-primary font-medium shadow-sm"
 93:               : "text-muted-foreground hover:text-primary hover:bg-muted/50"
 94:           }`}
 95:         >
 96:           {text}
 97:         </a>
 98:         {children.length > 0 && (
 99:           <ul className="pl-4 mt-2 border-l border-white/10">
100:             {children.map((child) => renderTocItem(child))}
101:           </ul>
102:         )}
103:       </li>
104:     );
105:   };
106: 
107:   const toc = buildToc(headings);
108: 
109:   if (headings.length === 0) return null;
110: 
111:   return (
112:     <nav aria-label="Table of Contents" className="relative">
113:       <button
114:         onClick={toggleVisibility}
115:         className="absolute -left-6 top-0 p-1.5 rounded-md bg-muted/50 text-muted-foreground hover:text-primary hover:bg-muted transition-colors"
116:         aria-label={isVisible ? "Hide table of contents" : "Show table of contents"}
117:         title={isVisible ? "Hide sidebar" : "Show sidebar"}
118:       >
119:         {isVisible ? (
120:           <PanelRightClose className="h-4 w-4" />
121:         ) : (
122:           <PanelRightOpen className="h-4 w-4" />
123:         )}
124:       </button>
125:      <div className={`transition-all duration-200 overflow-hidden ${isVisible ? 'w-full opacity-100' : 'w-0 opacity-0'}`}>
126:        <div className={`${isVisible ? 'visible' : 'invisible'}`}>
127:          <div className="font-medium mb-4 text-sm px-4">On This Page</div>
128:          <ul className="space-y-2">
129:            {toc.map((heading) => renderTocItem(heading))}
130:          </ul>
131:        </div>
132:      </div>
133:     </nav>
134:   );
135: }
`````

  6: <script is:inline>
  7:   function getThemePreference() {
  8:     if (typeof localStorage !== 'undefined' && localStorage.getItem('theme')) {
  9:       const stored = localStorage.getItem('theme');
 10:       if (['light', 'dark', 'high-contrast'].includes(stored)) {
 11:         return stored;
 12:       }
 13:     }
 14:     
 15:     // Check for system preference
 16:     if (window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches) {
 17:       return 'dark';
 18:     }
 19:     
 20:     // Default to dark theme to match the image
 21:     return 'dark';
 22:   }
 23:   
 24:   function setTheme(theme) {
 25:     const root = document.documentElement;
 26:     
 27:     // Remove all theme classes
 28:     root.classList.remove('light', 'dark', 'high-contrast');
 29:     
 30:     // Add the selected theme class (except for light which is the default)
 31:     if (theme !== 'light') {
 32:       root.classList.add(theme);
 33:     }
 34:     
 35:     // Set data-theme attribute for CSS selectors
 36:     root.setAttribute('data-theme', theme);
 37:     
 38:     // Store in localStorage
 39:     localStorage.setItem('theme', theme);
 40: 
 41:     // Dispatch event for React components
 42:     window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('theme-change', { detail: theme }));
 43:   }
 44: 
 45:   // Initialize theme
 46:   setTheme(getThemePreference());
 47: 
 48:   // Listen for system theme changes
 49:   window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').addEventListener('change', (e) => {
 50:     const currentTheme = localStorage.getItem('theme');
 51:     if (!currentTheme || currentTheme === 'system') {
 52:       setTheme(e.matches ? 'dark' : 'light');
 53:     }
 54:   });
 55: 
 56:   // Expose theme functions to window
 57:   window.setTheme = setTheme;
 58:   window.getThemePreference = getThemePreference;
 59:   
 60:   // Cycle to the next theme
 61:   window.cycleTheme = function() {
 62:     const currentTheme = getThemePreference();
 63:     
 64:     switch (currentTheme) {
 65:       case 'light':
 66:         setTheme('dark');
 67:         break;
 68:       case 'dark':
 69:         setTheme('high-contrast');
 70:         break;
 71:       case 'high-contrast':
 72:         setTheme('light');
 73:         break;
 74:       default:
 75:         setTheme('dark');
 76:     }
 77:   };
 78: 
 79:   // Listen for theme changes from React components
 80:   document.addEventListener('set-theme', (e) => {
 81:     if (e.detail && typeof e.detail === 'string') {
 82:       setTheme(e.detail);
 83:     }
 84:   });
 85: </script>

`````typescript
  1: import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useState } from 'react'
  2: 
  3: type Theme = 'light' | 'dark' | 'high-contrast' | 'system'
  4: 
  5: interface ThemeProviderProps {
  6:   children: React.ReactNode
  7:   defaultTheme?: Theme
  8: }
  9: 
 10: interface ThemeContextValue {
 11:   theme: Theme
 12:   setTheme: (theme: Theme) => void
 13: }
 14: 
 15: const ThemeContext = createContext<ThemeContextValue | undefined>(undefined)
 16: 
 17: export function ThemeProvider({
 18:   children,
 19:   defaultTheme = 'system'
 20: }: ThemeProviderProps) {
 21:   const [theme, setTheme] = useState<Theme>(defaultTheme)
 22: 
 23:   useEffect(() => {
 24:     const root = window.document.documentElement
 25:     root.classList.remove('light', 'dark', 'high-contrast')
 26: 
 27:     if (theme === 'system') {
 28:       const systemTheme = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches
 29:         ? 'dark'
 30:         : 'light'
 31:       root.classList.add(systemTheme)
 32:       root.setAttribute('data-theme', systemTheme)
 33:     } else {
 34:       root.classList.add(theme)
 35:       root.setAttribute('data-theme', theme)
 36:     }
 37: 
 38: 
 39:     localStorage.setItem('theme', theme)
 40:   }, [theme])
 41: 
 42: 
 43:   useEffect(() => {
 44:     if (theme === 'system') {
 45:       const mediaQuery = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')
 46: 
 47:       const handleChange = (e: MediaQueryListEvent) => {
 48:         const root = window.document.documentElement
 49:         const systemTheme = e.matches ? 'dark' : 'light'
 50: 
 51:         root.classList.remove('light', 'dark', 'high-contrast')
 52:         root.classList.add(systemTheme)
 53:         root.setAttribute('data-theme', systemTheme)
 54:       }
 55: 
 56:       mediaQuery.addEventListener('change', handleChange)
 57:       return () => mediaQuery.removeEventListener('change', handleChange)
 58:     }
 59:   }, [theme])
 60: 
 61:   return (
 62:     <ThemeContext.Provider value={{ theme, setTheme }}>
 63:       {children}
 64:     </ThemeContext.Provider>
 65:   )
 66: }
 67: 
 68: export function useTheme() {
 69:   const context = useContext(ThemeContext)
 70:   if (context === undefined) {
 71:     throw new Error('useTheme must be used within a ThemeProvider')
 72:   }
 73:   return context
 74: }
 75: 
 76:

 79: 
 80:   const toggleTheme = () => {

 82:       case 'light':
 83:         setTheme('dark')
 84:         break
 85:       case 'dark':
 86:         setTheme('high-contrast')
 87:         break
 88:       case 'high-contrast':
 89:         setTheme('light')
 90:         break
 91:       default:
 92:         setTheme('light')
 93:     }
 94:   }
 95: 
 96:   return (
 97:     <button
 98:       onClick={toggleTheme}
 99:       className="one-button-secondary p-2 rounded-full"
100:       aria-label="Toggle theme"
101:     >
102:       {theme === 'light' && (

## File: src/content/blog/history-of-ai-agents.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: "The Ghost in the Machine: How AI Agents Evolved from Science Fiction to Your Smartphone"
 3: description: "How AI Agents Evolved from Science Fiction to Your Smartphone"
 4: date: 2025-01-09
 5: picture: "/images/posts/office.webp"
 6: ---
 7: 
 8: In a sleek office building in Silicon Valley, an AI agent is negotiating a meeting schedule between executives across three continents. Meanwhile, in a London home, another digital agent is orchestrating a family's dinner delivery, adjusting the heating, and curating tomorrow's entertainment. These invisible assistants, once the stuff of science fiction, have quietly become part of our daily reality. But their journey from theoretical concept to ubiquitous helper has been anything but straightforward.
 9: 
10: "We've been trying to create autonomous digital agents since the dawn of computing," says Dr. Sarah Chen, AI historian at MIT. "But what's fascinating is how many times we thought we'd cracked it, only to discover new layers of complexity."
11: 
12: ## The Pioneers: Dreams of Digital Minds
13: 
14: The story begins in the 1950s, when the first computers were still filling entire rooms. Early pioneers like Allen Newell and Herbert Simon created the General Problem Solver (GPS), a program that attempted to mimic human problem-solving. It was primitive by today's standards, but it sparked a revolution in thinking about artificial intelligence.
15: 
16: "Those early systems were like digital savants," explains Professor James Martinez of Stanford University. "They could solve specific logical problems brilliantly, but they couldn't handle the messy reality of the real world. It's like they knew the rules of chess perfectly but couldn't recognize the board."
17: 
18: ## The Expert System Gold Rush
19: 
20: The 1980s brought what seemed like a breakthrough. Companies poured millions into "expert systems" – programs that could diagnose diseases or analyze chemical compounds by following decision trees crafted from human expertise. MYCIN, a medical diagnosis system, sometimes outperformed junior doctors in identifying bacterial infections.
21: 
22: But these systems had a fatal flaw: they couldn't learn or adapt. "It was like having a incredibly knowledgeable consultant who could never learn from new experiences," says Martinez. "The maintenance costs were astronomical, and they ultimately proved too brittle for real-world use."
23: 
24: ## The Reactive Revolution
25: 
26: By the 1990s, a new approach emerged. Rather than trying to build all-knowing oracles, researchers like Rodney Brooks at MIT proposed simpler agents that could react to their environment in real-time. This led to more robust robots and systems, but they still lacked the ability to plan ahead or learn from experience.
27: 
28: ## The Social Network
29: 
30: The turn of the millennium saw another shift: multi-agent systems, where multiple AI programs worked together like a digital team. "It was a beautiful idea," says Dr. Chen. "Different specialized agents collaborating to solve complex problems. But getting them to coordinate effectively proved as challenging as managing a room full of toddlers."
31: 
32: ## Today's Digital Butlers
33: 
34: Fast forward to today, and AI agents have become sophisticated digital assistants, powered by large language models and machine learning. They schedule our meetings, monitor our homes, and even trade stocks. But experts warn we're still far from the seamless, truly autonomous agents of science fiction.
35: 
36: "Current AI agents are like talented but inexperienced interns," explains Dr. Elena Rodriguez, head of AI research at DeepMind. "They can handle routine tasks impressively well, but they still need supervision and can make surprising mistakes."
37: 
38: ## The Next Frontier
39: 
40: As we look to the future, the industry faces several critical challenges. Privacy concerns loom large – how much should these digital agents know about us? Trust is another crucial factor – can we rely on them for increasingly important decisions?
41: 
42: "The technical challenges are significant," says Rodriguez, "but the human factors are even more crucial. We're not just building smart software anymore; we're creating entities that people need to trust and feel comfortable with."
43: 
44: ## The Human Touch
45: 
46: Perhaps the most intriguing development is how these AI agents are making us reconsider what it means to be human. As they become more capable, questions of consciousness, free will, and the nature of intelligence are no longer just philosophical debates but practical considerations.
47: 
48: "The next generation of AI agents won't just be tools," predicts Chen. "They'll be partners in our daily lives. The question isn't whether they'll be part of our future, but how we'll shape that future together."
49: 
50: As our digital assistants grow more sophisticated, one thing becomes clear: the ghost in the machine is starting to look more like a reflection of ourselves, with all the complexity and potential that implies. The real challenge may not be creating perfect AI agents, but learning to live and work alongside them effectively.
`````

## File: src/content/blog/the-ai-traders.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: "The AI Traders: Inside Wall Street's Algorithmic Revolution"
 3: description: "Special Report: How Artificial Intelligence is Reshaping Finance"
 4: date: 2025-01-09
 5: picture: "/images/posts/traders.webp"
 6: ---
 7: 
 8: By Anthony O'Connell
 9: 
10: At Goldman Sachs' trading floor in Lower Manhattan, the scene is different from what you might expect. Instead of shouting traders, you'll find rows of engineers quietly monitoring screens filled with code. Welcome to modern Wall Street, where AI systems now handle 60% of all U.S. equity trading volume.
11: 
12: "The human trader isn't extinct," explains David Solomon, Goldman's CEO. "But their role has fundamentally changed. They're now AI supervisors rather than direct market participants."
13: 
14: ## THE NEW MASTERS
15: 
16: JPMorgan's AI trading platform processes over 350 billion market data points daily. Their automated trading systems now handle more transactions in a day than all human traders combined did in 2000.
17: 
18: "Machine learning isn't just making trading faster," says Marianne Lake, JPMorgan's CEO. "It's discovering patterns humans never could have seen."
19: 
20: ### AI Trading by Numbers (2024)
21: - 60% of US equity trading volume is AI-driven
22: - 85% of forex trading is algorithmic
23: - $3 trillion daily AI-managed assets
24: - Microsecond reaction times
25: Source: Bloomberg Terminal Data
26: 
27: ## BLACKROCK'S BRAIN
28: 
29: Perhaps no system better represents this shift than BlackRock's Aladdin platform, which manages risk analysis for $21.6 trillion in assets worldwide. That's more than the GDP of the United States.
30: 
31: "Aladdin processes 200 million calculations across 25,000 portfolios every week," explains BlackRock's CTO, Rob Goldstein. "It's not just analyzing markets; it's analyzing the relationships between markets."
32: 
33: ## THE SPEED GAME
34: 
35: In the suburbs of New Jersey, specialized data centers host servers where milliseconds mean millions. Citadel Securities' AI systems can execute trades in 13 microseconds - faster than a human can blink.
36: 
37: "The speed race is over," says Citadel's Ken Griffin. "Now it's about who has the smartest algorithms, not just the fastest ones."
38: 
39: ## RENAISSANCE'S SECRET
40: 
41: Renaissance Technologies, the most successful hedge fund in history, has relied on AI and machine learning for decades. Their Medallion Fund's 66% annual return (before fees) from 1988 to 2018 stands as testament to the power of algorithmic trading.
42: 
43: ## THE WATCHDOGS
44: 
45: The SEC has responded by developing its own AI tools. "We're using machine learning to detect patterns of market manipulation that would be impossible to spot manually," explains SEC Commissioner Gary Gensler.
46: 
47: ## MAIN STREET IMPACT
48: 
49: These changes aren't limited to Wall Street. Retail investing platforms like Robinhood use AI to:
50: - Detect fraud
51: - Optimize order routing
52: - Provide automated customer service
53: - Analyze investment patterns
54: 
55: ## THE HUMAN ELEMENT
56: 
57: Despite the AI revolution, human judgment remains crucial. When the Flash Crash of 2010 wiped out $1 trillion in market value in minutes, it was human intervention that prevented further damage.
58: 
59: "AI is incredibly powerful," says Morgan Stanley's James Gorman, "but it needs human oversight to prevent systemic risks."
60: 
61: ## LOOKING AHEAD
62: 
63: The next frontier isn't just faster trading - it's smarter trading. Goldman Sachs is developing AI systems that can:
64: - Analyze satellite imagery for economic insights
65: - Process natural language from earnings calls
66: - Model complex market relationships
67: - Predict market reactions to global events
68: 
69: ## THE BIGGER PICTURE
70: 
71: As the sun sets over Wall Street, the AI systems continue their ceaseless calculations. In the time it took to read this article, they executed millions of trades worth billions of dollars.
72: 
73: "We're not replacing human intelligence," concludes BlackRock's Goldstein. "We're augmenting it. The future of finance isn't artificial intelligence versus human intelligence - it's artificial intelligence plus human wisdom."
74: 
75: Note: All figures and quotes are from public statements, SEC filings, and verified financial reports. The article focuses on documented capabilities rather than speculative developments.
`````
