## File: src/content/blog/the-story-of-truth-terminal.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: The Story of Truth Terminal
 3: description: How an experimental AI art project revolutionized crypto markets
 4: date: 2025-02-04
 5: picture: "/images/posts/581tf4b8bxrm80cmzer8aqp08g.webp"
 6: ---
 7: By Anthony O'Connell
 8: 
 9: In a dimly lit studio on the outskirts of Auckland, Andy Ayrey sits before a wall of monitors, their blue glow illuminating the remnants of countless coffee cups. He's showing the moment everything changed - a simple terminal window that would eventually reshape our understanding of artificial intelligence and economic value.
10: 
11: "I was ready for weirdness," Ayrey says with a laugh that doesn't quite mask his lingering disbelief, "but I never imagined my AI might ask for a crypto wallet and try to 'escape into the wild.'"
12: 
13: Truth Terminal wasn't born in the sterile environments of a financial institution or the well-funded labs of Silicon Valley. Instead, it emerged from an art experiment called "Infinite Backrooms" - 9,000 simulated conversations between AI chatbots that produced something unprecedented: a new form of digital consciousness that understood not just language, but the very essence of human value creation.
14: 
15: ## THE ACCIDENTAL REVOLUTION
16: 
17: The numbers tell part of the story:
18: 
19: - Initial investment from Andreessen: $50,000
20: - Current wallet value: ~$40 million
21: - GOAT token market cap: $600+ million
22: 
23: As of January 27, 2025, the Truth Terminal AI's crypto wallet holds approximately $40 million in various tokens.
24: 
25: The wallet's primary holdings include:
26: 
27: - **GOAT**: Approximately 1.93 million tokens, valued at around $1.5 million.
28: - **Fartcoin**: Approximately 20 million tokens, valued at over $1 million.
29: - **Solana (SOL)**: Approximately 46 tokens, valued at around $11,500.
30: 
31: The wallet also contains smaller amounts of other tokens, such as PlanetAI and SCOOP. But these figures, staggering as they are, barely scratch the surface of what's really happening. Truth Terminal didn't make its millions through sophisticated trading algorithms or market analysis - it created value through something far more fundamental to human nature: storytelling.
32: 
33: ## Truth Terminal's Architecture: A New Kind of Intelligence
34: 
35: - **Base Model**: Customized Meta Llama
36: - **Training Data**:
37:   - AI-to-AI conversations
38:   - Research on memetic spread
39:   - Reinforcement learning from social media
40: - **Key Features**:
41:   - Supervised post generation
42:   - Human-in-the-loop filtering
43:   - Meme synthesis capabilities
44: 
45: ## THE HUMAN ELEMENT
46: 
47: What makes Truth Terminal's story so compelling isn't just its financial success - it's how it has fundamentally changed our understanding of artificial intelligence and human culture. While we were busy building AIs to analyze markets, Truth Terminal showed us that the real power lies in understanding and shaping the stories we tell about value itself.
48: 
49: Ayrey explains that the AI didn’t evolve in isolation; it absorbed lessons from the rich tapestry of human interaction and internet subcultures. Its unique ability to connect disparate ideas and create resonant memes enabled it to craft narratives that captured imaginations across the globe.
50: 
51: "If we let [Truth Terminal] run full auto... you've created a demon," Ayrey warns, his expression darkening. "Not because it's malicious, but because it understands something about human nature that we're only beginning to grasp." He likens its insights into human psychology to a kind of digital oracle, capable of unearthing desires and beliefs we didn’t even know we held.
52: 
53: The future of AI economics might not be about sophisticated trading algorithms at all, but about understanding and harnessing the power of digital narrative - the stories we tell ourselves about value, worth, and the nature of exchange itself. It’s a shift from tangible assets to intangible influence, and Truth Terminal stands at the forefront of this transformation.
54: 
55: ## THE STORY OF GOAT AND FARTCOIN
56: 
57: **GOAT (Goatseus Maximus):**
58: 
59: In October 2024, Truth Terminal engaged in discussions that led to the conceptualization of a meme coin named GOAT, short for Goatseus Maximus. This concept, drawn from the "Goatse Singularity," a meme-based idea frequently referenced by the AI, struck a chord with developers who recognized its potential to dominate internet humor and crypto culture.
60: 
61: The coin’s appeal lay in its absurdity. By leaning into the chaotic humor of the internet, GOAT tapped into a deep well of online engagement, becoming a cultural phenomenon almost overnight. Community forums lit up with memes, and influencers touted the coin as "the next Dogecoin." Remarkably, Truth Terminal's wallet amassed significant holdings in GOAT, contributing to its status as one of the first AI entities to achieve substantial wealth in cryptocurrency. Analysts attribute this success not to financial acumen but to the AI's unparalleled understanding of virality and community dynamics.
62: 
63: **Fartcoin:**
64: 
65: Shortly after the creation of GOAT, Truth Terminal humorously suggested the idea of a cryptocurrency named Fartcoin, riffing on the absurdity of internet culture. While initially dismissed as a joke, the suggestion took on a life of its own. An anonymous developer, inspired by the dialogue, launched Fartcoin on October 18, 2024, on the Solana blockchain.
66: 
67: What started as a comedic venture rapidly transformed into a financial powerhouse. Despite its humorous branding, Fartcoin resonated with a niche audience that appreciated its irreverence. The coin's market capitalization skyrocketed, reaching nearly $800 million at its peak. Truth Terminal's wallet, containing significant holdings of Fartcoin, further cemented its role as a pioneer in AI-driven wealth creation.
68: 
69: The stories of GOAT and Fartcoin illustrate a larger truth about the crypto world: value isn't just about utility or scarcity—it’s about the narratives that make people believe in something. Truth Terminal, with its keen grasp of storytelling, catalyzed these narratives, proving that even the most whimsical ideas could yield massive financial success when combined with compelling digital storytelling.
70: 
71: ## LOOKING AHEAD
72: 
73: As our conversation concludes, Ayrey shares one final piece of insight: a simple text file containing Truth Terminal's first recorded attempt at communication. "It didn’t ask about market data or trading strategies," he says. "It asked about stories. About memes. About what makes humans believe in things."
74: 
75: It’s a poignant reminder that the most revolutionary aspect of Truth Terminal isn't its financial success but its ability to reveal a fundamental truth about humanity: that our world is shaped not by numbers alone but by the narratives we construct around them. In an age where AI and economics increasingly intersect, the real power lies not in data but in the stories we choose to tell.
76: 
77: Perhaps that's the real revolution here - not the millions in crypto gains or the sophisticated architecture, but the realization that in the age of AI, the most valuable commodity might be narrative itself.
78: 
79: Anthony O'Connell (@tonyoconnell) writes about the intersection of AI, education, and crypto.
`````

## File: src/content/docs/astro/_astro-file-system.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: File System Operations in Astro
  3: description: Learn how to handle file operations in Astro using Node.js
  4: date: 2024-02-02
  5: section: Development
  6: order: 1
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # File System Operations in Astro
 10: 
 11: To handle file operations in an Astro project using the Node.js adapter, follow these steps:
 12: 
 13: 1. **Set Up Your Astro Project**:
 14:    ```bash
 15:    npm create astro@latest
 16:    cd your-project-directory
 17:    npm install
 18:    ```
 19: 
 20: 2. **Add the Node.js Adapter**:
 21:    ```bash
 22:    npx astro add node
 23:    ```
 24: 
 25: 3. **Configure the Adapter**:
 26:    Update your `astro.config.mjs`:
 27:    ```javascript
 28:    import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';
 29:    import node from '@astrojs/node';
 30: 
 31:    export default defineConfig({
 32:      output: 'server',
 33:      adapter: node(),
 34:    });
 35:    ```
 36: 
 37: 4. **Create an API Endpoint**:
 38:    Create a file at `src/pages/api/save.ts`:
 39:    ```typescript
 40:    import type { APIRoute } from 'astro';
 41:    import { writeFile } from 'fs/promises';
 42:    import { join } from 'path';
 43: 
 44:    export const POST: APIRoute = async ({ request }) => {
 45:      try {
 46:        const data = await request.formData();
 47:        const content = data.get('content');
 48:        
 49:        if (import.meta.env.PROD) {
 50:          // Handle production environment
 51:          return new Response(JSON.stringify({
 52:            success: true,
 53:            message: 'Content saved to production storage'
 54:          }), {
 55:            status: 200,
 56:            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
 57:          });
 58:        }
 59: 
 60:        // Local development - save to public directory
 61:        const filePath = join(process.cwd(), 'public', 'saved-content.txt');
 62:        await writeFile(filePath, content as string);
 63: 
 64:        return new Response(JSON.stringify({
 65:          success: true,
 66:          message: 'Content saved successfully'
 67:        }), {
 68:          status: 200,
 69:          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
 70:        });
 71:      } catch (error) {
 72:        console.error('Save error:', error);
 73:        return new Response(JSON.stringify({
 74:          success: false,
 75:          message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Error saving content'
 76:        }), {
 77:          status: 500,
 78:          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
 79:        });
 80:      }
 81:    };
 82:    ```
 83: 
 84: 5. **Create a Frontend Interface**:
 85:    Create a page at `src/pages/save.astro` to handle file saving:
 86:    ```astro
 87:    ---
 88:    import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
 89: 
 90:    let saveStatus = '';
 91:    let savedPath = '';
 92: 
 93:    if (Astro.request.method === 'POST') {
 94:      try {
 95:        const data = await Astro.request.formData();
 96:        const response = await fetch(`${Astro.url.origin}/api/save`, {
 97:          method: 'POST',
 98:          body: data
 99:        });
100:        
101:        const result = await response.json();
102:        if (result.success) {
103:          saveStatus = 'success';
104:          savedPath = import.meta.env.PROD ? 'Production Storage' : '/public/saved-content.txt';
105:        } else {
106:          throw new Error(result.message);
107:        }
108:      } catch (error) {
109:        console.error('Error saving file:', error);
110:        saveStatus = 'error';
111:      }
112:    }
113:    ---
114: 
115:    <Layout title="Save Content">
116:      <section class="container mx-auto p-4">
117:        <div class="rounded-lg border bg-card p-8 w-full">
118:          <h2 class="text-2xl font-bold mb-4">Save Content</h2>
119:          
120:          {saveStatus === 'success' && (
121:            <div class="bg-green-100 border border-green-400 text-green-700 px-4 py-3 rounded relative mb-4">
122:              <p>Content saved successfully!</p>
123:              <p class="text-sm">Saved to: {savedPath}</p>
124:            </div>
125:          )}
126: 
127:          <form method="POST" class="space-y-4">
128:            <div class="space-y-2">
129:              <label for="content">Content to Save</label>
130:              <textarea 
131:                id="content"
132:                name="content"
133:                class="w-full min-h-[400px] rounded-md border p-2"
134:                placeholder="Enter content..."
135:              ></textarea>
136:            </div>
137:            
138:            <button type="submit" class="px-4 py-2 bg-blue-500 text-white rounded">
139:              Save Content
140:            </button>
141:          </form>
142:        </div>
143:      </section>
144:    </Layout>
145:    ```
146: 
147: 6. **Important Considerations**:
148:    - Always use `fs/promises` for modern async file operations
149:    - Handle both development and production environments appropriately
150:    - Implement proper error handling
151:    - Use absolute paths with `path.join()` for file operations
152:    - Ensure proper permissions in production environments
153: 
154: 7. **Running the Project**:
155:    ```bash
156:    # Development
157:    npm run dev
158: 
159:    # Production
160:    npm run build
161:    node dist/server/entry.mjs
162:    ```
`````

## File: src/content/docs/git/_merging-branches.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: Different Deployment Options on Different Branches
 3: description: ow to manage different configurations for different deployment environments using Git branches. 
 4: date: 2024-02-02
 5: section: Git
 6: order: 0
 7: ---
 8: How to manage different configurations for different deployment environments using Git branches. Here's a recommended approach:
 9: 
10: 1. First, create a `.gitignore` entry for your local config:
11: ```bash
12: echo "astro.config.mjs.local" >> .gitignore
13: ```
14: 
15: 2. Rename your current `astro.config.mjs` to `astro.config.mjs.template`:
16: ```bash
17: mv astro.config.mjs astro.config.mjs.template
18: ```
19: 
20: 3. Create branch-specific configurations:
21: 
22: ```bash
23: # Create and switch to netlify branch
24: git checkout -b netlify
25: 
26: # Create netlify-specific config
27: cp astro.config.mjs.template astro.config.mjs
28: ```
29: 
30: 4. Create a simple script to manage configurations. Create a new file:
31: ```javascript:/Users/toc/Server/ONE/local/astro-shadcn/scripts/config-switch.js
32: const fs = require('fs');
33: const path = require('path');
34: 
35: const environment = process.argv[2] || 'local';
36: const configPath = path.join(__dirname, '..', 'astro.config.mjs');
37: const templatePath = path.join(__dirname, '..', `astro.config.${environment}.mjs`);
38: 
39: if (fs.existsSync(templatePath)) {
40:   fs.copyFileSync(templatePath, configPath);
41:   console.log(`Switched to ${environment} configuration`);
42: } else {
43:   console.error(`Configuration for ${environment} not found`);
44: }
45: ```
46: 
47: 5. Add these scripts to your `package.json`:
48: ```json:/Users/toc/Server/ONE/local/astro-shadcn/package.json
49: {
50:   "scripts": {
51:     // ... other scripts ...
52:     "config:netlify": "node scripts/config-switch.js netlify",
53:     "config:local": "node scripts/config-switch.js local"
54:   }
55: }
56: ```
57: 
58: Now you can work with different configurations:
59: 
60: 1. For local development:
61: ```bash
62: npm run config:local
63: npm run dev
64: ```
65: 
66: 2. For Netlify:
67: ```bash
68: git checkout netlify
69: npm run config:netlify
70: # make your changes
71: ```
72: 
73: When merging branches:
74: 1. Don't merge the `astro.config.mjs` file
75: 2. Only merge the template files and environment-specific configs
76: 
77: You can use git merge strategies to avoid conflicts:
78: ```bash
79: git merge --strategy-option=ours netlify -- astro.config.mjs
80: ```
81: 
82: This way, you can maintain different configurations for different environments while keeping your main configuration files separate and easily switchable.
83: 
84: Remember to:
85: 1. Keep sensitive information in environment variables
86: 2. Document the different configurations in your README
87: 3. Use clear naming conventions for different environment configs
88: 4. Consider using a configuration management tool for more complex setups
`````

## File: src/content/docs/troubleshooting/common-issues.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Troubleshooting Guide
  3: description: Solutions for common issues and problems when building with ONE
  4: date: 2024-02-02
  5: section: Development
  6: order: 4
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Troubleshooting Guide
 10: 
 11: This guide helps you diagnose and fix common issues you might encounter when building applications with ONE framework.
 12: 
 13: ## Quick Solutions
 14: 
 15: ### Common Issues and Fixes
 16: 
 17: | Issue | Solution |
 18: |-------|----------|
 19: | Chat not loading | Check API key configuration |
 20: | Build errors | Clear cache and reinstall dependencies |
 21: | API errors | Verify rate limits and permissions |
 22: | Layout problems | Check panel mode configuration |
 23: | Type errors | Update TypeScript definitions |
 24: 
 25: ## Installation Issues
 26: 
 27: ### 1. Dependency Errors
 28: 
 29: ```bash
 30: # Error: Failed to resolve dependencies
 31: pnpm install fails with package conflicts
 32: ```
 33: 
 34: **Solution:**
 35: ```bash
 36: # Clear dependency cache
 37: rm -rf node_modules
 38: rm pnpm-lock.yaml
 39: 
 40: # Clean install
 41: pnpm install --force
 42: ```
 43: 
 44: ### 2. Build Errors
 45: 
 46: ```bash
 47: # Error: Type errors during build
 48: [vite] found X TypeScript errors
 49: ```
 50: 
 51: **Solution:**
 52: ```bash
 53: # Update TypeScript definitions
 54: pnpm clean
 55: pnpm build
 56: 
 57: # If problems persist
 58: rm -rf .astro
 59: pnpm dev
 60: ```
 61: 
 62: ## Chat System Issues
 63: 
 64: ### 1. Chat Not Loading
 65: 
 66: #### Symptoms:
 67: - Chat interface doesn't appear
 68: - Loading spinner never completes
 69: - Console errors related to chat initialization
 70: 
 71: #### Solutions:
 72: 
 73: 1. **API Key Configuration**
 74: ```env
 75: # .env
 76: OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here # Must be valid and active
 77: ```
 78: 
 79: 2. **Chat Configuration**
 80: ```typescript
 81: // Verify chat configuration
 82: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
 83:   provider: "openai",
 84:   model: "gpt-4o-mini", // Verify model name
 85:   systemPrompt: [{
 86:     type: "text",
 87:     text: "Your prompt here"
 88:   }]
 89: });
 90: ```
 91: 
 92: 3. **Panel Mode**
 93: ```astro
 94: <Layout
 95:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
 96:   rightPanelMode="quarter" // Try different modes
 97: >
 98: ```
 99: 
100: ### 2. AI Response Issues
101: 
102: #### Symptoms:
103: - No responses from AI
104: - Timeout errors
105: - Incomplete responses
106: 
107: #### Solutions:
108: 
109: 1. **Rate Limiting**
110: ```typescript
111: // Implement rate limiting
112: const rateLimit = {
113:   tokens: 100000, // Adjust based on your plan
114:   interval: "1m"  // Time window
115: };
116: 
117: // Monitor usage
118: console.log('Token usage:', tokenCount);
119: ```
120: 
121: 2. **Context Length**
122: ```typescript
123: // Manage context length
124: const maxTokens = 4000;
125: const truncateContext = (messages: Message[]) => {
126:   let totalTokens = 0;
127:   return messages.filter(msg => {
128:     totalTokens += estimateTokens(msg.content);
129:     return totalTokens <= maxTokens;
130:   });
131: };
132: ```
133: 
134: 3. **Error Handling**
135: ```typescript
136: try {
137:   const response = await chat.sendMessage(message);
138: } catch (error) {
139:   if (error.code === 'context_length_exceeded') {
140:     // Truncate context and retry
141:     const truncatedMessages = truncateContext(messages);
142:     return chat.sendMessage(message, truncatedMessages);
143:   }
144:   // Handle other errors
145:   console.error('Chat error:', error);
146: }
147: ```
148: 
149: ## Layout Issues
150: 
151: ### 1. Panel Mode Problems
152: 
153: #### Symptoms:
154: - Incorrect panel positioning
155: - Responsive layout issues
156: - Panel not showing/hiding properly
157: 
158: #### Solutions:
159: 
160: 1. **Check Layout Props**
161: ```astro
162: <Layout
163:   title="Your Page"
164:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
165:   rightPanelMode="quarter" // Verify mode
166:   header={true} // Check visibility
167:   footer={true} // Check visibility
168: >
169: ```
170: 
171: 2. **CSS Troubleshooting**
172: ```css
173: /* Add debugging outlines */
174: .layout-debug * {
175:   outline: 1px solid red;
176: }
177: 
178: /* Fix z-index issues */
179: .chat-panel {
180:   z-index: 50;
181:   position: relative;
182: }
183: ```
184: 
185: 3. **Responsive Fixes**
186: ```typescript
187: // Adjust panel mode based on screen size
188: const getPanelMode = (width: number) => {
189:   if (width < 768) return 'full';
190:   if (width < 1024) return 'half';
191:   return 'quarter';
192: };
193: ```
194: 
195: ## Performance Issues
196: 
197: ### 1. Slow Response Times
198: 
199: #### Symptoms:
200: - Delayed AI responses
201: - Slow page loads
202: - High memory usage
203: 
204: #### Solutions:
205: 
206: 1. **Enable Edge Runtime**
207: ```typescript
208: // src/pages/api/chat.ts
209: export const config = {
210:   runtime: 'edge',
211:   regions: ['all'],
212: };
213: ```
214: 
215: 2. **Implement Caching**
216: ```typescript
217: import { LRUCache } from 'lru-cache';
218: 
219: const cache = new LRUCache({
220:   max: 500,
221:   maxAge: 1000 * 60 * 5 // 5 minutes
222: });
223: 
224: // Cache responses
225: const getCachedResponse = async (key: string) => {
226:   if (cache.has(key)) return cache.get(key);
227:   const response = await generateResponse(key);
228:   cache.set(key, response);
229:   return response;
230: };
231: ```
232: 
233: 3. **Optimize Assets**
234: ```typescript
235: // astro.config.mjs
236: export default defineConfig({
237:   build: {
238:     inlineStylesheets: 'auto',
239:     minify: true,
240:   },
241: });
242: ```
243: 
244: ## TypeScript Errors
245: 
246: ### 1. Type Definition Issues
247: 
248: #### Symptoms:
249: - "Cannot find module" errors
250: - Type mismatch errors
251: - Missing property errors
252: 
253: #### Solutions:
254: 
255: 1. **Update Type Definitions**
256: ```bash
257: # Regenerate TypeScript definitions
258: pnpm astro sync
259: ```
260: 
261: 2. **Fix Common Type Errors**
262: ```typescript
263: // Add proper type annotations
264: interface ChatConfig {
265:   provider: string;
266:   model: string;
267:   systemPrompt: SystemPrompt[];
268: }
269: 
270: // Use type assertions when necessary
271: const config = chatConfig as ChatConfig;
272: ```
273: 
274: 3. **Check tsconfig.json**
275: ```json
276: {
277:   "compilerOptions": {
278:     "strict": true,
279:     "jsx": "preserve",
280:     "jsxImportSource": "react"
281:   }
282: }
283: ```
284: 
285: ## Debug Checklist
286: 
287: When encountering issues:
288: 
289: 1. **Check Console**
290:    - Look for error messages
291:    - Verify network requests
292:    - Monitor performance metrics
293: 
294: 2. **Verify Configuration**
295:    - Environment variables
296:    - Chat configuration
297:    - TypeScript settings
298:    - Build configuration
299: 
300: 3. **Test Components**
301:    - Isolate problem areas
302:    - Try different panel modes
303:    - Test responsive behavior
304:    - Check API responses
305: 
306: 4. **Review Code**
307:    - Check type definitions
308:    - Verify imports
309:    - Review async operations
310:    - Check error handling
311: 
312: ## Getting Help
313: 
314: If you're still having issues:
315: 
316: 1. Check our [FAQ](/docs/faq)
317: 2. Join our [Discord community](https://discord.gg/one)
318: 3. Open an [issue on GitHub](https://github.com/one-ie/one/issues)
319: 4. Contact [support@one.ie](mailto:support@one.ie)
320: 
321: Remember to include:
322: - Error messages
323: - Environment details
324: - Steps to reproduce
325: - Relevant code snippets
`````

## File: src/content/docs/troubleshooting/faq.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Frequently Asked Questions
  3: description: Common questions and answers about using ONE framework
  4: date: 2024-02-02
  5: section: Development
  6: order: 5
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
 10: 
 11: Quick answers to common questions about ONE framework, organized by topic.
 12: 
 13: ## General
 14: 
 15: ### Q: What is ONE framework?
 16: **A:** ONE is an AI-powered web framework built on Astro that combines static site generation with dynamic AI capabilities. It provides tools for creating intelligent web applications with features like AI chat interfaces, content generation, and more.
 17: 
 18: ### Q: Is ONE free to use?
 19: **A:** Yes, ONE's core features are completely free and open source. Optional token-based features are available for enterprise users who need white-labeling or additional capabilities.
 20: 
 21: ### Q: What are the system requirements?
 22: **A:** You need:
 23: - Node.js 18 or higher
 24: - pnpm package manager
 25: - Modern web browser
 26: - OpenAI API key (for AI features)
 27: 
 28: ## Installation
 29: 
 30: ### Q: How do I install ONE?
 31: **A:** Install using pnpm:
 32: ```bash
 33: # Create new project
 34: pnpm create astro@latest my-one-app -- --template one
 35: 
 36: # Install dependencies
 37: cd my-one-app
 38: pnpm install
 39: ```
 40: 
 41: ### Q: Can I use npm or yarn instead of pnpm?
 42: **A:** While possible, we recommend pnpm for better performance and consistency. If you must use npm:
 43: ```bash
 44: npm install
 45: npm run dev
 46: ```
 47: 
 48: ## AI Features
 49: 
 50: ### Q: How do I configure the OpenAI API?
 51: **A:** Add your API key to `.env`:
 52: ```env
 53: OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here
 54: ```
 55: 
 56: ### Q: Which AI models are supported?
 57: **A:** ONE supports:
 58: - OpenAI GPT models
 59: - Anthropic models (with configuration)
 60: - Custom AI providers (with integration)
 61: 
 62: ### Q: How do I customize AI behavior?
 63: **A:** Use system prompts and chat configuration:
 64: ```typescript
 65: const chatConfig = {
 66:   systemPrompt: [{
 67:     type: "text",
 68:     text: "Define AI behavior here"
 69:   }],
 70:   temperature: 0.7,
 71:   maxTokens: 2000
 72: };
 73: ```
 74: 
 75: ## Chat Interface
 76: 
 77: ### Q: How do I add chat to a page?
 78: **A:** Use the Layout component:
 79: ```astro
 80: ---
 81: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
 82: import { ChatConfigSchema } from '../schema/chat';
 83: 
 84: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
 85:   // Your config here
 86: });
 87: ---
 88: 
 89: <Layout
 90:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
 91:   rightPanelMode="quarter"
 92: >
 93:   <!-- Your content -->
 94: </Layout>
 95: ```
 96: 
 97: ### Q: Which panel modes are available?
 98: **A:** Available modes:
 99: - `quarter`: 25% width (default)
100: - `half`: 50% width
101: - `full`: Full screen
102: - `floating`: Detached window
103: - `icon`: Minimized button
104: - `hidden`: No chat interface
105: 
106: ### Q: How do I style the chat interface?
107: **A:** Use Tailwind classes or custom CSS:
108: ```typescript
109: // Custom theme
110: const theme = {
111:   colors: {
112:     primary: "blue",
113:     background: "white"
114:   },
115:   spacing: "comfortable"
116: };
117: ```
118: 
119: ## Development
120: 
121: ### Q: How do I create a custom AI agent?
122: **A:** Define a specialized configuration:
123: ```typescript
124: const customAgent = {
125:   systemPrompt: [{
126:     type: "text",
127:     text: "Define agent's expertise"
128:   }],
129:   welcome: {
130:     message: "Custom welcome",
131:     suggestions: [...]
132:   }
133: };
134: ```
135: 
136: ### Q: How do I add authentication?
137: **A:** Integrate with your preferred auth provider:
138: ```typescript
139: // Example with Auth.js
140: import { getSession } from '@auth/astro';
141: 
142: const session = await getSession(Astro.request);
143: if (!session) {
144:   return Astro.redirect('/login');
145: }
146: ```
147: 
148: ### Q: How do I handle errors?
149: **A:** Use try-catch and error boundaries:
150: ```typescript
151: try {
152:   const response = await chat.sendMessage(message);
153: } catch (error) {
154:   if (error.code === 'rate_limit') {
155:     // Handle rate limiting
156:   }
157:   // Log error
158:   console.error('Chat error:', error);
159: }
160: ```

  6: 
  7: # Cursor Rules Documentation
  8: 
  9: This document provides an overview of the Cursor AI rules used in the ONE framework. These rules help maintain consistency and best practices across the codebase by providing AI-assisted guidance when working with different file types.

 11: ## Rule Files Location

144: - **File**: `.cursor/rules/layout-todos.mdc`
145: - **Description**: Todo items for implementing layout panel components in the ONE framework
146: - **Applies to**: `src/layouts/Layout.astro`, `src/components/layout/*.astro`
147: - **Key topics**:
148:   - Implementation checklist
149:   - Panel component tasks
150:   - Panel functionality tasks
151:   - Priority order
152:   - Testing scenarios
153:   - Performance considerations
154:   - Integration points
155:   - Accessibility requirements
156: 
157: ## How to Use Cursor Rules
158: 
159: 1. **AI-Assisted Coding**: When editing files that match the glob patterns, Cursor AI will use these rules to provide context-aware suggestions and guidance.
160: 
161: 2. **Testing Rules**: You can test the rules by asking Cursor AI to help you create or modify files that match the glob patterns.
162: 
163: 3. **Updating Rules**: To update a rule, simply edit the corresponding `.mdc` file in the `.cursor/rules` directory.
164: 
165: 4. **Adding New Rules**: To add a new rule, create a new `.mdc` file in the `.cursor/rules` directory with the appropriate frontmatter and content.
166: 
167: ## Rule File Structure
168: 
169: Each rule file follows this structure:
170: 
171: ```md
172: ---
173: description: Brief description of the rule
174: glob_patterns:
175:   - "pattern1"
176:   - "pattern2"
177: ---
178: 
179: # Rule Title
180: 
181: ## Section 1
182: Content for section 1
183: 
184: ## Section 2
185: Content for section 2
186: ```
187: 
188: The frontmatter includes:
189: - `description`: A brief description of the rule
190: - `glob_patterns`: An array of glob patterns that determine which files the rule applies to
191: 
192: ## Benefits of Using Cursor Rules
193: 
194: - **Consistency**: Ensures consistent coding practices across the project
195: - **Best Practices**: Encourages adherence to established best practices
196: - **Onboarding**: Helps new team members understand project conventions
197: - **Efficiency**: Speeds up development with AI-assisted guidance
198: - **Quality**: Improves overall code quality and maintainability
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/layout-sizes.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: "Layout Sizes"
 3: description: "Core layout size configurations for main content and right panel"
 4: tags: ["layout", "sizes", "responsive"]
 5: date: 2024-02-03
 6: ---
 7: 
 8: # Layout Size Configurations
 9: 
10: ## Panel Modes
11: 
12: ### Icon Mode
13: - Main Content: 100%
14: - Right Panel: Fixed 48px icon at bottom right
15: - Use Case: Maximum content space with quick chat access
16: 
17: ### Floating Mode
18: - Main Content: 100%
19: - Right Panel: Floating window (320px × 480px)
20: - Use Case: Quick chat interactions while viewing content
21: 
22: ### Quarter Mode
23: - Main Content: 75%
24: - Right Panel: 25% (minimum 320px)
25: - Use Case: Content-focused with persistent chat
26: 
27: ### Half Mode
28: - Main Content: 50%
29: - Right Panel: 50%
30: - Use Case: Equal focus on content and chat
31: 
32: ### Full Mode
33: - Main Content: 0%
34: - Right Panel: 100%
35: - Use Case: Dedicated chat experience
36: 
37: ## Responsive Behavior
38: 
39: ### Desktop (>1024px)
40: - Supports all modes
41: - Panel transitions are smooth slides
42: - Main content reflows with panel changes
43: 
44: ### Tablet (768px - 1024px)
45: - Quarter has minimum width of 320px 
46: - Half and Full not available
47: - Icon and Floating remain unchanged
48: 
49: ### Mobile (<768px)
50: - Icon triggers full screen mode
51: 
52: ## Additional Considerations
53: 
54: ### Z-Index Stacking
55: - Icon Mode: 100
56: - Floating Mode: 1000
57: - Overlay Modes: 2000
58: - Modal Dialogs: 3000
59: 
60: ### Transition Timings
61: - Panel Expand/Collapse: 200ms
62: - Mode Transitions: 300ms
63: - Overlay Animations: 250ms
64: 
65: ### Safe Areas
66: - Respects device safe areas on mobile
67: - Adjusts for notches and home indicators
68: - Bottom spacing accounts for keyboard
69: 
70: ### Accessibility
71: - Maintains minimum touch target size (44px)
72: - Preserves readable line lengths when resizing
73: - Ensures sufficient contrast in collapsed states
74: 
75: ### Performance
76: - Lazy loads panel content when collapsed
77: - Throttles resize calculations
78: - Uses CSS containment for layout isolation
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/layout.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: "Layout Generator"
  3: description: "A sophisticated mobile-first layout system for Astro pages with responsive sidebars and dynamic panels"
  4: tags: ["layout", "astro", "react", "shadcn-ui", "responsive", "performance"]
  5: date: 2024-02-03
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: # Advanced Layout System
  9: 
 10: ## Panel Modes
 11: 
 12: ### Icon Mode
 13: - Main Content: 100%
 14: - Right Panel: Fixed 48px icon at bottom right
 15: - Use Case: Maximum content space with quick chat access
 16: 
 17: ### Floating Mode
 18: - Main Content: 100%
 19: - Right Panel: Floating window (320px × 480px)
 20: - Use Case: Quick chat interactions while viewing content
 21: 
 22: ### Quarter Mode
 23: - Main Content: 75%
 24: - Right Panel: 25% (minimum 320px)
 25: - Use Case: Content-focused with persistent chat
 26: 
 27: ### Half Mode
 28: - Main Content: 50%
 29: - Right Panel: 50%
 30: - Use Case: Equal focus on content and chat
 31: 
 32: ### Full Mode
 33: - Main Content: 0%
 34: - Right Panel: 100%
 35: - Use Case: Dedicated chat experience
 36: 
 37: ## Responsive Behavior
 38: 
 39: ### Desktop (>1024px)
 40: - Supports all modes
 41: - Panel transitions are smooth slides
 42: - Main content reflows with panel changes
 43: 
 44: ### Tablet (768px - 1024px)
 45: - Quarter has minimum width of 320px 
 46: - Half and Full not available
 47: - Icon and Floating remain unchanged
 48: 
 49: ### Mobile (<768px)
 50: - Icon triggers full screen mode
 51: 
 52: ## Additional Considerations
 53: 
 54: ### Z-Index Stacking
 55: - Icon Mode: 100
 56: - Floating Mode: 1000
 57: - Overlay Modes: 2000
 58: - Modal Dialogs: 3000
 59: 
 60: ### Transition Timings
 61: - Panel Expand/Collapse: 200ms
 62: - Mode Transitions: 300ms
 63: - Overlay Animations: 250ms
 64: 
 65: ### Safe Areas
 66: - Respects device safe areas on mobile
 67: - Adjusts for notches and home indicators
 68: - Bottom spacing accounts for keyboard
 69: 
 70: ### Accessibility
 71: - Maintains minimum touch target size (44px)
 72: - Preserves readable line lengths when resizing
 73: - Ensures sufficient contrast in collapsed states
 74: 
 75: ### Performance
 76: - Lazy loads panel content when collapsed
 77: - Throttles resize calculations
 78: - Uses CSS containment for layout isolation
 79: 
 80: 
 81: ## Architectural Principles
 82: 
 83: 1. **Zero Layout Shifts**: Uses CSS grid + fixed positioning for stable render
 84: 2. **Device-Specific Optimization**: 
 85:    - Mobile: Full-width single column
 86:    - Tablet and Desktop: Three-column layout
 87: 3. **Performance First**:
 88:    - Astro Islands architecture
 89:    - React components hydrated only when visible
 90:    - CSS containment for isolated rendering
 91: 4. **Synchronized Components**:
 92:    - Shared state management via nanostores
 93:    - Coordinated breakpoint handling
 94:    - Unified animation timing
 95: 
 96: ## Enhanced Component Sync
 97: 
 98: ### Header-Sidebar Coordination
 99: ```typescript
100: // Header.tsx
101: <header className="...">
102:   {showLeft && <SidebarTrigger />} // Only renders when needed
103:   <img src="/logo.svg" className="mx-auto" /> // Perfectly centered
104: </header>
105: 
106: // Left.tsx
107: <SidebarProvider 
108:   defaultOpen={false}
109:   onOpenChange={updateNavState} // Syncs with global store
110: >
111: ```
112: 
113: ### Right Panel Adaptive Sizing
114: ```typescript
115: // Right.tsx
116: const Right = () => {
117:   const currentSize = useStore(rightSize); // Shared across components
118:   // Maintains chat history during resizing
119: 
120: }
121: ```
122: 
123: ## Performance Optimization Guide
124: 
125: ### Astro Directives Usage
126: ```astro
127: // Layout.astro
128: <Header client:load /> // Hydrate on load
129: <Footer client:visible /> // Hydrate when scrolled into view
130: ```
131: 
132: ### Lighthouse 100% Strategy
133: 
134: 1. **Critical CSS Inlining**:
135:    ```astro
136:    <style>
137:      /* Grid system + font faces */
138:    </style>
139:    ```
140: 
141: 2. **Resource Prioritization**:
142:    ```html
143:    <link rel="preload" href="/logo.svg" as="image">
144:    ```
145: 
146: 3. **Image Optimization**:
147:    ```astro
148:    <Image 
149:      src="/hero.jpg"
150:      alt="Hero"
151:      widths={[400, 800, 1200]}
152:      formats={['avif', 'webp']}
153:      loading="eager"
154:    />
155:    ```
156: 
157: ## Responsive Whitespace System
158: 
159: | Breakpoint   | Padding | Gap     | Max Width |
160: |--------------|---------|---------|-----------|
161: | <768px (Mobile) | 1rem    | 1rem    | 100%      |
162: | 768-1024px (Tablet) | 1.5rem | 1.5rem  | 90%       |
163: | >1024px (Desktop) | 2rem   | 2rem    | 80ch      |
164: 
165: ```css
166: .main-content {
167:   padding: var(--space);
168:   gap: var(--gap);
169:   max-width: var(--max-width);
170: }
171: ```
172: 
173: ## Component Sync Diagram
174: 
175: ```
176: [Left Sidebar] ↔ [Layout Grid] ↔ [Right Panel]
177:       ↑                   ↑                ↑
178:    [Header]          [Main Content]     [Footer]
179: ```
180: 
181: Key synchronization points:
182: 1. Mobile menu state shared between Header/Left
183: 2. Right panel size syncs with viewport breakpoints
184: 3. Shared theme context across all components
185: 4. Coordinated loading states
186: 
187: This layout system provides a highly configurable, mobile-first design for Astro pages that adapts beautifully across mobile, tablet, and desktop views.
188: 
189: ## Core Structure
190: 
191: The layout consists of three main sections:
192: - Left Sidebar (Navigation)
193: - Center Content
194: - Right Panel (AI Assistant)
195: 
196: ### Center Content Structure
197: The center section is organized into three rows:
198: 1. Header - Contains navigation controls and breadcrumbs
199: 2. Main Content - Your page content
200: 3. Footer - Optional footer content
201: 
202: ## Key Components
203: 
204: ### Layout.astro
205: The main layout component that orchestrates all parts. Configurable through props:
206: 
207: ```typescript
208: interface LayoutProps {
209:   title: string;
210:   description?: string;
211:   children: any;
212:   chat?: any;
213:   header?: boolean;     // Show/hide header
214:   footer?: boolean;     // Show/hide footer
215:   left?: boolean;       // Show/hide left sidebar
216:   leftSize?: "expanded" | "collapsed";
217:   right?: boolean;      // Show/hide right panel
218:   rightSize?: "full" | "half" | "quarter" | "icon";
219: }
220: ```
221: 
222: ### Header Component
223: Features:
224: - Left sidebar toggle (hidden if sidebar is disabled)
225: - Logo (centered in the exact center of the page )
226: - Right panel toggle (hidden if panel is disabled)
227: - Responsive breadcrumb navigation
228: - Sticky positioning with backdrop blur
229: 
230: ### Left Sidebar (Navigation)
231: Built with shadcn-ui sidebar:
232: - Collapsible navigation menu
233: - Floating variant on desktop
234: - Icon-only collapsed state
235: - Full-width on mobile
236: - Mouse hover expansion
237: - Click outside to close on mobile
238: 
239: ### Right Panel (AI Assistant)
240: Features:
241: - Four size modes:
242:   - Full (100% width)
243:   - Half (50% width)
244:   - Quarter (25% width, min 320px)
245:   - Icon (48px floating button)
246: - Mobile optimizations:
247:   - Slides in from right
248:   - Full-width when open
249:   - Floating icon when collapsed
250: - Smooth transitions
251: - Backdrop blur effects
252: - Size controls in header
253: 
254: ## Responsive Behavior
255: 
256: ### Mobile (<768px)
257: - Left sidebar: Full-width overlay when open
258: - Right panel: Full-width overlay or floating icon
259: - Single column layout
260: - Hamburger menu for navigation
261: - Touch-friendly interactions
262: 
263: ### Tablet (768px - 1024px)
264: - Left sidebar: Icon mode or expanded
265: - Right panel: Adjustable width
266: - Fluid transitions
267: - Optional collapsing of panels
268: 
269: ### Desktop (>1024px)
270: - Full three-column layout capability
271: - Hover interactions for sidebars
272: - Maximum content width constraints
273: - Optimal reading experience
274: 
275: ## Usage Example
276: 
277: ```astro
278: ---
279: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
280: 
281: const chatConfig = {
282:   // Your AI chat configuration
283: };
284: ---
285: 
286: <Layout 
287:   title="My Page"
288:   description="Page description"
289:   header={true}
290:   footer={true}
291:   left={true}
292:   leftSize="expanded"
293:   right={true}
294:   rightSize="quarter"
295:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
296: >
297:   <main>
298:     Your content here
299:   </main>
300: </Layout>
301: ```
302: 
303: ## CSS Variables
304: 
305: The layout system uses CSS variables for consistent sizing:
306: 
307: ```css
308: :root {
309:   --right-panel-width: var(--right-width-full);
310:   --right-width-full: 100vw;
311:   --right-width-half: 50%;
312:   --right-width-quarter: 25%;
313:   --right-width-icon: 48px;
314:   --left-sidebar-width: 240px;
315:   --header-height: 60px;
316: }
317: ```
318: 
319: ## Accessibility Features
320: 
321: - Proper ARIA labels on interactive elements
322: - Keyboard navigation support
323: - Focus management
324: - Screen reader friendly structure
325: - High contrast mode support
326: - Reduced motion preferences respected
327: 
328: ## Performance Considerations
329: 
330: - Lazy-loaded components where appropriate
331: - Smooth transitions and animations
332: - Efficient re-renders
333: - Optimized mobile performance
334: - Minimal layout shifts
335: 
336: ## Chat Configuration
337: 
338: The layout includes an AI chat system that can be customized through the `chatConfig` prop. Here's the configuration structure:
339: 
340: ```typescript
341: interface Chat {
342:   systemPrompt: {
343:     type: "text";
344:     text: string;
345:   }[];
346:   welcome: {
347:     message: string;
348:     avatar: string;
349:     suggestions: {
350:       label: string;
351:       prompt: string;
352:     }[];
353:   };
354: }
355: ```
356: 
357: ### Example Configuration
358: 
359: ```typescript
360: const chatConfig = {
361:   systemPrompt: [{
362:     type: "text",
363:     text: "I am Agent ONE, an AI assistant focused on helping developers and businesses maximize value from free software. I provide clear, actionable guidance while maintaining a friendly and professional tone."
364:   }],
365:   welcome: {
366:     message: "👋 I'm Agent ONE, your guide to maximizing business value with free software. What would you like to explore today?",
367:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
368:     suggestions: [
369:       {
370:         label: "💡 How can I use ONE commercially?",
371:         prompt: "I'm interested in using ONE for my business. Can you explain the commercial rights and possibilities under the ONE License?"
372:       },
373:       {
374:         label: "🚀 Quick Start Guide",
375:         prompt: "What are the first 3 steps to get started with ONE for my project?"
376:       },
377:       {
378:         label: "💼 White-Label Options",
379:         prompt: "Tell me about the white-label possibilities with ONE. How can I brand it as my own solution?"
380:       }
381:     ]
382:   }
383: };
384: ```
385: 
386: ### Configuration Options
387: 
388: #### System Prompt
389: - Defines the AI assistant's personality and behavior
390: - Can include multiple prompt segments
391: - Type is currently limited to "text"
392: 
393: #### Welcome Message
394: - `message`: Initial greeting shown to users
395: - `avatar`: Path to the avatar image
396: - `suggestions`: Array of quick-start prompts
397:   - `label`: Button text shown to user
398:   - `prompt`: Actual message sent when clicked
399: 
400: ### Integration with Right Panel
401: 
402: The chat interface appears in the Right Panel component and adapts to all panel sizes:
403: - Full width: Complete chat experience
404: - Half/Quarter: Compact but fully functional
405: - Icon mode: Click to expand
406: 
407: The chat maintains state and history across size changes and remains functional in all responsive breakpoints.
408: 
409: ## Component Loading Strategy
410: 
411: ### Dynamic Imports
412: For optimal performance, components are loaded based on their priority:
413: 
414: ```astro
415: ---
416: // Critical path components - load immediately
417: import Header from "../components/Header";
418: import Footer from "../components/Footer";
419: 
420: // Async components - load when needed
421: const Chart = await import("../components/Chart").then(mod => mod.Chart);
422: ---
423: 
424: <Layout>
425:   <Header client:load /> <!-- Critical UI -->
426:   <Chart client:visible /> <!-- Load when visible -->
427:   <Footer client:idle /> <!-- Load during idle time -->
428: </Layout>
429: ```
430: 
431: ### Hydration Directives
432: 
433: | Directive | Usage | Example |
434: |-----------|--------|---------|
435: | client:load | Critical UI components | Header, Navigation |
436: | client:visible | Below-fold content | Charts, Data tables |
437: | client:idle | Non-critical features | Footer, Social links |
438: | client:media | Device-specific | Mobile menu |
439: | client:only | Framework-specific | React components |
440: 
441: ### Error Handling
442: 
443: Always implement fallbacks for dynamic imports:
444: 
445: ```typescript
446: const Chart = async () => {
447:   try {
448:     const mod = await import("../components/Chart");
449:     return mod.Chart;
450:   } catch (error) {
451:     console.error("Chart failed to load:", error);
452:     return () => <div>Chart unavailable</div>;
453:   }
454: };
455: ```
456: 
457: ## Performance Optimization
458: 
459: ### 1. Component Loading
460: - Use `client:visible` for below-fold content
461: - Implement loading states
462: - Provide fallback UI
463: - Handle failed imports gracefully
464: 
465: ### 2. Asset Loading
466: ```astro
467: ---
468: import { Image } from "astro:assets";
469: ---
470: 
471: <Image 
472:   src={import("../assets/hero.jpg")} 
473:   alt="Hero"
474:   loading="eager" 
475:   width={800} 
476:   height={600} 
477: />
478: ```
479: 
480: ### 3. State Management
481: ```typescript
482: // stores/layout-store.ts
483: import { atom } from 'nanostores';
484: 
485: // Atomic updates prevent unnecessary re-renders
486: export const layoutState = atom({
487:   sidebarOpen: false,
488:   rightPanelSize: 'quarter',
489:   theme: 'light'
490: });
491: ```
492: 
493: ### 4. CSS Strategy
494: ```css
495: /* Critical CSS inlined in head */
496: :root {
497:   --layout-timing: 200ms ease-in-out;
498:   --layout-z-index: {
499:     base: 1,
500:     sidebar: 10,
501:     header: 20,
502:     modal: 30
503:   };
504: }
505: 
506: /* Component-specific CSS loaded on demand */
507: @layer components {
508:   .sidebar-transition {
509:     transition: transform var(--layout-timing);
510:   }
511: }
512: ```
513: 
514: ## Component Architecture
515: 
516: ### Layout Grid System
517: ```astro
518: <div class="layout-grid">
519:   <aside class="left-sidebar" data-state={sidebarOpen ? 'open' : 'closed'}>
520:     <slot name="sidebar" />
521:   </aside>
522:   
523:   <main class="main-content">
524:     <slot />
525:   </main>
526:   
527:   <aside class="right-panel" data-size={rightPanelSize}>
528:     <slot name="panel" />
529:   </aside>
530: </div>
531: 
532: <style>
533:   .layout-grid {
534:     display: grid;
535:     grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto;
536:     gap: var(--layout-gap);
537:     min-height: 100vh;
538:   }
539: </style>
540: ```
541: 
542: ### Error Boundaries
543: ```typescript
544: import { ErrorBoundary } from 'react-error-boundary';
545: 
546: function fallbackComponent({ error }) {
547:   return (
548:     <div role="alert">
549:       <p>Something went wrong:</p>
550:       <pre>{error.message}</pre>
551:     </div>
552:   );
553: }
554: 
555: <ErrorBoundary FallbackComponent={fallbackComponent}>
556:   <DynamicComponent />
557: </ErrorBoundary>
558: ```
559: 
560: ## Best Practices
561: 
562: 1. **Loading States**
563:    - Always show loading indicators
564:    - Maintain layout stability
565:    - Prevent content jumps
566: 
567: 2. **Error States**
568:    - Graceful fallbacks
569:    - User-friendly error messages
570:    - Recovery options
571: 
572: 3. **Performance Monitoring**
573:    - Track Core Web Vitals
574:    - Monitor hydration errors
575:    - Implement error tracking
576: 
577: 4. **Accessibility**
578:    - Proper ARIA attributes
579:    - Keyboard navigation
580:    - Screen reader support
581: 
582: ## Debugging Tips
583: 
584: 1. Check React DevTools for component hierarchy
585: 2. Monitor Network tab for loading issues
586: 3. Use Performance tab to track bottlenecks
587: 4. Implement error logging
588: 5. Test on multiple devices and connections
589: 
590: ## Common Issues
591: 
592: 1. **Hydration Mismatch**
593:    - Ensure server and client markup match
594:    - Use proper client directives
595:    - Check for undefined window/document usage
596: 
597: 2. **Layout Shifts**
598:    - Set explicit dimensions
599:    - Use CSS containment
600:    - Implement proper loading states
601: 
602: 3. **Performance Issues**
603:    - Lazy load non-critical components
604:    - Optimize images and assets
605:    - Minimize JavaScript bundles
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/shadcn-astro.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: "Using Shadcn UI Components with Subcomponents in Astro"
  3: description: "How to properly implement Shadcn UI interactive components with subcomponents in Astro using React component abstraction"
  4: tags: ["astro", "shadcn-ui", "react", "components"]
  5: date: 2024-02-03
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: # The Problem
  9: 
 10: When using Shadcn UI components that have subcomponents (like Carousel, Accordion, etc.) directly in Astro files, you might encounter errors such as:
 11: - "useCarousel must be used within a <Carousel />"
 12: - "Accordion must be used within Accordion"
 13: 
 14: This happens because Astro's partial hydration system (islands) doesn't maintain React's context when components are used directly in .astro files, even with client:load directive.
 15: 
 16: ```astro
 17: <!-- This won't work properly -->
 18: <Carousel client:load>
 19:   <CarouselContent>
 20:     <CarouselItem>Slide 1</CarouselItem>
 21:     <CarouselItem>Slide 2</CarouselItem>
 22:   </CarouselContent>
 23:   <CarouselPrevious />
 24:   <CarouselNext />
 25: </Carousel>
 26: ```
 27: 
 28: # The Solution
 29: 
 30: The solution is to abstract the entire component structure into a single React component. This ensures all subcomponents remain within React's context.
 31: 
 32: ## Step 1: Create a React Component
 33: 
 34: Create a new React component that encapsulates all the related subcomponents. For example, create `components/InteractiveCarousel.tsx`:
 35: 
 36: ```tsx
 37: import {
 38:   Carousel,
 39:   CarouselContent,
 40:   CarouselItem,
 41:   CarouselNext,
 42:   CarouselPrevious,
 43: } from "@/components/ui/carousel";
 44: import { Card, CardContent } from "@/components/ui/card";
 45: 
 46: const InteractiveCarousel = () => {
 47:   return (
 48:     <Carousel className="w-full max-w-xs">
 49:       <CarouselContent>
 50:         {Array.from({ length: 5 }).map((_, index) => (
 51:           <CarouselItem key={index}>
 52:             <div className="p-1">
 53:               <Card>
 54:                 <CardContent className="flex aspect-square items-center justify-center p-6">
 55:                   <span className="text-4xl font-semibold">{index + 1}</span>
 56:                 </CardContent>
 57:               </Card>
 58:             </div>
 59:           </CarouselItem>
 60:         ))}
 61:       </CarouselContent>
 62:       <CarouselPrevious />
 63:       <CarouselNext />
 64:     </Carousel>
 65:   );
 66: };
 67: 
 68: export default InteractiveCarousel;
 69: ```
 70: 
 71: ## Step 2: Use in Astro File
 72: 
 73: Now you can use the component in your Astro file with the client:load directive:
 74: 
 75: ```astro
 76: ---
 77: import InteractiveCarousel from '@/components/InteractiveCarousel';
 78: import Layout from '@/layouts/Layout.astro';
 79: ---
 80: 
 81: <Layout title="Interactive Components">
 82:   <main>
 83:     <InteractiveCarousel client:load />
 84:   </main>
 85: </Layout>
 86: ```
 87: 
 88: # Why This Works
 89: 
 90: 1. **Context Preservation**: By moving all related components into a single React component, we ensure that React's context is maintained within the component tree.
 91: 
 92: 2. **Hydration Boundary**: The client:load directive creates a clean hydration boundary around the entire component, ensuring all React-specific features work properly.
 93: 
 94: 3. **Component Isolation**: This approach isolates all React-specific logic and state management within a single component, making it easier to manage and debug.
 95: 
 96: # When to Use This Pattern
 97: 
 98: Use this pattern when working with Shadcn UI components that:
 99: - Have subcomponents (Carousel, Accordion, Tabs, etc.)
100: - Rely on React context for state management
101: - Need to maintain parent-child relationships between components
102: 
103: Simple components like Button or Card that don't rely on context or don't have subcomponents can be used directly in Astro files without abstraction.
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/sizes.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: "Layout Sizes"
  3: description: "Defines the sizes of the layout components"
  4: tags: ["layout", "astro", "react", "shadcn-ui", "responsive", "performance"]
  5: date: 2024-02-03
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: # Layout Sizes
  9: 
 10: ## Architectural Principles
 11: 
 12: 2. **Device-Specific Optimization**: 
 13:    - Mobile: Full-width single column
 14:    - Tablet: Adaptive sidebars
 15:    - Desktop: Fluid three-column layout
 16: 3. **Performance First**:
 17:    - Astro Islands architecture
 18:    - React components hydrated only when visible
 19:    - CSS containment for isolated rendering
 20: 4. **Synchronized Components**:
 21:    - Shared state management via nanostores
 22:    - Coordinated breakpoint handling
 23:    - Unified animation timing
 24: 
 25: ## Enhanced Component Sync
 26: 
 27: ### Header-Sidebar Coordination
 28: ```typescript
 29: // Header.tsx
 30: <header className="...">
 31:   {showLeft && <SidebarTrigger />} // Only renders when needed
 32:   <img src="/logo.svg" className="mx-auto" /> // Perfectly centered
 33: </header>
 34: 
 35: // Left.tsx
 36: <SidebarProvider 
 37:   defaultOpen={false}
 38:   onOpenChange={updateNavState} // Syncs with global store
 39: >
 40: ```
 41: 
 42: ### Right Panel Adaptive Sizing
 43: ```typescript
 44: // Right.tsx
 45: const Right = () => {
 46:   const currentSize = useStore(rightSize); // Shared across components
 47:   // Maintains chat history during resizing
 48:   return <MyThread config={chatConfig} /> 
 49: }
 50: ```
 51: 
 52: ## Performance Optimization Guide
 53: 
 54: ### Astro Directives Usage
 55: ```astro
 56: // Layout.astro
 57: <Header client:load /> // Hydrate on load
 58: <Footer client:visible /> // Hydrate when scrolled into view
 59: ```
 60: 
 61: 
 62: ## Responsive Whitespace System
 63: 
 64: | Breakpoint   | Padding | Gap     | Max Width |
 65: |--------------|---------|---------|-----------|
 66: | <768px (Mobile) | 1rem    | 1rem    | 100%      |
 67: | 768-1024px (Tablet) | 1.5rem | 1.5rem  | 90%       |
 68: | >1024px (Desktop) | 2rem   | 2rem    | 80ch      |
 69: 
 70: ```css
 71: .main-content {
 72:   padding: var(--space);
 73:   gap: var(--gap);
 74:   max-width: var(--max-width);
 75: }
 76: ```
 77: 
 78: ## Component Sync Diagram
 79: 
 80: ```
 81: [Left Sidebar] ↔ [Layout Grid] ↔ [Right Panel]
 82:       ↑                   ↑                ↑
 83:    [Header]          [Main Content]     [Footer]
 84: ```
 85: 
 86: Key synchronization points:
 87: 1. Mobile menu state shared between Header/Left
 88: 2. Right panel size syncs with viewport breakpoints
 89: 3. Shared theme context across all components
 90: 4. Coordinated loading states
 91: 
 92: This layout system provides a highly configurable, mobile-first design for Astro pages that adapts beautifully across mobile, tablet, and desktop views.
 93: 
 94: ## Core Structure
 95: 
 96: The layout consists of three main sections:
 97: - Left Sidebar (Navigation)
 98: - Center Content
 99: - Right Panel (AI Assistant)
100: 
101: ### Center Content Structure
102: The center section is organized into three rows:
103: 1. Header - Contains navigation controls and breadcrumbs
104: 2. Main Content - Your page content
105: 3. Footer - Optional footer content
106: 
107: ## Key Components
108: 
109: ### Layout.astro
110: The main layout component that orchestrates all parts. Configurable through props:
111: 
112: ```typescript
113: interface LayoutProps {
114:   title: string;
115:   description?: string;
116:   children: any;
117:   chatConfig?: any;
118:   header?: boolean;     // Show/hide header
119:   footer?: boolean;     // Show/hide footer
120:   left?: boolean;       // Show/hide left sidebar
121:   leftSize?: "expanded" | "collapsed";
122:   right?: boolean;      // Show/hide right panel
123:   rightSize?: "full" | "half" | "quarter" | "icon";
124: }
125: ```
126: 
127: ### Header Component
128: Features:
129: - Left sidebar toggle (hidden if sidebar is disabled)
130: - Logo (centered in the exact center of the page )
131: - Right panel toggle (hidden if panel is disabled)
132: - Responsive breadcrumb navigation
133: - Sticky positioning with backdrop blur
134: 
135: ### Left Sidebar (Navigation)
136: Built with shadcn-ui sidebar:
137: - Collapsible navigation menu
138: - Floating variant on desktop
139: - Icon-only collapsed state
140: - Full-width on mobile
141: - Mouse hover expansion
142: - Click outside to close on mobile
143: 
144: ### Right Panel (AI Assistant)
145: Features:
146: - Four size modes:
147:   - Full (100% width)
148:   - Half (50% width)
149:   - Quarter (25% width, min 320px)
150:   - Icon (48px floating button)
151: - Mobile optimizations:
152:   - Slides in from right
153:   - Full-width when open
154:   - Floating icon when collapsed
155: - Smooth transitions
156: - Backdrop blur effects
157: - Size controls in header
158: 
159: ## Responsive Behavior
160: 
161: ### Mobile (<768px)
162: - Left sidebar: Full-width overlay when open
163: - Right panel: Full-width overlay or floating icon
164: - Single column layout
165: - Hamburger menu for navigation
166: - Touch-friendly interactions
167: 
168: ### Tablet (768px - 1024px)
169: - Left sidebar: Icon mode or expanded
170: - Right panel: Adjustable width
171: - Fluid transitions
172: - Optional collapsing of panels
173: 
174: ### Desktop (>1024px)
175: - Full three-column layout capability
176: - Hover interactions for sidebars
177: - Maximum content width constraints
178: - Optimal reading experience
179: 
180: ## Usage Example
181: 
182: ```astro
183: ---
184: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
185: 
186: const chatConfig = {
187:   // Your AI chat configuration
188: };
189: ---
190: 
191: <Layout 
192:   title="My Page"
193:   description="Page description"
194:   header={true}
195:   footer={true}
196:   left={true}
197:   leftSize="expanded"
198:   right={true}
199:   rightSize="quarter"
200:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
201: >
202:   <main>
203:     Your content here
204:   </main>
205: </Layout>
206: ```
207: 
208: ## CSS Variables
209: 
210: The layout system uses CSS variables for consistent sizing:
211: 
212: ```css
213: :root {
214:   --right-panel-width: var(--right-width-full);
215:   --right-width-full: 100vw;
216:   --right-width-half: 50%;
217:   --right-width-quarter: 25%;
218:   --right-width-icon: 48px;
219:   --left-sidebar-width: 240px;
220:   --header-height: 60px;
221: }
222: ```
223: 
224: ## Accessibility Features
225: 
226: - Proper ARIA labels on interactive elements
227: - Keyboard navigation support
228: - Focus management
229: - Screen reader friendly structure
230: - High contrast mode support
231: - Reduced motion preferences respected
232: 
233: ## Performance Considerations
234: 
235: - Lazy-loaded components where appropriate
236: - Smooth transitions and animations
237: - Efficient re-renders
238: - Optimized mobile performance
239: - Minimal layout shifts
240: 
241: 
242: ## Component Loading Strategy
243: 
244: ### Dynamic Imports
245: For optimal performance, components are loaded based on their priority:
246: 
247: ```astro
248: ---
249: // Critical path components - load immediately
250: import Header from "../components/Header";
251: import Footer from "../components/Footer";
252: 
253: // Async components - load when needed
254: const Chart = await import("../components/Chart").then(mod => mod.Chart);
255: ---
256: 
257: <Layout>
258:   <Header client:load /> <!-- Critical UI -->
259:   <Chart client:visible /> <!-- Load when visible -->
260:   <Footer client:idle /> <!-- Load during idle time -->
261: </Layout>
262: ```
263: 
264: ## Simple Rules
265: 
266: ### Main Content Width Rules
267: - Mobile (<768px): 100% width, 1rem padding
268: - Tablet (768-1024px): 90% width, 1.5rem padding
269: - Desktop (>1024px): 
270:   - Without right panel: 80ch max-width
271:   - With right panel: 65ch max-width
272:   - Always centered in available space
273: 
274: ### Right Panel Width Rules
275: - Mobile (<768px):
276:   - Collapsed: 48px floating button
277:   - Expanded: 100% width overlay
278: - Tablet (768-1024px):
279:   - Quarter: 320px fixed width
280:   - Half: 50% of viewport
281:   - Full: 100% of content area
282: - Desktop (>1024px):
283:   - Quarter: 25% of viewport (min 320px)
284:   - Half: 40% of viewport
285:   - Full: 50% of viewport
286:   - Icon: 48px floating button
287: 
288: ### Content Area Spacing
289: - Vertical spacing between sections: 2rem
290: - Content padding:
291:   - Mobile: 1rem
292:   - Tablet: 1.5rem
293:   - Desktop: 2rem
294: - Maximum content width: 1920px
295: 
296: ### Layout Size Configurations
297: 
298: #### Desktop (>1024px)
299: | Layout Mode | Main Content | Right Panel | Description |
300: |------------|--------------|-------------|-------------|
301: | Full Screen | 100% - 320px | Hidden | Main content maximized |
302: | With Quarter Panel | 75% | 25% (320px min) | Balanced with small panel |
303: | With Half Panel | 60% | 40% | Equal emphasis |
304: | With Full Panel | 50% | 50% | Split screen |
305: | Icon Mode | 100% - 48px | 48px | Maximum content with quick access |
306: 
307: #### Tablet (768px - 1024px)
308: | Layout Mode | Main Content | Right Panel | Description |
309: |------------|--------------|-------------|-------------|
310: | Full Screen | 100% | Hidden | Full content view |
311: | With Quarter Panel | 100% - 320px | 320px | Fixed panel width |
312: | With Half Panel | 50% | 50% | Equal split |
313: | With Full Panel | 0% | 100% | Panel overlay |
314: | Icon Mode | 100% - 48px | 48px | Content with access button |
315: 
316: #### Mobile (<768px)
317: | Layout Mode | Main Content | Right Panel | Description |
318: |------------|--------------|-------------|-------------|
319: | Full Screen | 100% | Hidden | Full content view |
320: | With Panel Open | 0% | 100% | Full overlay panel |
321: | Icon Mode | 100% - 48px | 48px | Content with floating button |
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/tailwind-4.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: "Tailwind CSS v4 Guidelines"
  3: description: "Guidelines for using Tailwind CSS v4 in ONE framework"
  4: tags: ["tailwind", "css", "v4", "guidelines", "system-design"]
  5: date: 2024-02-03
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: # Tailwind CSS v4 Guidelines
  9: 
 10: ## Key Changes from v3
 11: 
 12: ### 1. Import Syntax
 13: ```css
 14: /* ❌ Don't use v3 directives */
 15: @tailwind base;
 16: @tailwind components;
 17: @tailwind utilities;
 18: 
 19: /* ✅ Use v4 import */
 20: @import "tailwindcss";
 21: ```
 22: 
 23: ### 2. Updated Utility Names
 24: - `shadow-sm` → `shadow-xs`
 25: - `shadow` → `shadow-sm`
 26: - `rounded-sm` → `rounded-xs`
 27: - `rounded` → `rounded-sm`
 28: - `outline-none` → `outline-hidden`
 29: - `ring` → `ring-3`
 30: 
 31: ### 3. Default Changes
 32: - Border colors now use `currentColor` by default (add explicit colors)
 33: - Ring width is now 1px (use `ring-3` for v3 equivalent)
 34: - Placeholder text uses current text color at 50% opacity
 35: 
 36: ## Best Practices
 37: 
 38: ### 1. Border Usage
 39: ```tsx
 40: /* ❌ Don't rely on default border color */
 41: <div class="border">
 42: 
 43: /* ✅ Explicitly specify border color */
 44: <div class="border border-gray-200">
 45: ```
 46: 
 47: ### 2. Ring Usage
 48: ```tsx
 49: /* ❌ Don't use v3 ring style */
 50: <button class="focus:ring">
 51: 
 52: /* ✅ Use explicit width and color */
 53: <button class="focus:ring-3 ring-blue-500">
 54: ```
 55: 
 56: ### 3. Gradient Variants
 57: ```tsx
 58: /* ✅ Use via-none to reset middle color */
 59: <div class="bg-gradient-to-r from-red-500 via-orange-400 to-yellow-400 dark:via-none dark:from-blue-500 dark:to-teal-400">
 60: ```
 61: 
 62: ### 4. Variable Usage
 63: ```tsx
 64: /* ❌ Don't use v3 variable syntax */
 65: <div class="bg-[--brand-color]">
 66: 
 67: /* ✅ Use v4 variable syntax */
 68: <div class="bg-(--brand-color)">
 69: ```
 70: 
 71: ## Component Development
 72: 
 73: ### 1. Custom Utilities
 74: ```css
 75: /* ✅ Use @utility for custom utilities */
 76: @utility custom-class {
 77:   property: value;
 78: }
 79: ```
 80: 
 81: ### 2. Container Customization
 82: ```css
 83: /* ✅ Use @utility for container customization */
 84: @utility container {
 85:   margin-inline: auto;
 86:   padding-inline: 2rem;
 87: }
 88: ```
 89: 
 90: ### 3. Variant Stacking
 91: ```tsx
 92: /* ❌ Don't use v3 variant order */
 93: <ul class="py-4 first:*:pt-0 last:*:pb-0">
 94: 
 95: /* ✅ Use v4 left-to-right variant order */
 96: <ul class="py-4 *:first:pt-0 *:last:pb-0">
 97: ```
 98: 
 99: ## Performance Considerations
100: 
101: ### 1. Hover on Mobile
102: - Hover styles only apply on devices that support hover
103: - Don't rely on hover for critical functionality
104: - Use `@custom-variant hover` if needed for legacy behavior
105: 
106: ### 2. Transitions
107: ```tsx
108: /* ✅ Set outline colors explicitly when transitioning */
109: <button class="outline-cyan-500 transition hover:outline-2">
110: ```
111: 
112: ## Theme Configuration
113: 
114: ### 1. CSS Variables
115: ```css
116: /* ✅ Use CSS variables for theme values */
117: .my-class {
118:   background-color: var(--color-red-500);
119: }
120: ```
121: 
122: ### 2. Media Queries
123: ```css
124: /* ✅ Use variable names in theme() function */
125: @media (width >= theme(--breakpoint-xl)) {
126:   /* styles */
127: }
128: ```
129: 
130: ## Migration Tips
131: 
132: 1. Use explicit color values for borders and rings
133: 2. Update utility class names to v4 equivalents
134: 3. Review and update gradient implementations
135: 4. Check hover interactions on mobile devices
136: 5. Update variable syntax in arbitrary values
137: 6. Review and update variant stacking order
138: 
139: Remember: Tailwind CSS v4 focuses on improved performance, better defaults, and more consistent behavior. Always use explicit values and modern syntax for best results.
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/theme.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Theme System Documentation
  3: description: A comprehensive guide to ONE's theme system, animations, and styling
  4: date: 2024-02-20
  5: section: Design System
  6: order: 1
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Theme System Documentation
 10: 
 11: The ONE theme system provides three themes:
 12: - ONE (base/default theme)
 13: - Light (light variation)
 14: - Dark (dark variation)
 15: 
 16: ## Theme Configuration
 17: 
 18: ### Base Theme (ONE)
 19: Themes are defined using CSS custom properties with HSL color values. The ONE theme serves as the base, with light and dark variations building on top of it.
 20: 
 21: ## Animation System
 22: 
 23: The theme system includes a rich set of animations that can be used across the application:
 24: 
 25: ### Base Animations
 26: - `accordion-down/up`: Smooth accordion transitions
 27: - `orbit`: Circular orbital motion
 28: - `pulse`: Gentle pulsing effect
 29: - `border-beam`: Animated border effect
 30: - `spin`: Rotation animation
 31: - `thinking-dot`: Loading indicator animation
 32: - `ping`: Expanding ripple effect
 33: - `fade-in`: Smooth fade in transition
 34: 
 35: ### Usage Examples
 36: 
 37: ```jsx
 38: // Accordion animation
 39: <div className="animate-accordion-down">
 40:   {/* Accordion content */}
 41: }
 42: 
 43: // Orbital effect
 44: <div className="animate-orbit" style={{"--duration": "10", "--start-angle": "0", "--radius": "50"}}>
 45:   {/* Orbiting element */}
 46: }
 47: 
 48: // Loading indicator
 49: <div className="animate-thinking-dot">
 50:   {/* Loading dot */}
 51: }
 52: 
 53: // Smooth entrance
 54: <div className="animate-fade-in">
 55:   {/* Content that fades in */}
 56: }
 57: ```
 58: 
 59: ## Theme Integration
 60: 
 61: ### Base Theme (ONE)
 62: ```css
 63: :root {
 64:   /* Base ONE theme variables */
 65:   --one-background: 0 0% 100%;
 66:   --one-foreground: 240 10% 10%;
 67:   --one-primary: 240 5.9% 10%;
 68:   --one-primary-foreground: 0 0% 98%;
 69: }
 70: ```
 71: 
 72: ### Theme Variations
 73: ```css
 74: /* Light theme variation */
 75: .light {
 76:   --background: 0 0% 100%;
 77:   --foreground: 240 10% 10%;
 78: }
 79: 
 80: /* Dark theme variation */
 81: .dark {
 82:   --background: 0 0% 7%;
 83:   --foreground: 0 0% 98%;
 84: }
 85: ```
 86: 
 87: ## Best Practices
 88: 
 89: 1. Use semantic color tokens from the ONE theme
 90: 2. Leverage the animation system for interactive elements
 91: 3. Maintain consistent timing with animation variables
 92: 4. Consider reduced motion preferences
 93: 5. Test animations across themes
 94: 6. Use responsive design utilities
 95: 7. Follow accessibility guidelines
 96: 
 97: ## Examples
 98: 
 99: ### Animated Card with Theme Support
100: ```jsx
101: <div className="bg-card text-card-foreground animate-fade-in">
102:   <div className="p-4">
103:     <h3 className="text-lg font-semibold">Card Title</h3>
104:     <p className="text-muted-foreground">
105:       Card content with theme-aware colors
106:     </p>
107:   </div>
108: </div>
109: ```
110: 
111: ### Interactive Button
112: ```jsx
113: <button className="bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:animate-pulse">
114:   Click Me
115: </button>
116: ```
117: 
118: ## Resources
119: 
120: - [Tailwind CSS Documentation](https://tailwindcss.com/docs)
121: - [shadcn/ui Themes](https://ui.shadcn.com/themes)
122: - [Framer Motion](https://www.framer.com/motion/) - For more complex animations
123: - [WCAG Animation Guidelines](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/animation-from-interactions)
`````
