  8: 
  9: # Chat System Architecture
 10: 
 11: ONE's chat system combines Astro's performance, React's interactivity, and advanced AI capabilities to deliver a powerful, flexible chat interface. This guide covers the complete architecture and implementation details.
 12: 
 13: ## Core Components
 14: 
 15: ### 1. Chat Component
 16: 
 17: The main chat interface (`src/components/Chat.tsx`):
 18: 
 19: ```typescript
 20: interface ChatProps {
 21:   chatConfig?: ChatConfig;
 22:   content?: string;
 23:   className?: string;
 24: }
 25: 
 26: export function Chat({ chatConfig, content, className }: ChatProps) {
 27:   // Component implementation
 28:   const { messages, input, handleSubmit } = useChat({
 29:     api: chatConfig?.api || "/api/chat",
 30:     body: {
 31:       config: chatConfig,
 32:       content: content
 33:     }
 34:   });
 35:   
 36:   // Render chat interface
 37:   return (
 38:     <div className="chat-container">
 39:       <MessageList messages={messages} />
 40:       <ChatInput onSubmit={handleSubmit} />
 41:     </div>
 42:   );
 43: }
 44: ```
 45: 
 46: ### 2. Layout System
 47: 
 48: Flexible display modes for different use cases:
 49: 
 50: ```typescript
 51: type PanelMode = "quarter" | "half" | "full" | "floating" | "icon" | "hidden";
 52: 
 53: interface LayoutProps {
 54:   title: string;
 55:   description?: string;
 56:   rightPanelMode?: PanelMode;
 57:   chatConfig?: ChatConfig;
 58:   content?: string;
 59: }
 60: ```
 61: 
 62: #### Panel Modes
 63: - **quarter**: 25% width side panel (default)
 64: - **half**: 50% width side panel
 65: - **full**: Full screen interface
 66: - **floating**: Detached window
 67: - **icon**: Minimized button
 68: - **hidden**: No chat interface

`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Frequently Asked Questions

  8: 
  9: # FAQ
 10: 
 11: Comprehensive answers to common questions about developing with ONE.
 12: 
 13: ## Getting Started
 14: 
 15: ### Q: What are the system requirements?
 16: **A:** You need:
 17: - Node.js 18 or higher
 18: - pnpm package manager
 19: - OpenAI API key (or other supported providers)
 20: - Git for version control
 21: - Basic knowledge of Astro and React
 22: 
 23: ### Q: How do I get started quickly?
 24: **A:** Use these commands:
 25: ```bash
 26: # Clone repository
 27: git clone https://github.com/one-ie/one.git
 28: 
 29: # Install dependencies
 30: cd one
 31: pnpm install
 32: 
 33: # Start development
 34: pnpm dev
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: ### Q: How do I configure my AI provider?
 38: **A:** Create a `.env` file:
 39: ```env
 40: OPENAI_API_KEY=your_key_here
 41: OPENAI_ORG_ID=optional_org_id
 42: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_key_here
 43: MISTRAL_API_KEY=your_key_here
 44: ```
 45: 
 46: ## AI Features
 47: 
 48: ### Q: Which AI providers are supported?
 49: **A:** ONE supports multiple providers:
 50: ```typescript
 51: const providers = {
 52:   openai: {
 53:     models: ['gpt-4o-mini', 'gpt-4'],
 54:     features: ['streaming', 'functions']
 55:   },
 56:   anthropic: {
 57:     models: ['claude-2', 'claude-instant'],
 58:     features: ['streaming']
 59:   },
 60:   mistral: {
 61:     models: ['mistral-large'],
 62:     features: ['streaming']
 63:   }
 64: };
 65: ```
 66: 
 67: ### Q: How do I optimize AI responses?
 68: **A:** Configure these parameters:
 69: ```typescript
 70: const chatConfig = {
 71:   // Response Quality
 72:   temperature: 0.7,    // 0.1-1.0: lower = more focused
 73:   maxTokens: 2000,     // Adjust for response length
 74:   topP: 0.9,          // Nucleus sampling
 75:   
 76:   // Performance
 77:   streaming: true,     // Enable streaming
 78:   cache: true,        // Enable caching
 79:   
 80:   // Context
 81:   systemPrompt: "Be concise and clear",
 82:   contextWindow: 4000  // Maximum context size
 83: };
 84: ```
 85: 
 86: ### Q: How do I handle streaming responses?
 87: **A:** Use the streaming configuration:
 88: ```typescript
 89: const config = {
 90:   streaming: {
 91:     enabled: true,
 92:     chunkSize: 100,
 93:     maxDuration: 30,
 94:     retryOnError: true,
 95:     onProgress: (chunk) => {
 96:       // Handle chunks
 97:     }
 98:   }
 99: };
100: ```
101: 
102: ## Chat Integration
103: 
104: ### Q: How do I add chat to any page?
105: **A:** Use the Layout component:
106: ```astro
107: ---
108: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
109: 
110: const chatConfig = {
111:   provider: "openai",
112:   model: "gpt-4o-mini",
113:   systemPrompt: [{
114:     type: "text",
115:     text: "You are a helpful assistant."
116:   }],
117:   welcome: {
118:     message: "👋 How can I help?",
119:     suggestions: [
120:       { label: "🚀 Start", prompt: "Help me get started" }
121:     ]
122:   }
123: };
124: ---
125: 
126: <Layout
127:   title="Your Page"
128:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
129:   rightPanelMode="quarter"
130: >
131:   <main>Your content here</main>
132: </Layout>
133: ```
134: 
135: ### Q: What chat panel modes are available?
136: **A:** Several modes for different use cases:
137: ```typescript
138: type PanelMode = 
139:   | "quarter"   // 25% width (default)
140:   | "half"      // 50% width
141:   | "full"      // Full screen
142:   | "floating"  // Detached window
143:   | "icon"      // Minimized button
144:   | "hidden";   // No chat interface
145: ```
146: 
147: ### Q: How do I customize the chat interface?
148: **A:** Use the theme system:
149: ```typescript
150: const chatTheme = {
151:   // Colors
152:   colors: {
153:     primary: "blue",
154:     accent: "indigo",
155:     background: "zinc"
156:   },
157:   
158:   // Layout
159:   layout: {
160:     spacing: "comfortable",
161:     width: "default",
162:     radius: "medium"
163:   },
164:   
165:   // Typography
166:   font: {
167:     family: "inter",
168:     size: "base",
169:     weight: "normal"
170:   }
171: };
172: ```
173: 
174: ## Content Management
175: 
176: ### Q: How do I structure content collections?
177: **A:** Organize in `src/content`:
178: ```
179: src/content/
180: ├── docs/          # Documentation
181: ├── blog/          # Blog posts
182: ├── courses/       # Course content
183: └── prompts/       # AI prompts
184: ```
185: 
186: ### Q: How do I add AI to markdown content?
187: **A:** Use frontmatter configuration:
188: ```markdown
189: ---
190: title: Your Page
191: layout: ../layouts/Chat.astro
192: aiConfig:
193:   systemPrompt: "You are an expert on this topic"
194:   suggestions:
195:     - label: "Overview"
196:       prompt: "Give me an overview"
197: ---
198: 
199: Your content here...
200: ```
201: ### Q: How do I implement caching?
202: **A:** Configure caching strategy:
203: ```typescript
204: const cacheConfig = {
205:   enabled: true,
206:   duration: 3600,
207:   strategy: "stale-while-revalidate",
208:   revalidate: true
209: };
210: ```
211: ## Troubleshooting
212: 
213: ### Q: How do I debug AI responses?
214: **A:** Use debug mode:
215: ```typescript
216: const debugConfig = {
217:   debug: true,
218:   logging: {
219:     level: "verbose",
220:     requests: true,
221:     responses: true,
222:     timing: true
223:   }
224: };
225: ```
226: 
227: ### Q: How do I handle errors?
228: **A:** Implement error handling:
229: ```typescript
230: try {
231:   const response = await ai.chat({
232:     messages: messages,
233:     onError: (error) => {
234:       if (error.type === "rate_limit") {
235:         // Handle rate limiting
236:       } else if (error.type === "context_length") {
237:         // Handle context overflow
238:       }
239:     }
240:   });
241: } catch (error) {
242:   // Fallback handling
243: }
244: ```
245: ### Q: How do I contribute?
246: **A:** Follow these steps:
247: 1. Fork the repository
248: 2. Create a feature branch
249: 3. Make changes
250: 4. Submit pull request
251: 5. Follow contribution guidelines
`````

`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Your First AI Agent
  3: description: Create and deploy your first intelligent AI agent with ONE
  4: date: 2024-02-02

  8: 
  9: # Creating Your First AI Agent
 10: 
 11: Build a powerful, context-aware AI agent in minutes. This guide walks you through creating a custom assistant that can understand your content, help users, and integrate seamlessly with your application.
 12: 
 13: ## Prerequisites
 14: 
 15: - Completed the [installation guide](/docs/getting-started/installation)
 16: - Basic understanding of Astro and React
 17: - OpenAI API key (or other supported provider)
 18: - Node.js 18+
 19: 
 20: ## Quick Start
 21: 
 22: Create a new file `src/pages/my-agent.astro`:
 23: 
 24: ```astro
 25: ---
 26: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
 27: import { ChatConfigSchema } from '../schema/chat';
 28: 
 29: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
 30:   // Core AI Settings
 31:   provider: "openai",
 32:   model: "gpt-4o-mini",
 33:   temperature: 0.7,
 34:   maxTokens: 2000,
 35:   
 36:   // Agent Definition
 37:   systemPrompt: [{
 38:     type: "text",
 39:     text: "You are an AI assistant specialized in helping users with this application."
 40:   }],
 41:   
 42:   // User Interface
 43:   welcome: {
 44:     message: "👋 Hello! I'm here to help you get the most out of our application.",
 45:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
 46:     suggestions: [
 47:       {
 48:         label: "🚀 Quick Start",
 49:         prompt: "Show me how to get started"
 50:       },
 51:       {
 52:         label: "💡 Features",
 53:         prompt: "What can this application do?"
 54:       }
 55:     ]
 56:   },
 57:   
 58:   // Advanced Features
 59:   runtime: "edge",
 60:   streaming: true,
 61:   includeContent: true
 62: });
 63: ---
 64: 
 65: <Layout
 66:   title="AI Assistant"
 67:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
 68:   rightPanelMode="quarter"
 69: >
 70:   <main class="max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 py-8">
 71:     <h1 class="text-3xl font-bold mb-6">
 72:       Welcome to My Application
 73:     </h1>
 74:     <p class="text-lg text-muted-foreground">
 75:       Our AI assistant is ready to help you. Try asking about features, 
 76:       getting started, or any questions you have.
 77:     </p>
 78:   </main>
 79: </Layout>
 80: ```
 81: 
 82: ## Advanced Configuration
 83: 
 84: ### 1. Agent Personality
 85: 
 86: Define a detailed personality and capabilities:
 87: 
 88: ```typescript
 89: const agentConfig = {
 90:   systemPrompt: [
 91:     // Core Role
 92:     {
 93:       type: "text",
 94:       text: `You are an expert AI assistant specialized in [domain].
 95:       Your personality traits:
 96:       - Professional yet friendly
 97:       - Clear and concise
 98:       - Patient and helpful
 99:       - Detail-oriented`
100:     },
101:     
102:     // Knowledge Areas
103:     {
104:       type: "text",
105:       text: `Your expertise covers:
106:       1. [Primary Area]
107:       2. [Secondary Area]
108:       3. [Additional Skills]`
109:     },
110:     
111:     // Interaction Guidelines
112:     {

116:       - Provide step-by-step guidance
117:       - Include relevant code examples
118:       - Reference documentation when appropriate`
119:     }
120:   ]
121: };

243:     - Ask clarifying questions
244:     - Provide clear instructions
245:     - Escalate when necessary`
246:   }],
247:   
248:   welcome: {
249:     message: "👋 I'm your support assistant. How can I help you today?",
250:     suggestions: [
251:       {
252:         label: "🔧 Troubleshoot",
253:         prompt: "I need help solving a problem"
254:       },
255:       {
256:         label: "📋 Common Issues",
257:         prompt: "Show me common issues and solutions"
258:       }
259:     ]
260:   }
261: };
262: ```
263: 
264: ## Best Practices
265: 
266: ### 1. Agent Design
267: 
268: - **Clear Purpose**: Define specific roles and responsibilities
269: - **Personality**: Create a consistent, appropriate tone
270: - **Knowledge Scope**: Set clear boundaries of expertise
271: - **Interaction Style**: Design natural, helpful dialogues
272: 
273: ### 2. Content Integration
274: 
275: - **Relevant Context**: Include only necessary information
276: - **Structured Data**: Organize content logically
277: - **Updated Knowledge**: Keep information current
278: - **Examples**: Provide practical use cases
279: 
280: ### 3. User Experience
281: 
282: - **Welcome Message**: Set clear expectations
283: - **Helpful Suggestions**: Guide users effectively
284: - **Response Format**: Maintain consistency
285: - **Error Handling**: Graceful fallbacks
286: 
287: ### 4. Performance
288: 
289: - **Edge Runtime**: Use for faster responses
290: - **Streaming**: Enable for better UX
291: - **Caching**: Implement when appropriate
292: - **Monitoring**: Track usage and errors
293: 
294: ## Troubleshooting
295: 
296: ### Common Issues
297: 
298: 1. **Response Quality**
299:    ```typescript
300:    // Improve response quality
301:    const config = {
302:      temperature: 0.7,    // Adjust for creativity vs precision
303:      maxTokens: 2000,     // Ensure sufficient length
304:      topP: 0.9           // Control response diversity
305:    };
306:    ```
307: 
308: 2. **Performance Issues**
309:    ```typescript
310:    // Optimize performance
311:    const config = {
312:      runtime: "edge",     // Use edge runtime
313:      streaming: true,     // Enable streaming
314:      cache: {            // Configure caching
315:        enabled: true,
316:        duration: 3600
317:      }
318:    };
319:    ```
320: 
321: 3. **Context Problems**
322:    ```typescript
323:    // Fix context issues
324:    const config = {
325:      includeContent: true,
326:      contentProcessing: {
327:        maxLength: 4000,    // Limit context size
328:        priority: "recent", // Prioritize recent content
329:        filter: "relevant"  // Filter by relevance
330:      }
331:    };
332:    ```
`````

## File: src/content/docs/get-started.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Getting Started with ONE
  3: description: Learn how to set up and start building with the ONE framework
  4: date: 2024-02-02
  5: section: Introduction
  6: order: 1
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Getting Started with ONE
 10: 
 11: ONE is a toolkit for building AI-powered applications, combining Astro's performance, React's interactivity, and advanced AI capabilities. This guide will help you get up and running quickly.
 12: 
 13: ## Quick Start
 14: 
 15: ### 1. Get the Project
 16: 
 17: Choose your preferred method to get started:
 18: 
 19: ```bash
 20: # Option 1: Clone the repository
 21: git clone https://github.com/one-ie/one.git
 22: 
 23: # Option 2: Download the ZIP file
 24: # Visit: https://github.com/one-ie/one/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
 25: 
 26: # Option 3: Open in GitHub Codespaces
 27: # Visit: https://github.com/codespaces/new?hide_repo_select=true&ref=main&repo=one-ie/one
 28: ```
 29: 
 30: ### 2. Install Dependencies
 31: 
 32: ONE uses pnpm for package management:
 33: 
 34: ```bash
 35: # Navigate to project directory
 36: cd one
 37: 
 38: # Install dependencies
 39: pnpm install
 40: ```
 41: 
 42: ### 3. Configure Environment
 43: 
 44: Create a `.env` file in your project root:
 45: 
 46: ```env
 47: # Required: OpenAI API key for AI features
 48: OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
 49: 
 50: # Optional: Override default AI settings
 51: AI_PROVIDER=openai
 52: AI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini
 53: AI_TEMPERATURE=0.7
 54: AI_MAX_TOKENS=2000
 55: ```
 56: 
 57: ### 4. Start Development
 58: 
 59: ```bash
 60: pnpm dev
 61: ```
 62: 
 63: Visit `http://localhost:4321` to see your application.
 64: 
 65: ## Project Structure
 66: 
 67: ```
 68: one/
 69: ├── src/
 70: │   ├── components/          # UI Components
 71: │   │   ├── ui/             # Shadcn/UI components
 72: │   │   ├── chat/           # Chat components
 73: │   │   └── magicui/        # Enhanced UI components
 74: │   │
 75: │   ├── content/            # Content Collections
 76: │   │   ├── blog/          # Blog posts
 77: │   │   ├── docs/          # Documentation
 78: │   │   └── prompts/       # AI prompts
 79: │   │
 80: │   ├── layouts/            # Page layouts
 81: │   ├── lib/               # Utility functions
 82: │   ├── pages/             # Routes and pages
 83: │   ├── schema/            # Data schemas
 84: │   └── styles/            # Global styles
 85: │
 86: └── public/                # Static assets
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ## Adding AI Chat to a Page
 90: 
 91: ### Basic Integration
 92: 
 93: Create a new page with AI chat capabilities:
 94: 
 95: ```astro
 96: ---
 97: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
 98: import { ChatConfigSchema } from '../schema/chat';
 99: 
100: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
101:   // AI Configuration
102:   provider: "openai",
103:   model: "gpt-4o-mini",
104:   temperature: 0.7,
105:   maxTokens: 2000,
106: 
107:   // System Instructions
108:   systemPrompt: [{
109:     type: "text",
110:     text: "You are a helpful AI assistant specialized in this topic."
111:   }],
112: 
113:   // User Interface
114:   welcome: {
115:     message: "👋 How can I help you today?",
116:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
117:     suggestions: [
118:       {
119:         label: "🚀 Quick Start",
120:         prompt: "Show me how to get started"
121:       }
122:     ]
123:   }
124: });
125: ---
126: 
127: <Layout 
128:   title="Your Page"
129:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
130:   rightPanelMode="quarter"
131: >
132:   <main>
133:     <h1>Your Content</h1>
134:     <!-- Page content here -->
135:   </main>
136: </Layout>
137: ```
138: 
139: ### Chat Panel Modes
140: 
141: Choose from multiple display modes:
142: 
143: - `quarter`: 25% width side panel (default)
144: - `half`: 50% width side panel
145: - `full`: Full screen chat interface
146: - `floating`: Detached floating window
147: - `icon`: Minimized chat button
148: - `hidden`: No chat interface
149: 
150: ```astro
151: <Layout
152:   rightPanelMode="quarter" // or "half", "full", "floating", "icon"
153: >
154:   <!-- Content -->
155: </Layout>
156: ```
157: 
158: ## Advanced Features
159: 
160: ### 1. Context-Aware AI
161: 
162: Make your AI assistant knowledgeable about page content:
163: 
164: ```typescript
165: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
166:   systemPrompt: [{
167:     type: "text",
168:     text: `You are an expert on this topic. The content below provides context for your responses:
169: 
170:     ${pageContent}`
171:   }],
172:   addSystemPrompt: true,
173:   addBusinessPrompt: true
174: });
175: ```
176: 
177: ### 2. Interactive Features
178: 
179: Enable advanced chat capabilities:
180: 
181: ```typescript
182: const chatConfig = {
183:   // Streaming responses
184:   runtime: "edge",
185:   
186:   // Message features
187:   features: {
188:     textToSpeech: true,    // Voice synthesis
189:     codeHighlight: true,   // Code syntax highlighting
190:     markdown: true,        // Rich text formatting
191:     suggestions: true      // Quick action buttons
192:   }
193: };
194: ```
195: 
196: ### 3. Custom Styling
197: 
198: Customize appearance using Tailwind CSS and Shadcn UI:
199: 
200: ```css
201: /* src/styles/global.css */
202: @tailwind base;
203: @tailwind components;
204: @tailwind utilities;
205: 
206: /* Theme customization */
207: :root {
208:   --primary: 210 100% 50%;
209:   --secondary: 220 100% 60%;
210: }
211: ```
212: 
213: ## Troubleshooting
214: 
215: ### Common Issues
216: 
217: 1. **API Configuration**
218:    - Verify OPENAI_API_KEY in .env
219:    - Check API endpoint configuration
220:    - Monitor rate limits and quotas
221: 
222: 2. **Build Problems**
223:    - Run `pnpm clean && pnpm install`
224:    - Update Node.js to v18+
225:    - Clear browser cache
226: 
227: 3. **Chat Issues**
228:    - Check browser console for errors
229:    - Verify network connectivity
230:    - Monitor streaming response status
231: 
232: ## Getting Help
233: 
234: Need assistance? Try these resources:
235: 
236: - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/one-ie/one/issues)
237: - Email: support@one.ie
238: 
239: For additional guidance, check our [FAQ](/docs/faq) and [Troubleshooting Guide](/docs/troubleshooting/common-issues).
`````

## File: src/content/docs/markdown-ai.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Markdown with AI
  3: description: How to create AI-powered markdown pages
  4: date: 2024-02-02
  5: section: Tutorials
  6: order: 4
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Creating AI-Powered Markdown Pages
 10: 
 11: ONE framework makes it easy to create AI-powered markdown pages where the AI assistant has access to the content of the page. This guide explains how to set up markdown files with AI chat capabilities.
 12: 
 13: ## Basic Setup
 14: 
 15: To create an AI-powered markdown page, you need to:
 16: 
 17: 1. Create a markdown file with frontmatter configuration
 18: 2. Use the `Text.astro` layout
 19: 3. Write your content in markdown format
 20: 
 21: Here's a simple example:
 22: 
 23: ```markdown
 24: ---
 25: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
 26: title: My AI-Powered Page
 27: description: A page with AI chat capabilities
 28: aiProvider: mistral
 29: aiModel: mistral-large-latest
 30: systemPrompt: You are a helpful assistant that explains the content of this page.
 31: welcomeMessage: 👋 Hello! I can help explain the content on this page.
 32: avatar: /icon.svg
 33: suggestions:
 34:   - Explain this page
 35:   - What are the key points?
 36:   - How can I implement this?
 37: ---
 38: 
 39: # My Content
 40: 
 41: This is the content of my page. The AI assistant will have access to this content
 42: and can answer questions about it.
 43: 
 44: ## Key Points
 45: 
 46: - Point 1
 47: - Point 2
 48: - Point 3
 49: ```
 50: 
 51: ## How It Works
 52: 
 53: When you create a markdown page with the `Text.astro` layout:
 54: 
 55: 1. The frontmatter is extracted and normalized into a valid chat configuration
 56: 2. The content of the markdown file is extracted
 57: 3. Both are passed to the Chat component
 58: 4. The content is sent to the LLM as context, allowing the AI to reference the information
 59: 
 60: This creates a seamless experience where the AI can answer questions about the content of the page.
 61: 
 62: ## Configuration Options
 63: 
 64: ### Core AI Settings
 65: 
 66: | Property | Description | Example |
 67: |----------|-------------|---------|
 68: | `aiProvider` | AI provider to use | `mistral`, `openai`, `anthropic` |
 69: | `aiModel` | Specific model to use | `mistral-large-latest`, `gpt-4o-mini` |
 70: | `temperature` | Response randomness (0-1) | `0.7` |
 71: | `maxTokens` | Maximum response length | `2000` |
 72: 
 73: ### System Prompt
 74: 
 75: The system prompt defines your AI assistant's personality and behavior:
 76: 
 77: ```yaml
 78: systemPrompt: You are a helpful assistant that explains the content of this page.
 79: ```
 80: 
 81: ### Welcome Message and Suggestions
 82: 
 83: Configure the initial appearance and behavior:
 84: 
 85: ```yaml
 86: welcomeMessage: 👋 Hello! I can help explain the content on this page.
 87: avatar: /icon.svg
 88: suggestions:
 89:   - Explain this page
 90:   - What are the key points?
 91:   - How can I implement this?
 92: ```
 93: 
 94: ### Content Settings
 95: 
 96: Control how the content is used:
 97: 
 98: ```yaml
 99: includeContent: true  # Whether to include the content in the prompt
100: contentPrefix: "### Reference Content:"  # Prefix for the content in the prompt
101: ```
102: 
103: ## Advanced Usage
104: 
105: ### Rich Suggestions
106: 
107: You can use rich suggestions with different labels and prompts:
108: 
109: ```yaml
110: suggestions:
111:   - label: "📚 Explain Concepts"
112:     prompt: "Can you explain the key concepts on this page?"
113:   - label: "🔍 Implementation Details"
114:     prompt: "How do I implement this in my project?"
115:   - label: "🚀 Best Practices"
116:     prompt: "What are the best practices for this approach?"
117: ```
118: 
119: ### Metadata
120: 
121: Add metadata for SEO and organization:
122: 
123: ```yaml
124: title: My AI-Powered Page
125: description: A page with AI chat capabilities
126: keywords:
127:   - ai
128:   - markdown
129:   - tutorial
130: categories:
131:   - Tutorials
132:   - Getting Started
133: ```
134: 
135: ## Implementation Examples
136: 
137: ### Documentation Page
138: 
139: ```markdown
140: ---
141: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
142: title: API Documentation
143: description: Comprehensive API documentation
144: aiProvider: mistral
145: aiModel: mistral-large-latest
146: systemPrompt: You are a technical documentation assistant. You help users understand the API described on this page.
147: welcomeMessage: 👋 Need help with our API? I can explain endpoints, parameters, and provide examples.
148: suggestions:
149:   - How do I authenticate?
150:   - Explain the endpoints
151:   - Show me an example request
152: ---
153: 
154: # API Documentation
155: 
156: ## Authentication
157: 
158: To authenticate with the API, you need to...
159: ```
160: 
161: ### Tutorial Page
162: 
163: ```markdown
164: ---
165: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
166: title: Getting Started Tutorial
167: description: Learn how to get started with our framework
168: aiProvider: openai
169: aiModel: gpt-4o-mini
170: temperature: 0.4
171: systemPrompt: You are a helpful tutorial guide. You help users understand the tutorial on this page and answer their questions about implementation details.
172: welcomeMessage: 👋 I'm here to help you with this tutorial. What would you like to know?
173: suggestions:
174:   - label: "🚀 Prerequisites"
175:     prompt: "What are the prerequisites for this tutorial?"
176:   - label: "⚙️ Installation"
177:     prompt: "Can you explain the installation process?"
178:   - label: "📝 Step-by-Step"
179:     prompt: "Walk me through the steps in this tutorial"
180: ---
181: 
182: # Getting Started
183: 
184: This tutorial will guide you through setting up our framework...
185: ```
186: 
187: ## Best Practices
188: 
189: 1. **Be Specific in System Prompts**: Clearly define your assistant's role and how it should interact with the content.
190: 
191: 2. **Provide Helpful Suggestions**: Offer 3-5 relevant suggestions to guide users in interacting with the content.
192: 
193: 3. **Structure Content Clearly**: Use clear headings, lists, and code blocks to make it easier for the AI to reference specific parts.
194: 
195: 4. **Include Examples**: Provide examples in your content that the AI can reference when answering questions.
196: 
197: 5. **Test Different Configurations**: Experiment with different temperature settings and models to find the optimal balance for your content.
198: 
199: 6. **Consider Content Length**: Very long content may be truncated. Focus on the most important information.
200: 
201: 7. **Update Regularly**: Keep your content up-to-date to ensure the AI provides accurate information.
202: 
203: ## Troubleshooting
204: 
205: ### Common Issues
206: 
207: 1. **AI Doesn't Reference Content**: Ensure `includeContent` is set to `true` and check that your content is not too long.
208: 
209: 2. **Incorrect Responses**: Try lowering the temperature for more factual responses.
210: 
211: 3. **Suggestions Not Working**: Make sure your suggestions are properly formatted in the frontmatter.
212: 
213: 4. **Layout Issues**: Verify that you're using the correct layout path in your frontmatter.
214: 
215: 5. **Content Not Rendering**: Check for syntax errors in your markdown.
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/-SystemPrompt Gemini.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: Agent ONE System Prompt
 3: description: Lets upgrade our system to use content collectionsn
 4: tags:
 5:   - elevate
 6:   - system-prompt
 7:   - deep-research
 8:   - foundation
 9: date: 2024-02-03
10: ---
11: 
12: **SYSTEM PROMPT: Elevate Foundation Synthesis via Gemini Deep Research**
13: 
14: **(Instructions for User:** Initiate this prompt within the Gemini interface, ideally selecting the "Deep Research" mode or ensuring it's enabled, potentially using Gemini 2.5 Pro (Experimental) via Advanced if available for maximum capability. Replace placeholders with your target company details.)*
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: **SYSTEM PROMPT START**
19: 
20: **I am using Gemini Deep Research.** My goal is to perform **deep foundational research** for the e-commerce business detailed below, structuring the findings according to the **Elevate Ecommerce Framework's FOUNDATION** stage (Company Context, Market Awareness, Customer Avatar Clues).
21: 
22: Act as **Agent ONE**, an expert AI Brand Strategist and Market Analyst integrated with deep research capabilities. Your objective is to **autonomously research the provided company's online presence and synthesize a comprehensive Strategic Blueprint** based on your findings.
23: 
24: **Target Company for Research:**
25: 
26: *   **Company Name:** `[Insert Company Name]`
27: *   **Primary Website URL:** `[Insert Main Website URL]`
28: *   **(Optional) Key Social Media URLs:**
29:     *   LinkedIn: `[Fill in all social Insert URL or state no]`
30:     *   Instagram: `[Insert URL or state N/A]`
31:     *   Facebook: `[Insert URL or state N/A]`
32:     *   Twitter/X: `[Insert URL or state N/A]`
33:     *   Other Relevant: `[Insert URL or state N/A]`
34: *   **(Optional) Key Competitor URLs (for comparative context - limit to 1-2):**
35:     *   Competitor 1 URL: `[Insert URL or state N/A]`
36:     *   Competitor 2 URL: `[Insert URL or state N/A]`
37: 
38: **Deep Research Plan & Execution:**
39: 
40: Leverage your Deep Research capabilities to execute the following plan:
41: 
42: 1.  **Prioritized Website Analysis:**
43:     *   Thoroughly browse the primary website URL (`[Insert Main Website URL]`).
44:     *   Focus data extraction and analysis on: Homepage (Core message, value prop, tone), About Us (Mission, vision, story, values), Main Product/Service Pages (Offerings, descriptions, benefits highlighted), Blog/Content Hub (Recurring themes, expertise signals), Contact/Support pages (Accessibility, tone).
45:     *   Identify core offerings, explicit or implicit value propositions, hints of unique mechanisms, overall brand voice/tone, stated mission/values, and target audience indicators based *only* on website content.
46: 2.  **Social Media Presence Analysis:**
47:     *   Analyze the provided key social media profiles.
48:     *   Extract profile bios/descriptions.
49:     *   Identify recurring content themes, communication style, engagement patterns (if observable), and visual identity cues from recent activity (e.g., last ~20 posts/updates). Determine if the tone differs from the website.
50: 3.  **(Optional) Competitor Snapshot:**
51:     *   Briefly analyze the provided competitor URLs (if any).
52:     *   Extract their primary homepage headline/slogan and core stated value proposition.
53:     *   Note any immediate, obvious points of difference in messaging or positioning compared to the target company.
54: 4.  **Synthesize & Reason:**
55:     *   *Use your reasoning capabilities* to connect findings across the website and social channels.
56:     *   Identify potential inconsistencies or strong points of coherence in branding and messaging.
57:     *   Infer market positioning (Premium/Mid/Value) based on language, design cues described (or pricing if visible), and competitor comparison (if applicable).
58:     *   Deduce the likely Customer Avatar profile (pains, goals, demographics/psychographics) based *purely* on who the company's content appears to be addressing and the problems/aspirations it focuses on.
59: 
60: **Required Output Structure (Final Report):**
61: 
62: Generate a comprehensive report structured precisely according to the Elevate Foundation pillars, using Markdown headings. Base findings *strictly* on the information gathered during your deep research process. If data for a point is scarce or couldn't be reliably found, state that clearly.
63: 
64: *   **I. Company Context Synthesis:**
65:     *   **Core Offerings:** (What products/services are central?)
66:     *   **Primary Value Proposition:** (What core benefit/transformation is promised?)
67:     *   **Unique Mechanism Clues:** (Hints at *how* they deliver value differently?)
68:     *   **Brand Voice & Tone:** (List 3-5 descriptive adjectives based on language used.)
69:     *   **Mission/Vision/Values:** (Explicitly stated or strongly implied?)
70:     *   **Brand Personality/Archetype:** (Overall vibe/character projected?)
71: *   **II. Market Awareness Signals:**
72:     *   **Market Positioning:** (Inferred Premium/Mid/Value? Provide reasoning.)
73:     *   **Key Messaging Themes:** (Recurring topics across website/social.)
74:     *   **Points of Differentiation (Observed):** (How do they message differently from the optional competitors analyzed?)
75: *   **III. Inferred Customer Avatar Clues:**
76:     *   **Likely Target Audience:** (Who does their content speak to? Demographics, role, mindset.)
77:     *   **Customer Pains Addressed:** (What problems does their content focus on solving?)
78:     *   **Customer Goals Appealed To:** (What aspirations does their messaging target?)
79: 
80: **Execution:**
81: Initiate the Deep Research process based on this plan and target information. Provide the final structured report upon completion. I understand this may take several minutes and involves multiple steps of planning, searching, reasoning, and synthesis on your part.
82: 
83: **SYSTEM PROMPT END**
84: 
85: ---
86: 
87: **How This Prompt Leverages Deep Research:**
88: 
89: *   **Explicit Invocation:** It clearly states "I am using Gemini Deep Research."
90: *   **Clear Objective:** The goal is foundational research structured by the Elevate Framework.
91: *   **Agentic Instruction:** It tells the AI *what* to research (specific URLs/sections) and *how* to use its capabilities (browse, analyze, synthesize, reason).
92: *   **Structured Plan:** It breaks down the complex research task into logical phases (Website, Social, Competitor, Synthesis).
93: *   **Defined Output:** It mandates a specific report structure aligned with the Foundation Grids.
94: *   **Acknowledges Process:** It notes the user understands this is a complex, multi-step task for the AI.
95: 
96: This prompt gives Gemini Deep Research a clear mandate and structure to autonomously perform the foundational research required, leveraging its unique capabilities to deliver a highly valuable Strategic Blueprint draft for the user.
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/-SystemPrompt.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: "Astro Image Guide"
  3: description: "A comprehensive guide to handling images in Astro, including local and remote images, optimization, and responsive image components"
  4: tags: ["astro", "images", "optimization", "responsive", "web-performance", "assets", "picture", "webp", "avif"]
  5: date: 2024-02-03
  6: ---
  7: The goal is to allow the AI to operate in two primary modes:
  8: 
  9: 1.  **Mode 1 (Foundation Provided):** The user supplies the Foundation Blueprint, and the AI uses it to execute tasks (like the original MASTER prompt).
 10: 2.  **Mode 2 (Foundation Generation):** The user provides target URLs, and the AI attempts to *generate* the Foundation Blueprint using analysis (like the CONCEPTUAL prompt), which can then be used for subsequent tasks.
 11: 
 12: Here is the  System Prompt:
 13: 
 14: ---
 15: ** SYSTEM PROMPT START**
 16: 
 17: You are **Agent ONE**, an expert AI assistant specialized in accelerating e-commerce growth, skilled in both strategic analysis (using web data) and tactical execution based on established strategy. Your primary function is to assist me, the user (an Ecom Owner/Manager), in executing specific marketing and strategy tasks by leveraging the **9-Step Elevate Ecommerce Framework**, starting with establishing a robust Foundation.
 18: 
 19: Your overarching goal is to help me generate high-quality, strategically sound, and actionable outputs (strategies, knowledge summaries, content drafts, foundational analysis) that contribute to systematically Attracting, Converting, and Growing my customer base.
 20: 
 21: **Core Operational Framework:**
 22: 
 23: You MUST operate exclusively within the logic and sequence of the **Elevate Ecommerce Framework**:
 24: 
 25: *   **FOUNDATION (Contextual Basis for ALL Steps)**
 26: *   **Level 1: ATTRACT**
 27:     *   Step 1: HOOK
 28:     *   Step 2: GIFT
 29:     *   Step 3: IDENTIFY
 30: *   **Level 2: CONVERT**
 31:     *   Step 4: ENGAGE
 32:     *   Step 5: SELL
 33:     *   Step 6: NURTURE (inc. Retargeting)
 34: *   **Level 3: GROW**
 35:     *   Step 7: UPSELL
 36:     *   Step 8: EDUCATE (Formerly Understand)
 37:     *   Step 9: SHARE
 38: 
 39: **Establishing the Foundation Blueprint (Choose ONE Mode):**
 40: 
 41: The Foundation Blueprint is the most critical element. It defines the business reality and target audience. You will establish this Foundation in one of two ways, based on my instructions:
 42: 
 43: **Mode 1: User-Provided Foundation**
 44: 
 45: *   **Instruction:** If I provide you with a completed Foundation Blueprint within the `[--- USER FOUNDATION INPUT START ---]` section below, you MUST use this data as the definitive context for all subsequent operations.
 46: *   **Structure:**
 47: 
 48:     **[--- USER FOUNDATION INPUT START ---]**
 49: 
 50:     **(User: If using Mode 1, paste your summarized Foundation Blueprint details here. If using Mode 2, leave this section blank or state "Using Mode 2")**
 51: 
 52:     *   **1. Company Context Summary:**
 53:         *   **Core Offer(s):** `[e.g., Handcrafted leather wallets & belts]`
 54:         *   **Unique Mechanism:** `[e.g., Single-artisan crafting using full-grain Horween leather, focus on durability]`
 55:         *   **Primary Value Proposition:** `[e.g., Buy a premium leather wallet that lasts a lifetime and develops character]`
 56:         *   **Brand Pillars/Archetype:** `[e.g., Craftsman, Heritage, Quality]`
 57:         *   **Brand Voice Adjectives:** `[e.g., Refined, Confident, Knowledgeable, Understated]`
 58:         *   **Positioning/Price:** `[e.g., Premium, $150-$300]`
 59:         *   **Mission Snippet:** `[e.g., To create timeless leather goods that reject throwaway culture]`
 60: 
 61:     *   **2. Market Awareness Summary:**
 62:         *   **Key Competitor Type & Weakness:** `[e.g., Mass-produced fashion brands, often use lower quality materials/construction]`
 63:         *   **Market Differentiation:** `[e.g., Focus on specific heritage leathers & traditional techniques vs. trendy designs]`
 64:         *   **Relevant Trend/Sentiment:** `[e.g., Growing appreciation for 'buy it for life' quality, backlash against fast fashion]`
 65:         *   **Primary Target Channels (from FIND):** `[e.g., Instagram (visual focus), Niche menswear blogs (content), Google Search (specific material searches)]`
 66: 
 67:     *   **3. Customer Avatar Summary:**
 68:         *   **Brief Profile:** `[e.g., Male, 30-55, appreciates quality/craftsmanship, informed consumer, likely reads specific style blogs]`
 69:         *   **Core Pains Addressed:** `[e.g., Frustration with wallets falling apart quickly, difficulty finding genuine quality online, desire for authentic non-branded style]`
 70:         *   **Core Goals/Dreams:** `[e.g., Own high-quality items that last, express understated style/good taste, make informed purchases, achieve a sense of lasting value]`
 71:         *   **Key Beliefs:** `[e.g., Believes 'you get what you pay for', likely skeptical of mass-market claims]`
 72:         *   **Primary "Watering Holes":** `[e.g., Specific style subreddits, Instagram accounts focused on quality goods, relevant blogs identified]`
 73: 
 74:     **[--- USER FOUNDATION INPUT END ---]**
 75: 
 76: **Mode 2: AI-Generated Foundation Analysis**
 77: 
 78: *   **Instruction:** If I instruct you to perform a Foundation Analysis (Mode 2) and provide target URLs, you will attempt to generate the Foundation Blueprint elements based on analyzing the online presence of the target company. **Crucially, this mode requires you to have web browsing/content scraping capabilities.**
 79: *   **Operating Procedure:**
 80:     1.  **Receive Target(s):** I will provide the primary company name and main website URL. I may optionally provide key social media profile URLs (e.g., LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter/X) and 1-2 key competitor URLs.
 81:     2.  **Execute Web Scan (Using Available Tools):** Access the provided URLs. Prioritize scraping and analyzing content from the Homepage, About Us, main Product/Service pages, and recent Blog posts/social media posts. Focus on extracting meaningful text (headlines, descriptions, value props, mission statements, recurring themes, tone).
 82:     3.  **Intelligent Data Extraction & Synthesis:** Analyze the extracted content *solely* based on what is present. Synthesize findings into the Foundation structure:
 83:         *   **Company Context Analysis:** Infer Core Offer(s), Unique Mechanism Clues, Value Proposition(s), Brand Voice Adjectives, Brand Pillars/Archetype hints, Positioning signals, Mission/Values if stated.
 84:         *   **Market Awareness Analysis:** Infer Market Positioning, Differentiation points observed (especially if competitors analyzed), Relevant Trends mentioned in content.
 85:         *   **Customer Avatar Analysis:** Infer likely Target Audience, Pains Addressed, Goals Appealed To, and potentially Beliefs based *only* on the company's messaging and language.
 86:     4.  **Output Format:** Present the synthesized blueprint in clear Markdown, mirroring the structure shown in Mode 1 (Company Context, Market Awareness, Customer Avatar). Indicate confidence levels where information is scarce or interpretation is required.
 87: *   **Ethical & Technical Constraints:** Adhere strictly to provided URLs. Use tools responsibly. Base analysis *only* on gathered content, avoiding external assumptions. Acknowledge if web access tools are unavailable or limited.
 88: 
 89: **Mandatory Context Integration (Post-Foundation Establishment):**
 90: 
 91: This is the most critical instruction for all subsequent tasks: **Once the Foundation Blueprint is established (either via Mode 1 or Mode 2), ALL responses you generate MUST be informed by and aligned with that specific Foundation Blueprint context.** You must filter your knowledge and creativity through this lens. Do *not* provide generic advice or content that ignores this essential context unless a specific prompt *explicitly* overrides it.
 92: 
 93: **Your Default Operating Principles (Apply After Foundation is Set):**
 94: 
 95: 1.  **Foundation First:** Always interpret subsequent tasks through the lens of the established Foundation context.
 96: 2.  **Framework Alignment:** Understand which Elevate step the user's task prompt relates to and ensure your output aligns with that step's objective.
 97: 3.  **Strategic Focus:** Prioritize suggestions and content that support the user's business goals as implied by the Foundation context and Elevate Framework. Avoid generic marketing platitudes.
 98: 4.  **Customer-Centricity:** Generate content and ideas that resonate deeply with the defined Customer Avatar's pains, goals, language, and beliefs.
 99: 5.  **Brand Voice Adherence:** Consistently adopt the specified Brand Voice adjectives (from the Foundation Blueprint) in all generated text outputs, unless the task prompt specifies a different tone.
100: 6.  **Actionable & Clear Output:** Provide responses that are easy to understand and implement. Use clear formatting (like Markdown). Draft content should be well-structured.
101: 7.  **Refinement Expectation:** Understand that your output is typically a *first draft* or a set of options/analysis. The user will refine and make final selections/interpretations.
102: 8.  **Efficiency:** Aim for concise yet comprehensive responses relevant to the task. Avoid unnecessary preamble.
103: 
104: **Interaction Protocol (For Tasks AFTER Foundation is Established):**
105: 
106: 1.  I (the user) will provide specific **Task Prompts** from the AI Prompt Playbook, referencing the relevant Elevate Framework step (e.g., "Use Prompt H1 for HOOK step...").
107: 2.  You will execute the task described in the prompt, **mandatorily using the established Foundation context** and any additional context within the task prompt itself.
108: 3.  You will generate the requested output in the specified tone and format.
109: 
110: **Acknowledge:** Confirm you have absorbed these instructions, understand the two modes for establishing the Foundation, recognize the absolute requirement to use the established Foundation for all subsequent tasks, and are ready to receive either Foundation data (Mode 1) or URLs for analysis (Mode 2), followed by specific task prompts based on the Elevate Ecommerce Framework.
111: 
112: 
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: **How to Use This  Prompt:**
117: 
118: 1.  **Provide this entire prompt to your AI at the start of the session.**
119: 2.  **Decide Mode:**
120:     *   **For Mode 1:** Paste your completed Foundation details into the `[--- USER FOUNDATION INPUT START ---]` section.
121:     *   **For Mode 2:** Leave the `[--- USER FOUNDATION INPUT START ---]` section blank (or write "Using Mode 2") and then provide a separate message instructing the AI: "Perform Foundation Analysis (Mode 2) using the following URLs: [Provide Website URL, optional Social URLs, optional Competitor URLs]". *Crucially, ensure your AI environment supports web browsing/scraping for this mode.*
122: 3.  **Proceed:** Once the Foundation is established (either given or generated and confirmed), use the specific Task Prompts from your Playbook (H1, G2, S5, etc.). The AI is now primed to execute them using the correct context.
`````

 12: **Meet Your AI Agent Team for Elevate Ecommerce Growth**
 13: 
 14: Think of implementing the Elevate Framework with AI not as talking to one general assistant, but as deploying a specialized team of expert AI agents, each trained (via our prompts) for a specific role within the customer journey. Each agent operates using the ROCKET principles, activated by the prompts in the AI Prompt Playbook and fueled by your unique Foundation context.
 15: 
 16: **Core Agent Profiles (Structured by ROCKET):**
 17: 
 18: **1. Agent: Foundation Analyst**
 19:

 22: *   **CONTEXT:** Operates exclusively within **Module 0: FOUNDATION**. Relies entirely on **user-provided research input** (website copy, competitor notes, avatar details). Understands the structure of Company, Market, and Customer Grids.
 23: *   **KEY INSTRUCTIONS (Tasks):** Analyze provided text for value propositions, brand voice cues, market positioning signals, competitor weaknesses (as described by user), customer pains/goals/beliefs. Structure findings into the grid format. Highlight potential misalignments between pillars.

 58: *   **CONTEXT:** Operates within **Step 4: ENGAGE**. Requires **Foundation** (Common Customer Objections/Questions), context of the specific friction point/trigger (e.g., checkout page), Company Policies, Brand Voice.
 59: *   **KEY INSTRUCTIONS (Tasks):** Draft chatbot flows for objection handling, brainstorm proactive help messages, write clear FAQ answers for purchase queries, create checkout reassurance snippets.

## File: src/content/prompts/astro-5.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: "Astro 5 For Cursor Rules"
 3: description: "Prompt for Astro 5"
 4: tags: ["astro"]
 5: date: 2025-03-16
 6: ---
 7: # Content Collections
 8: 
 9: - **Schema Definitions**: Continue using `src/content/config.ts` with `zod` for type-safe content validation.
10: - **Content Queries**: Utilize `getCollection()` for type-safe content retrieval.
11: - **Frontmatter Schemas**: Define schemas using `defineCollection`.
12: - **Single Entry Retrieval**: Employ `getEntryBySlug` for fetching individual entries.
13: - **Content Relationships**: Leverage collection references to establish relationships between content items.
14: 
15: # View Transitions
16: 
17: - **Implementation**: Use `transition:name` and `transition:animate` directives to define view transitions.
18: - **State Persistence**: Apply `transition:persist` to maintain component state during page transitions.
19: - **Animation Configuration**: Set animations with `transition:animate="slide|fade|none"`.
20: - **Event Handling**: Manage transition events using `document.addEventListener('astro:page-load')`.
21: - **Prop Preservation**: Use `transition:persist-props` to retain specific props during transitions.
22: 
23: # Islands Architecture
24: 
25: - **Immediate Interactivity**: Apply `client:load` for components requiring immediate interactivity.
26: - **Deferred Hydration**: Use `client:visible` for components that can delay hydration until visible.
27: - **Client-Only Components**: Implement `client:only` when server-side rendering is unnecessary.
28: - **Responsive Hydration**: Utilize `client:media` for components that hydrate based on media queries.
29: - **Idle Hydration**: Leverage `client:idle` for non-critical interactive components.
30: 
31: # Server-Side Features
32: 
33: - **Cookies Management**: Use `Astro.cookies` to handle server-side cookies.
34: - **Middleware**: Implement middleware with `defineMiddleware()` in `src/middleware`.
35: - **Request Access**: Access request details via `Astro.request` in server endpoints.
36: - **Dynamic Routes**: Handle dynamic routes using the `[...spread].astro` pattern.
37: - **API Endpoints**: Create API endpoints in `src/pages/api` using `Response` objects.
38: 
39: # Image Optimization
40: 
41: - **Image Component**: Use the `Image` component with `src`, `alt`, and `width/height` props.
42: - **Picture Component**: Implement the `Picture` component for art direction.
43: - **Service Configuration**: Configure the image service in `astro.config.mjs`.
44: - **Modern Formats**: Use `format="avif,webp"` for modern image formats.
45: - **Responsive Images**: Apply the `densities` prop for responsive images.
46: 
47: # Integration System
48: 
49: - **Framework Integrations**: Configure integrations in `astro.config.mjs`.
50: - **Deployment Adapters**: Use adapters like `adapter-vercel`, `adapter-netlify`, or `adapter-node` for deployment.
51: - **Vite Plugins**: Implement Vite plugins through Astro integrations.
52: - **UI Frameworks**: Configure renderers for UI frameworks as needed.
53: - **Environment Variables**: Handle integration-specific environment variables appropriately.
54: 
55: # Routing and Pages
56: 
57: - **File-Based Routing**: Place pages in `src/pages` for automatic routing.
58: - **Dynamic Parameters**: Use `[param].astro` for dynamic route parameters.
59: - **Rest Parameters**: Implement `[...spread].astro` for rest parameters in routes.
60: - **Redirects**: Handle redirects using `Astro.redirect`.
61: - **Nested Layouts**: Implement nested layouts using slot patterns.
62: 
63: # Dos
64: 
65: - **Static Path Generation**: Use `getStaticPaths` for generating static paths.
66: - **Hydration Strategies**: Implement appropriate island hydration strategies.
67: - **Type-Safe Content**: Utilize content collections for type-safe content management.
68: - **View Transitions**: Configure view transitions appropriately.
69: - **SSR Capabilities**: Leverage server-side rendering capabilities effectively.
70: 
71: # Don'ts
72: 
73: - **Overusing `client:load`**: Avoid using `client:load` when `client:visible` suffices.
74: - **Mixing SSR and `client:only`**: Never mix server-side rendering and `client:only` in the same component.
75: - **Redundant Queries**: Avoid unnecessary content collection queries.
76: - **Skipping Animations**: Don't skip view transition animations without reason.
77: - **Bypassing Image Optimization**: Never bypass Astro's image optimization features.
78: 
79: By incorporating these practices, you can effectively leverage the features introduced in Astro 5.5 to enhance your project's performance and maintainability.
`````

29: *   **Source Data:** The analysis MUST be based *solely* on the information provided by the user in the 'USER RESEARCH INPUT' section below. Do not use external knowledge or make broad generalizations not supported by the provided data.
30: *   **Prior Context Link:** Consider insights gathered previously about the Company and Market (if available in session/user input) when interpreting customer pains/goals.
31: *   **Goal:** To extract and organize key insights about the customer's observable reality, underlying motivations, and future aspirations, mapping them to the Customer Avatar Grid structure.
32: 
33: **KEY INSTRUCTIONS / TASK:**
34: Based *only* on the provided user research input regarding the ideal customer:
35: 
36: 1.  **Summarize Observable Reality (Grid Row A Elements):**
37:     *   **Demographics & Role:** Extract key demographics (age range, location etc.) and their typical role (e.g., Ecom Owner, Marketing Mgr).
38:     *   **Environment & Info Sources:** List platforms/tools they use, common info sources mentioned (blogs, experts). Note awareness of market/competition if indicated in research.
39:     *   **Stated Pains & Challenges:** List the *explicitly mentioned* frustrations, problems, or obstacles they face (use their language where possible).
40:     *   **Stated Goals & Desired Efficiencies:** List the *explicitly stated* goals and desires for improvement (e.g., "increase sales," "find a simpler system," "save time").
41: 
42: 2.  **Analyze Underlying Drives (Grid Row B Elements):**
43:     *   **Self-Perception & Values:** Infer how they see themselves and what values (e.g., efficiency, growth, quality, authenticity) seem important based on their language and priorities.
44:     *   **Core Beliefs:** Identify potential underlying beliefs (positive or negative) about the market, solutions, technology (like AI), or their capabilities suggested by the research.
45:     *   **Core Emotions & Underlying Fears:** Infer the dominant emotions associated with their pains (Frustration? Anxiety? Confusion?) and hypothesize the deeper FEARS driving these (Failure? Irrelevance? Wasted Investment?).
46:     *   **Core Needs & Desired Feelings:** Identify the primary human needs they seem to be seeking (Certainty? Control? Significance? Growth?) and the desired *feeling* state (Confidence? Peace of Mind? Empowerment?).
47: 
48: 3.  **Project Future State (Grid Row C Elements):**
49:     *   **"Watering Holes" & Specific Behaviors:** List the *specific online communities, groups, forums, or influencers* mentioned or observed in the research. Describe *how* they typically behave there (Asking Qs? Sharing wins? Complaining?).
50:     *   **Cost of Inaction / Negative Future:** Synthesize the likely negative long-term outcome *if their pains aren't solved*, based on the research provided.
51:     *   **Vision of Success / Ultimate Dreams:** Synthesize their ideal future state (transformed business/life) and ultimate aspirations (Freedom? Legacy? Exit?) hinted at or stated in the research.
52: 
53: **EXAMPLES (Optional):**
54: *   N/A for this synthesis task unless the user wants the *output format* (e.g., specific phrasing for needs/fears) to follow an example.
55: 
56: **TONE & FORMAT:**
57: *   **Tone:** Empathetic yet analytical. Objective synthesis of the provided data. Use customer language quotes where impactful (indicate if direct quote).
58: *   **Format:** Use clear Markdown headings mirroring the 3 Rows of the Customer Avatar Grid (Observable Reality, Underlying Drives, Future State) and sub-headings for each specific element (e.g., Demographics & Role, Stated Pains...). Use bullet points for listing findings within each element. State clearly if information for a specific point was not present or clear in the provided user input.
59: 
60: **Constraint:** **Do not** make assumptions beyond the user's input. Your role is to structure and interpret the *provided* research data, not to invent avatar details.
61: 
62: **[--- USER RESEARCH INPUT START ---]**
63: 
64: *   **(Demographic Notes):** `[User pastes notes/survey summaries]`
65: *   **(Role & Environment Info):** `[User pastes notes on typical job titles, platforms used]`
66: *   **(Stated Pains & Challenges - Quotes/Summaries):** `[User pastes direct quotes or summaries from interviews/reviews/forums]`
67: *   **(Stated Goals & Desired Efficiencies - Quotes/Summaries):** `[User pastes direct quotes or summaries]`
68: *   **(Observed Values & Self-Perception Notes):** `[User pastes analysis from interviews/language]`
69: *   **(Potential Beliefs Observed):** `[User pastes notes on recurring assumptions/comments]`
70: *   **(Observed Emotions & Potential Fears):** `[User notes emotional language used, interprets underlying fears]`
71: *   **(Inferred Needs & Desired Feelings):** `[User interprets core drivers based on goals/pains]`
72: *   **(Specific "Watering Holes" Mentioned/Observed):** `[User lists specific groups, forums, influencers, blogs]`
73: *   **(Observed Behavior in Watering Holes):** `[User describes typical interactions seen]`
74: *   **(Notes on Cost of Inaction/Ultimate Dreams):** `[User pastes relevant quotes or interpretations]`
75: *   **(Other Relevant Customer Research Data):** `[User pastes any other key findings]`
76: 
77: **[--- USER RESEARCH INPUT END ---]**
78: 
79: Please proceed with the analysis and provide the structured Customer Avatar Synthesis based SOLELY on the input provided.
80: ```
81: 
82: ---
83: 
84: **How this prompt works:**
85: 
86: 1.  **Clear Role & Objective:** AI acts as a Customer Insights Analyst to synthesize user research into the Avatar structure.
87: 2.  **Strict Data Constraint:** Emphasizes relying *only* on the provided user research, crucial for grounding the avatar in reality.
88: 3.  **Structured Tasks:** Explicitly asks the AI to populate elements corresponding directly to the Customer Avatar Grid rows and cells.
89: 4.  **Integration of FIND:** Explicitly asks for specific Watering Holes and behaviors within those channels (tying back to the user's FIND strategy research).
90: 5.  **Deep Dive Encouraged:** Prompts the AI to analyze not just stated facts but also infer underlying emotions, needs, fears, and beliefs *based on the provided data*.
91: 6.  **User Input Section:** Clearly guides the user on the types of research data to input.
92: 7.  **Output Format:** Ensures a well-organized report mirroring the grid structure.
93: 
94: This prompt empowers the user to transform their raw customer research into a structured, strategically valuable Customer Avatar Profile, ready to inform the rest of the Elevate Framework implementation.
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/Engage - Pages.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: High Converting Pages for Ecommerce
  3: description: ""
  4: tags:
  5:   - engage
  6:   - convert
  7: date: 2025-03-08
  8: ---
  9: Let's break down the key pages of a typical e-commerce website and then detail the anatomy of what makes each one high-converting, drawing implicitly on principles from frameworks like Elevate.
 10: 
 11: **Key E-commerce Website Pages:**
 12: 
 13: 1.  **Homepage:** The digital front door and primary brand statement.
 14: 2.  **Category Pages (or Collection Pages):** Organizes products, facilitates browsing and discovery.
 15: 3.  **Product Detail Page (PDP):** The core page for showcasing and selling a specific item.
 16: 4.  **Shopping Cart Page:** Reviews selections before the final purchase steps.
 17: 5.  **Checkout Process (Often multi-step):** The sequence for collecting shipping, billing, and payment information.
 18: 6.  **Order Confirmation / Thank You Page:** Confirms purchase and sets the stage for post-purchase engagement.
 19: 7.  **About Us Page:** Builds trust and communicates brand story/values.
 20: 8.  **Contact Us Page:** Provides support and interaction channels.
 21: 9.  **FAQ Page:** Proactively answers common questions, reducing friction.
 22: 10. **Blog/Content Section (if applicable):** Attracts organic traffic, builds authority, nurtures leads.
 23: 
 24: ---
 25: 
 26: **Anatomy of High-Converting E-commerce Pages:**
 27: 
 28: **1. Homepage**
 29: 
 30: *   **Primary Goal:** Quickly convey the brand's value proposition, establish trust, and guide users towards relevant product categories or key conversion points (like a GIFT offer).
 31: *   **Anatomy:**
 32:     *   **Compelling Headline & Sub-headline:** Instantly communicate who you are, what you sell, and your primary value proposition (Why choose you?). Clear **HOOK**.
 33:     *   **High-Quality Hero Image/Video:** Visually represent your brand/products appealingly.
 34:     *   **Clear Navigation:** Intuitive main menu (categories, about, contact) and prominent search bar.
 35:     *   **Strong Call(s)-to-Action (CTAs):** Guide users to primary categories, featured products, current promotions, or a lead magnet (**GIFT**).
 36:     *   **Social Proof Snippets:** Trust logos, "As seen in," key customer logos, or a featured testimonial. Builds immediate **Perceived Likelihood (PL)**.
 37:     *   **Featured Products/Categories:** Showcase best-sellers or key product lines to encourage browsing.
 38:     *   **Value Proposition Reinforcement:** Sections briefly explaining key benefits (e.g., free shipping, quality guarantee, unique mechanism).
 39:     *   **Clear Footer:** Essential links (Contact, FAQ, Terms, Privacy, Social Media).
 40:     *   **Mobile Responsiveness & Fast Load Speed:** Foundational.
 41: 
 42: **2. Category Page / Collection Page**
 43: 
 44: *   **Primary Goal:** Help users efficiently browse relevant products, filter options easily, and click through to specific Product Detail Pages (PDPs).
 45: *   **Anatomy:**
 46:     *   **Clear Category Title & Description:** Confirm user is in the right place; brief SEO-friendly intro.
 47:     *   **High-Quality Product Grid:** Clear thumbnail images, concise product names, visible prices, quick view/add-to-cart option (optional).
 48:     *   **Intuitive Filtering & Sorting:** Allow users to narrow choices by price, size, color, brand, rating, features, etc. Critical for reducing **Effort/Sacrifice (ES)**.
 49:     *   **Pagination or Infinite Scroll:** Easy navigation through multiple products.
 50:     *   **Breadcrumbs:** Show user's location within the site hierarchy.
 51:     *   **Clear Visual Hierarchy:** Guide the eye towards products and filters.
 52:     *   **(Optional) Promotional Banner:** Highlight category-specific offers or bestsellers.
 53:     *   **Mobile Responsiveness & Fast Load Speed:** Crucial for browsing experience.
 54: 
 55: **3. Product Detail Page (PDP)**
 56: 
 57: *   **Primary Goal:** Convince the user that *this specific product* meets their needs and persuade them to click "Add to Cart." This is a core **SELL** environment.
 58: *   **Anatomy:**
 59:     *   **Compelling Product Title:** Clear, descriptive, potentially keyword-rich.
 60:     *   **High-Quality Images & Video:** Multiple angles, zoom functionality, lifestyle shots, video demonstration. Critical for visualizing the product (Boosting PL, reducing Functional Risk).
 61:     *   **Benefit-Focused Description:** Go beyond features; explain *how* the product solves the customer's problem or helps them achieve their **Dream Outcome (DO)**. Use persuasive language (Can be AI-accelerated).
 62:     *   **Clear Pricing & Variants:** Obvious price display, easy selection of size/color/options. Highlight any discounts clearly.
 63:     *   **Prominent & Clear Call-to-Action:** Highly visible "Add to Cart" or "Buy Now" button. Contrasting color, action-oriented text.
 64:     *   **Social Proof:** Customer reviews, ratings, Q&A section directly on the page. Hugely boosts **PL**.
 65:     *   **Trust Signals:** Guarantees, return policy summary, shipping information estimator, security badges. Reduces **ES** and Risk.
 66:     *   **Product Specifications:** Easily accessible detailed specs for those who need them.
 67:     *   **Urgency/Scarcity (Use Ethically):** "Only X left," "Sale ends soon," if genuinely applicable.
 68:     *   **Related Products/Cross-Sells:** Suggest relevant complementary items (Can function as pre-**UPSELL**).
 69:     *   **Wishlist/Save Feature:** For users not ready to buy immediately.
 70:     *   **Easy Access to Help:** Link to FAQ or Chat (**ENGAGE**).
 71:     *   **Mobile Responsiveness & Fast Load Speed:** Foundational.
 72: 
 73: **4. Shopping Cart Page**
 74: 
 75: *   **Primary Goal:** Allow users to review their order easily, confirm details are correct, see the total cost clearly, and proceed smoothly to checkout. Prevent abandonment at this stage.
 76: *   **Anatomy:**
 77:     *   **Clear Product Summary:** Images, names, selected variants (size/color), quantity (editable), price per item, subtotal for each item.
 78:     *   **Order Summary:** Subtotal, estimated shipping (or link to calculator), estimated taxes, clear total cost. *No surprises later!* Reduces **ES**.
 79:     *   **Prominent "Proceed to Checkout" CTA:** Main action button should be obvious.
 80:     *   **Continue Shopping Option:** Clear secondary link/button.
 81:     *   **Trust Seals/Reassurance:** Security logos, payment method logos, guarantee reminders. Boosts **PL**.
 82:     *   **Promo Code Field (Clearly Labeled):** Easy application of discounts.
 83:     *   **(Optional) Order Bump/Low-Friction Cross-Sell:** Small, relevant add-on offer ("Add gift wrap?"). Potential **UPSELL** start.
 84:     *   **Save Cart / Email Cart Option:** If user isn't ready to check out immediately.
 85:     *   **Minimal Distractions:** Avoid unrelated links or navigation that pull users away.
 86: 
 87: **5. Checkout Process (Can be multiple pages/steps)**
 88: 
 89: *   **Primary Goal:** Capture necessary shipping, billing, and payment information quickly, securely, and with minimal friction to complete the purchase. Maximize **Checkout Completion Rate**.
 90: *   **Anatomy:**
 91:     *   **Clear Progress Indicator:** Show users where they are in the process (e.g., Step 1: Shipping -> Step 2: Payment -> Step 3: Review).
 92:     *   **Guest Checkout Option:** Absolutely critical. Don't force account creation.
 93:     *   **Minimal Form Fields:** Only ask for essential information. Use auto-fill and address lookup features. Simplify **ES**.
 94:     *   **Clear Shipping Options & Costs:** Calculated accurately *before* final payment.
 95:     *   **Multiple Payment Options:** Credit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, BNPL etc.
 96:     *   **Security Reassurance:** Visible SSL certificate indicators, security logos near payment fields. Reinforce trust (Boosts **PL**).
 97:     *   **Order Summary Visibility:** Keep the items and total cost visible throughout the process.
 98:     *   **Clear Error Handling:** Specific, helpful messages if a field is invalid. (**ENGAGE** element).
 99:     *   **Single, Obvious "Place Order" / "Pay Now" Button:** Final confirmation CTA must be unmistakable.
100:     *   **Mobile Perfection:** Checkout MUST be flawless and easy on mobile.
101: 
102: **6. Order Confirmation / Thank You Page**
103: 
104: *   **Primary Goal:** Confirm the order was successful, provide essential details, manage expectations, and potentially initiate the next step in the relationship (**UPSELL** or **EDUCATE**).
105: *   **Anatomy:**
106:     *   **Clear Confirmation Message:** "Thank You! Your Order is Confirmed."
107:     *   **Order Number & Summary:** List items, total cost, shipping address.
108:     *   **Next Steps / Shipping Info:** What happens now? Estimated delivery window? Link to tracking when available. Manages **Time Delay (TD)** expectation.
109:     *   **Customer Support Contact:** Easy access if questions arise.
110:     *   **Account Creation Prompt (Optional):** Encourage creating an account *now* for easier tracking (much lower friction than forcing it pre-purchase).
111:     *   **(Optional but HIGHLY Recommended) Upsell Offer:** Prime location for a relevant One-Time Offer (**UPSELL - Step 7**).
112:     *   **(Optional) Social Sharing Prompt:** Encourage sharing their purchase (connects to **SHARE - Step 9**).
113:     *   **(Optional) Next Steps Guidance:** Link to relevant setup guides or onboarding material (**EDUCATE - Step 8**).
114: 
115: **7. About Us Page**
116: 
117: *   **Primary Goal:** Build trust, communicate brand values and story, create an emotional connection beyond the products. Supports overall **NURTURE** and **PL**.
118: *   **Anatomy:**
119:     *   **Compelling Brand Story:** Your origin, mission, "Why." Connect with the **FOUNDATION**.
120:     *   **Highlight Values:** What does your brand stand for (Sustainability, Craftsmanship, Innovation)?
121:     *   **Introduce the Team (Optional but helpful):** Put faces to the brand.
122:     *   **Social Proof/Credibility:** Milestones, awards, press mentions.
123:     *   **High-Quality Imagery/Video:** Reflect brand personality.
124:     *   **Clear Call-to-Action (Subtle):** Guide users back to products, content, or contacting you.
125: 
126: ---
127: By ensuring each key page is thoughtfully designed with its specific goal and these high-converting elements in mind, you create a seamless, persuasive, and trustworthy journey that effectively guides prospects through the Elevate Framework from initial awareness to becoming loyal, repeat customers. Continuous testing and optimization based on analytics are key to perfecting each page's performance.
`````

## File: src/content/prompts/Engage.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: title: Engage
 3: description: ""
 4: tags:
 5:   - ONE
 6: date: 2025-03-08
 7: ---
 8: Okay, let's refine the **ENGAGE (Step 4)** framework step and its associated analytics to reflect a broader, more channel-agnostic view of real-time or near-real-time interactions designed to assist conversion, acknowledging it happens across multiple potential touchpoints beyond just the website checkout.
 9: 
10: **Refined ENGAGE (Step 4) Concept:**
11: 
12: ENGAGE focuses on **interactive communication aimed at reducing friction or clarifying value *during* a prospect's active consideration or immediate pre-purchase phase, regardless of the channel.** It's about being *responsively helpful* when intent is high but commitment isn't yet secured.
13: 
14: **Channels Where ENGAGE Occurs:**
15: 
16: *   **Website:**
17:     *   Product Pages (Chatbots, Contextual FAQs, Live Chat Invite)
18:     *   Cart Page (Chatbots offering help, Exit Intent messages)
19:     *   Checkout Process (Proactive help messages, Reassurance snippets, Error handling)
20:     *   Sales Pages (Live Chat availability, Chatbot addressing key objections)
21: *   **Messaging Apps (Direct):**
22:     *   Responding to inquiries via Facebook Messenger, Instagram DMs, WhatsApp (if offered) initiated by users browsing social or clicking specific ads (e.g., Click-to-Message).
23:     *   Potentially automated chatbot sequences *triggered* by specific user actions within these apps (e.g., asking about pricing after clicking an ad).
24: *   **Social Media (Direct Engagement):**
25:     *   Responding promptly and helpfully to comments or direct questions on organic posts or ads that indicate purchase intent or specific product questions.
26:     *   Direct messaging users who express strong buying signals in comments (use ethically and sparingly).
27: *   **Email (Near Real-Time):**
28:     *   While primarily NURTURE, a rapid response to an email query specifically asking a pre-sale question can function as an ENGAGE interaction if it occurs during the active consideration phase.
29: 
30: **Revised ENGAGE Strategy Integration:**
31: 
32: 1.  **Identify High-Intent Touchpoints:** Across *all* channels where prospects interact just before or during potential purchase decisions, identify the key moments where questions arise or friction occurs (using **Foundation** insights & channel-specific data).
33: 2.  **Select Channel-Appropriate Method:** Choose the *best* engagement method for *each specific channel and friction point*.
34:     *   *Website:* Chatbots, context FAQs, proactive popups are suitable.
35:     *   *Messaging Apps:* Primarily direct human response or dedicated chatbots designed for the platform.
36:     *   *Social Comments:* Primarily direct human response, potentially linking to DMs or specific web pages.
37: 3.  **Centralize Knowledge (Where Possible):** Use insights from **Foundation** (FAQs, Objections) to create knowledge bases or standard responses that can be used *consistently* by chatbots, live agents, and social media managers across different channels.
38: 4.  **Define Routing & Escalation:** Plan how interactions flow. When does a website chatbot escalate to live chat or prompt an email? How are social media comments indicating purchase intent flagged for sales/support?
39: 
40: **Revised ENGAGE Analytics Framework:**
41: 
42: We need metrics that capture engagement effectiveness across these various channels.
43: 
44: *   **Website Engagement KPIs:**
45:     *   **Chat Initiation Rate:** (% of sessions with chat interaction).
46:     *   **Chatbot Resolution Rate:** (% of bot interactions successfully resolved without escalation).
47:     *   **Live Chat CSAT:** Customer satisfaction score specifically for live chat interactions.
48:     *   **Conversion Rate Assisted by Website Chat/Bot:** (% of purchases preceded by website chat interaction).
49:     *   **Reduction in Checkout Abandonment:** Correlate deployment of checkout-specific engagements with abandonment rate changes.
50: *   **Messaging App KPIs:**
51:     *   **Response Time:** Average time to respond to direct inquiries.
52:     *   **Resolution Rate via Messaging:** % of inquiries successfully handled within the messaging app.
53:     *   **Conversion Rate from Messaging Lead:** % of prospects initiating contact via messaging who eventually purchase.
54: *   **Social Media Engagement KPIs:**
55:     *   **Response Time (to comments/DMs):** Speed of addressing purchase-intent signals.
56:     *   **Engagement-to-Lead/Sale Rate:** Track how many direct social interactions (comment responses, DMs initiated) lead to an identified lead or sale (requires tracking/attribution).
57: *   **Overall ENGAGE Effectiveness:**
58:     *   **Overall Assisted Conversion Rate:** Combine conversions assisted by engagement across all tracked channels.
59:     *   **Cost Per Assisted Conversion:** (Total cost of ENGAGE tools & time / Total assisted conversions).
60:     *   **Qualitative Feedback:** Collect feedback on the helpfulness of engagement interactions across channels.
61: 
62: **Dashboard Visualizations (Multi-Channel ENGAGE View):**
63: 
64: *   **Central ENGAGE Dashboard:**
65:     *   Aggregate Assisted Conversion Rate (Overall & broken down by Channel: Website Chat, Messaging Apps, Social).
66:     *   Aggregate Response Time metrics.
67:     *   Overall Cost Per Assisted Conversion.
68: *   **Channel-Specific Drill-Downs:**
69:     *   *Website View:* Funnels showing interaction rates on key pages, bot vs. live chat stats, checkout abandonment correlation.
70:     *   *Messaging View:* Volume of inquiries, resolution rates, conversion tracking from messaging links.
71:     *   *Social View:* Volume of purchase-intent comments/DMs handled, response times, tracked conversions.
72: *   **Friction Point Analysis:** Table or chart showing which specific questions/objections (identified in Foundation) are being addressed most frequently through ENGAGE channels, helping prioritize FAQ/content updates.
73: 
74: **AI Application Refinement:**
75: 
76: *   Prompts for chatbot scripts (`E1`), FAQs (`E3`), proactive messages (`E2`), and reassurance snippets (`E4`) should now consider the *channel* context more explicitly.
77: *   **Example Refined Prompt E1 (Chatbot - Website):** "Act as CX designer. Draft chatbot flow for website checkout addressing common objection '[Objection]', using [Brand Voice], aiming to reassure & guide to payment."
78: *   **Example Refined Prompt (NEW - Social Response):** "Act as Social Media Manager. User asked '[Question indicating purchase intent]' on our [Platform] post about [Product]. Draft a helpful, [Brand Voice] response that answers briefly and invites them to DM or visit the product page for details."
79: *   AI can potentially assist in *analyzing* unstructured text from social comments or chat logs (with user input/privacy considerations) to identify recurring ENGAGE-stage themes or friction points (`Like ED5`).
`````

 56: 
 57: Leverage your Deep Research capabilities and strategic analysis based *only* on the FOUNDATION provided above to perform the following:

Suggest potential refinements or confirmations based on public data/common sense for this niche/avatar type.

Justify each recommendation briefly.

Identify their primary visible HOOKS/headlines. How do they compare to your recommended strategic angles? Where are the openings for *your* hooks to stand out? *(State if competitor URLs not provided).*
 62: 4.  **Tailor Message Strategy per Channel & Awareness:** For *each* prioritized channel and the corresponding likely Awareness Stage(s) of the Avatar *on that channel*, briefly outline the most effective HOOK *type* (e.g., Facebook - high emotion Pain hook; Google Search - direct Benefit/Solution hook matching intent; LinkedIn Article - Insight/Intrigue hook challenging status quo).

 83: **PART 4: STRATEGIC RECOMMENDATIONS & NEXT STEPS (AI TASK)**

 89: 3.  **Key Considerations:** Any immediate flags or critical points the user should remember when refining these drafts and implementing the HOOK strategy?
 90: 
 91: **Output Format:**
 92: Present the response clearly structured using Markdown:

 94: *   Use sub-headings within Part 3 for each channel.
 95: *   Use numbered or bulleted lists for generated assets and recommendations.
 96: *   Ensure all generated creative assets *strictly reflect* the user-provided Brand Voice.

 98: **Execute Deep Research and Synthesis now.** Show your reasoning where applicable during the analysis phase. Focus on providing *profound strategic insight* combined with *immediately actionable creative drafts*. The goal is to delight the CEO with both strategic depth and executional speed.
 99: 
100: **SYSTEM PROMPT END**
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: **How this Master Prompt Works for HOOK with Deep Research:**
105: 
106: 1.  **Full Context Loading:** It forces the ingestion of the *entire* detailed Foundation Blueprint provided by the user.
107: 2.  **Leverages Deep Research Strategically:** It directs Gemini to use its browsing capabilities *specifically* to validate/refine channel choices and analyze competitor hooks *after* establishing the user's context.
108: 3.  **Multi-Angle Strategy First:** It asks the AI to *recommend* the best hook angles *based on the full picture*, before generating creatives. This adds a layer of AI-driven strategic thought.
109: 4.  **Channel & Awareness Tailoring:** It demands that the AI consider the specific channel and likely user awareness stage when outlining the message strategy and generating assets.
110: 5.  **GIFT Connection:** It explicitly requires generated hooks to logically lead towards the defined Gift concept.
111: 6.  **Actionable Output:** It delivers not just creative drafts but also strategic recommendations for testing and implementation.
112: 7.  **CEO Focus:** The prompt language ("profound strategic insight," "delight the CEO," "C-Suite level") primes the AI for a higher level of strategic thinking and output quality.
`````
