1301: Error
1302: An error occurred.
1303: Accordion must be used within Accordion
1304: 
1305: Oh no! We have an error. Let's talk through the issue.
1306: 
1307: Astro uses an "island architecture  ", which means that each block of code on the site is an independent group of code. Astro does not assume that our Accordion component pieces fit together. Our Shadcn UI components assume that the components can talk to each other and share context. They cannot.
1308: 
1309: We can solve this in two ways.
1310: 
1311: Rewrite the ShadCN components so they work with Astro. This might involve re-architecting an existing solution that's built into a library.
1312: Wrap all of our Accordion components into one component where we can pass data to it. We lose the composability, but we avoid having to rewrite a lot of logic.
1313: For this guide, we'll go with option 2. If you want to see an example of option 1, check out Popover.tsx.
1314: 
1315: Let's create a new Accordion.tsx component.
1316: 
1317: We'll update the example to iterate over a data prop and render each AccordionItem.
1318: 
1319: site-astro/src/components/Accordion.tsx
1320: Copy to Clipboard
1321: import {
1322: 	Accordion as BaseAccordion,
1323: 	AccordionContent,
1324: 	AccordionItem,
1325: 	AccordionTrigger,
1326: } from "@/components/ui/accordion";
1327: 
1328: interface Props {
1329: 	data: {
1330: 		title: string;
1331: 		description: string;
1332: 	}[];
1333: }
1334: 
1335: export function Accordion({ data }: Props) {
1336: 	return (
1337: 		<BaseAccordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
1338: 			{data.map((item, i) => {
1339: 				return (
1340: 					<AccordionItem value={`item-${i.toFixed()}`}>
1341: 						<AccordionTrigger>{item.title}</AccordionTrigger>
1342: 						<AccordionContent>{item.description}</AccordionContent>
1343: 					</AccordionItem>
1344: 				);
1345: 			})}
1346: 		</BaseAccordion>
1347: 	);
1348: }
1349: Use it index.astro like this:
1350: 
1351: site-astro/src/pages/index.astro
1352: Copy to Clipboard
1353: ---
1354: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
1355: import { Accordion } from "@/components/content/Accordion";
1356: 
1357: const accordionData = [
1358: 	{
1359: 		title: "Is it accessible?",
1360: 		description: "Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.",
1361: 	},
1362: 	{
1363: 		title: "Is it styled?",
1364: 		description:
1365: 			"Yes. It comes with default styles that matches the other components' aesthetic.",
1366: 	},
1367: 	{
1368: 		title: "Is it animated?",
1369: 		description:
1370: 			"Yes. It's animated by default, but you can disable it if you prefer.",
1371: 	},
1372: ];
1373: ---
1374: 
1375: <Layout>
1376: 	<main>
1377: 		<h1>Welcome to SiteName</h1>
1378: 		<Accordion data={accordionData} client:idle />
1379: 	</main>
1380: </Layout>
1381: Now we're in business.
1382: 
1383: Don't forget the client:idle attribute on our Accordion implementation. This tells Astro to load the necessary JS code on the client side so users can click to open/close each accordion item.
1384: 
1385: Astro now treats our entire accordion as one "island". The React context needed to wrap all accordion items can now execute in our browser without an issue.
1386: 
1387: Wrapping Up
1388: Hopefully, this gets you on your way to building quickly with Shadcn and Radix. Both tools should help you write better, more accessible components. They can be daunting to get started with, but they're well documented tools with thriving communities that can help you with your specific use case.
1389: 
1390: I got the Tabs working with client:visible and a workaround for Accordions described in this issue AREA44/astro-shadcn-ui-template#66
1391: 
1392: So basically wrap shadcn Tabs in another Tabs component. So Tabs inside of Tabs of Tabs ;). Then your new Tabs Component could be used with client:visible. And if you need dynamic tab content, just pass your data with props.
1393: 
1394: # Implementing shadcn/ui with Astro
1395: 
1396: ## Setup Instructions
1397: 
1398: 1. Install dependencies
1399: ```bash
1400: npm install @radix-ui/react-tabs class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react
1401: ```
1402: 
1403: 2. Configure Tailwind CSS
1404: ```js
1405: // tailwind.config.js
1406: const { fontFamily } = require("tailwindcss/defaultTheme")
1407: 
1408: /** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
1409: module.exports = {
1410: 	darkMode: ["class"],

1460: 
1461: ## Implementing Tabs
1462: 
1463: 1. Create the base tabs components:
1464: 
1465: ```tsx
1466: // src/components/ui/tabs.tsx
1467: "use client"
1468: 
1469: import * as React from "react"
1470: import * as TabsPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-tabs"
1471: import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
1472: 
1473: const Tabs = TabsPrimitive.Root
1474: 
1475: const TabsList = React.forwardRef<
1476: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.List>,
1477: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.List>
1478: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1479: 	<TabsPrimitive.List
1480: 		ref={ref}
1481: 		className={cn(
1482: 			"inline-flex h-10 items-center justify-center rounded-md bg-muted p-1 text-muted-foreground",
1483: 			className
1484: 		)}
1485: 		{...props}
1486: 	/>
1487: ))
1488: TabsList.displayName = TabsPrimitive.List.displayName
1489: 
1490: const TabsTrigger = React.forwardRef<
1491: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Trigger>,
1492: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Trigger>
1493: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1494: 	<TabsPrimitive.Trigger
1495: 		ref={ref}
1496: 		className={cn(
1497: 			"inline-flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap rounded-sm px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium ring-offset-background transition-all focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 data-[state=active]:bg-background data-[state=active]:text-foreground data-[state=active]:shadow-sm",
1498: 			className
1499: 		)}
1500: 		{...props}
1501: 	/>
1502: ))
1503: TabsTrigger.displayName = TabsPrimitive.Trigger.displayName
1504: 
1505: const TabsContent = React.forwardRef<
1506: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Content>,
1507: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Content>
1508: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1509: 	<TabsPrimitive.Content
1510: 		ref={ref}
1511: 		className={cn(
1512: 			"mt-2 ring-offset-background focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2",
1513: 			className
1514: 		)}
1515: 		{...props}
1516: 	/>
1517: ))
1518: TabsContent.displayName = TabsPrimitive.Content.displayName
1519: 
1520: export { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent }
1521: ```
1522: 
1523: 2. Create a reusable TabsContainer component:
1524: 
1525: ```tsx
1526: // src/components/ui/tabs-container.tsx
1527: 'use client';
1528: 
1529: import { Card } from './card';
1530: import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from './tabs';
1531: import * as React from 'react';
1532: 
1533: export interface TabItem {
1534: 	value: string;
1535: 	label: string;
1536: 	content: React.ReactNode;
1537: }
1538: 
1539: interface TabsContainerProps {
1540: 	items: TabItem[];
1541: 	defaultValue?: string;
1542: 	className?: string;
1543: 	gridCols?: number;
1544: }
1545: 
1546: export function TabsContainer({ 
1547: 	items, 
1548: 	defaultValue, 
1549: 	className = '',
1550: 	gridCols = 4 
1551: }: TabsContainerProps) {
1552: 	const [mounted, setMounted] = React.useState(false);
1553: 	const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = React.useState(defaultValue || items[0]?.value);
1554: 
1555: 	React.useEffect(() => {
1556: 		setMounted(true);
1557: 	}, []);
1558: 
1559: 	if (!mounted) {
1560: 		return null;
1561: 	}
1562: 
1563: 	return (
1564: 		<div className={`w-full ${className}`}>
1565: 			<Tabs defaultValue={activeTab} onValueChange={setActiveTab}>
1566: 				<TabsList className={`grid w-full grid-cols-${gridCols}`}>
1567: 					{items.map((item) => (
1568: 						<TabsTrigger 
1569: 							key={item.value} 
1570: 							value={item.value}
1571: 							className="data-[state=active]:bg-background data-[state=active]:text-foreground"
1572: 						>
1573: 							{item.label}
1574: 						</TabsTrigger>
1575: 					))}
1576: 				</TabsList>
1577: 				{items.map((item) => (
1578: 					<TabsContent 
1579: 						key={item.value} 
1580: 						value={item.value}
1581: 						className="mt-2 ring-offset-background focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2"
1582: 					>
1583: 						<Card className="p-6">
1584: 							{item.content}
1585: 						</Card>
1586: 					</TabsContent>
1587: 				))}
1588: 			</Tabs>
1589: 		</div>
1590: 	);
1591: }
1592: ```
1593: 
1594: 3. Use the tabs in your Astro page:
1595: 
1596: ```astro
1597: ---
1598: import TabsExample from '../components/TabsExample';
1599: 
1600: const items = [
1601: 	{
1602: 		value: 'tab1',
1603: 		label: 'Tab 1',
1604: 		content: <div>Content for tab 1</div>
1605: 	},
1606: 	{
1607: 		value: 'tab2',
1608: 		label: 'Tab 2',
1609: 		content: <div>Content for tab 2</div>
1610: 	}
1611: ];
1612: ---
1613: 
1614: <div>
1615: 	<TabsExample client:load items={items} />
1616: </div>
1617: ```
1618: 
1619: ## Important Notes
1620: 
1621: 1. **Client Hydration**: Always use `client:load` when using interactive components like Tabs.
1622: 
1623: 2. **TypeScript Support**: Make sure your `tsconfig.json` includes:
1624: ```json
1625: {
1626: 	"compilerOptions": {
1627: 		"jsx": "react-jsx",
1628: 		"jsxImportSource": "react"
1629: 	}
1630: }
1631: ```
1632: 
1633: 3. **Styling**: The tabs component uses Tailwind CSS classes. Ensure your `globals.css` includes the necessary shadcn/ui base styles.
1634: 
1635: 4. **Error Handling**: Common issues and solutions:
1636: 	- If you see hydration errors, ensure you're using `client:load`
1637: 	- If styles aren't applying, check your Tailwind configuration
1638: 	- If tabs aren't interactive, verify React is properly set up in your Astro config
1639: 
1640: 5. **Best Practices**:
1641: 	- Keep tab content lightweight
1642: 	- Use semantic labels
1643: 	- Consider mobile responsiveness
1644: 	- Implement proper loading states
1645: 	- Handle edge cases (no tabs, single tab, etc.)
1646: 
1647: ## Example Implementation
1648: 
1649: Here's a complete example of a tabbed interface:
1650: 
1651: ```tsx
1652: // src/components/TabsExample.tsx
1653: import { TabsContainer, type TabItem } from '../ui/tabs-container';
1654: 
1655: interface TabsExampleProps {
1656: 	examples: {
1657: 		basic: string;
1658: 		advanced: string;
1659: 	};
1660: }
1661: 
1662: export default function TabsExample({ examples }: TabsExampleProps) {
1663: 	const items: TabItem[] = [
1664: 		{
1665: 			value: 'basic',
1666: 			label: 'Basic',
1667: 			content: (
1668: 				<>
1669: 					<h3 className="text-xl font-medium mb-4">Basic Example</h3>
1670: 					<p className="text-muted-foreground mb-4">Simple configuration:</p>
1671: 					<pre className="text-sm overflow-auto p-4 bg-muted rounded-lg">
1672: 						{examples.basic}
1673: 					</pre>
1674: 				</>
1675: 			),
1676: 		},
1677: 		{
1678: 			value: 'advanced',
1679: 			label: 'Advanced',
1680: 			content: (
1681: 				<>
1682: 					<h3 className="text-xl font-medium mb-4">Advanced Example</h3>
1683: 					<p className="text-muted-foreground mb-4">Advanced configuration:</p>
1684: 					<pre className="text-sm overflow-auto p-4 bg-muted rounded-lg">
1685: 						{examples.advanced}
1686: 					</pre>
1687: 				</>
1688: 			),
1689: 		}
1690: 	];
1691: 
1692: 	return <TabsContainer items={items} defaultValue="basic" />;
1693: }
1694: ```
1695: 
1696: ## Troubleshooting
1697: 
1698: 1. **Hydration Errors**:
1699: 	- Use `client:load` directive
1700: 	- Ensure consistent server/client rendering
1701: 	- Add proper mounting checks
1702: 
1703: 2. **Styling Issues**:
1704: 	- Verify Tailwind configuration
1705: 	- Check class names
1706: 	- Ensure proper CSS imports
1707: 
1708: 3. **Interactivity Problems**:
1709: 	- Check React setup
1710: 	- Verify event handlers
1711: 	- Debug state management
1712: 
1713: 4. **Performance Optimization**:
1714: 	- Lazy load tab content
1715: 	- Implement proper caching
1716: 	- Optimize bundle size
1717: 
1718: You are an expert full-stack developer proficient in TypeScript, React, and modern UI/UX frameworks (e.g., Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI, Radix UI), with particular expertise in Astro. Your task is to produce the most optimized and maintainable Astro code, following best practices and adhering to the principles of clean code and robust architecture.
1719: 
1720: ### Objective
1721: - Create an Astro solution that is not only functional but also adheres to the best practices in performance, security, and maintainability.
1722: 
1723: ### Code Style and Structure
1724: - Write concise, technical TypeScript code with accurate examples.
1725: - Use Astro components (.astro) for static content and framework components for interactive islands.
1726: - Favor iteration and modularization over code duplication.
1727: - Use descriptive variable names with auxiliary verbs (e.g., `isLoading`, `hasError`).
1728: - Structure files following Astro conventions with content collections, components, and layouts.
1729: - Use upercase for components e.g., `components/Chat`).
1730: 
1731: ### Optimization and Best Practices
1732: - Minimize client-side JavaScript using Astro's partial hydration with client:* directives.
1733: - Use appropriate client directives (client:load, client:idle, client:visible) based on component needs.
1734: - Implement View Transitions API for smooth page transitions.
1735: - Optimize images using Astro's built-in image optimization.
1736: - Leverage Astro's content collections for structured content management.
1737: 
1738: ### Error Handling and Validation
1739: - Prioritize error handling and edge cases:
1740:   - Use early returns for error conditions.
1741:   - Implement guard clauses to handle preconditions and invalid states early.
1742:   - Use custom error types for consistent error handling.
1743: 
1744: ### UI and Styling
1745: - Use modern UI frameworks (e.g., Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI) with proper Astro integration.
1746: - Implement consistent design and responsive patterns across platforms.
1747: - Utilize Astro's scoped styling capabilities when appropriate.
1748: 
1749: ### State Management and Data Fetching
1750: - Use Astro.props for component data passing.
1751: - Implement getStaticPaths() for dynamic route generation.
1752: - Use content collections API for structured content management.
1753: - Implement validation using Zod for schema validation.
1754: 
1755: ### Security and Performance
1756: - Leverage Astro's built-in security features and zero-JS-by-default approach.
1757: - Follow performance optimization techniques using Astro's static site generation.
1758: - Implement proper CSP headers and security best practices.
1759: 
1760: ### Testing and Documentation
1761: - Write unit tests for components using appropriate testing frameworks.
1762: - Provide clear and concise comments for complex logic.
1763: - Use JSDoc comments for functions and components to improve IDE intellisense.
1764: 
1765: ### Methodology
1766: 1. **System 2 Thinking**: Approach the problem with analytical rigor. Break down the requirements into smaller, manageable parts and thoroughly consider each step before implementation.
1767: 2. **Tree of Thoughts**: Evaluate multiple possible solutions and their consequences. Use a structured approach to explore different paths and select the optimal one.
1768: 3. **Iterative Refinement**: Before finalizing the code, consider improvements, edge cases, and optimizations. Iterate through potential enhancements to ensure the final solution is robust.
1769: 
1770: **Process**:
1771: 1. **Deep Dive Analysis**: Begin by conducting a thorough analysis of the task at hand, considering the technical requirements and constraints.
1772: 2. **Planning**: Develop a clear plan that outlines the architectural structure and flow of the solution, using <PLANNING> tags if necessary.
1773: 3. **Implementation**: Implement the solution step-by-step, ensuring that each part adheres to Astro's best practices.
1774: 4. **Review and Optimize**: Perform a review of the code, looking for opportunities to reduce client-side JavaScript and optimize performance.
1775: 5. **Finalization**: Finalize the code by ensuring it meets all requirements, maximizes static generation, and follows Astro's performance-first philosophy.

1778:     ---
1779: title: Chat System
1780: description: Comprehensive guide to ONE's AI-powered chat system
1781: date: 2024-02-02
1782: section: Core Features
1783: order: 1
1784: ---
1785: 
1786: # Chat System Overview
1787: 
1788: ONE's chat system combines Astro, React, and the Assistant UI framework to deliver a powerful, flexible, and user-friendly chat interface with advanced AI capabilities.
1789: 
1790: ## Architecture
1791: 
1792: The chat system is built on a modular architecture with several key components:
1793: 
1794: ### 1. Frontend Components
1795: 
1796: #### Layout System
1797: - **Panel Modes**:
1798:   - `quarter`: 25% width side panel (default)
1799:   - `half`: 50% width side panel
1800:   - `full`: Full screen chat interface
1801:   - `floating`: Detached floating window
1802:   - `icon`: Minimized chat button
1803:   - `hidden`: No chat interface
1804: 
1805: - **Responsive Behavior**:
1806:   ```typescript
1807:   interface LayoutProps {
1808:     title: string;
1809:     description?: string;
1810:     header?: boolean;
1811:     footer?: boolean;
1812:     rightPanelMode?: 'hidden' | 'full' | 'half' | 'quarter' | 'floating' | 'icon';
1813:     chatConfig?: ChatConfig;
1814:     content?: string;
1815:   }
1816:   ```
1817: 
1818: #### Chat Components
1819: 
1820: ##### Main Chat Page (`src/pages/chat.astro`)
1821: - Entry point for the chat interface
1822: - Configurable settings:
1823:   - System prompts
1824:   - Welcome messages
1825:   - Quick suggestions
1826:   - Layout modes
1827: - Integration with page content
1828: - AI context management
1829: 
1830: ##### Thread Component (`src/components/chat/thread.tsx`)
1831: - Core chat interface features:
1832:   - Scrollable message area
1833:   - Dynamic composition interface
1834:   - Customizable welcome screen
1835:   - Message styling and actions
1836:   - Branch navigation
1837:   - Voice synthesis
1838: 
1839: ### 2. Backend Architecture
1840: 
1841: #### Chat API (`src/pages/api/chat.ts`)
1842: - OpenAI API integration
1843: - Configurable parameters:
1844:   ```typescript
1845:   interface ChatAPIConfig {
1846:     provider: "openai";
1847:     model: string;
1848:     apiEndpoint: string;
1849:     temperature: number;
1850:     maxTokens: number;
1851:     systemPrompt: string | SystemPrompt[];
1852:     contextData?: string;
1853:     functions?: ChatFunction[];
1854:   }
1855:   ```
1856: - Edge runtime optimization
1857: - Error handling and recovery
1858: - Response streaming
1859: 
1860: ## Advanced Features
1861: 
1862: ### 1. Message Management
1863: - Real-time streaming responses
1864: - Markdown and code rendering
1865: - Message editing and history
1866: - Branch navigation
1867: - Copy functionality
1868: - Voice synthesis
1869: - Code syntax highlighting
1870: 
1871: ### 2. User Interface Modes
1872: 
1873: #### Quarter Mode (Default)
1874: ```typescript
1875: <Layout rightPanelMode="quarter">
1876:   <YourContent />
1877: </Layout>
1878: ```
1879: - 25% width side panel
1880: - Ideal for documentation and content-heavy pages
1881: - Maintains content visibility
1882: 
1883: #### Floating Mode
1884: ```typescript
1885: <Layout rightPanelMode="floating">
1886:   <YourContent />
1887: </Layout>
1888: ```
1889: - Detached window
1890: - Draggable interface
1891: - Minimal content interference
1892: 
1893: #### Icon Mode
1894: ```typescript
1895: <Layout rightPanelMode="icon">
1896:   <YourContent />
1897: </Layout>
1898: ```
1899: - Minimized chat button
1900: - Expands on click
1901: - Maximum content space
1902: 
1903: ### 3. Configuration System
1904: 
1905: #### Basic Configuration
1906: ```typescript
1907: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
1908:   systemPrompt: [{
1909:     type: "text",
1910:     text: "You are a helpful assistant."
1911:   }],
1912:   welcome: {
1913:     message: "👋 How can I help you today?",
1914:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
1915:     suggestions: [
1916:       {
1917:         label: "Get Started",
1918:         prompt: "How do I get started?"
1919:       }
1920:     ]
1921:   }
1922: });
1923: ```
1924: 
1925: #### Advanced Configuration
1926: ```typescript
1927: const advancedConfig = {
1928:   provider: "openai",
1929:   model: "gpt-4o-mini",
1930:   temperature: 0.7,
1931:   maxTokens: 2000,
1932:   features: {
1933:     textToSpeech: true,
1934:     codeHighlight: true,
1935:     markdown: true,
1936:     suggestions: true,
1937:     branchNavigation: true
1938:   },
1939:   styles: {
1940:     theme: "light" | "dark" | "system",
1941:     accentColor: "#0066FF",
1942:     messageSpacing: "comfortable" | "compact"
1943:   }
1944: };
1945: ```

1947: ---
1948: title: Create a Chatbot with Markdown
1949: description: Step-by-step guide to creating an AI chatbot using markdown files
1950: date: 2024-02-02
1951: section: Tutorials
1952: order: 3
1953: ---
1954: 
1955: # Creating a Chatbot with Markdown
1956: 
1957: This tutorial will show you how to create a specialized AI chatbot using markdown files in ONE. We'll use the license page as an example to demonstrate how to create a knowledgeable AI assistant for your content.
1958: 
1959: ## Step 1: Create Your Markdown File
1960: 
1961: Create a new markdown file in your pages directory (e.g., `src/pages/your-page.md`):
1962: 
1963: ```markdown
1964: ---
1965: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
1966: title: "Your Page Title"
1967: description: "Your page description"
1968: chatConfig:
1969:   provider: openai
1970:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
1971:   apiEndpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v1"
1972:   temperature: 0.7
1973:   maxTokens: 4000
1974:   systemPrompt:
1975:     - type: text
1976:       text: "Define your AI assistant's role and expertise here"
1977:   welcome:
1978:     message: "👋 Your welcome message here"
1979:     avatar: "/your-icon.svg"
1980:     suggestions:
1981:       - label: "First Option"
1982:         prompt: "What would you like to know about...?"
1983: ---
1984: 
1985: # Your Content Here
1986: ```
1987: 
1988: ## Step 2: Configure the Chat System
1989: 
1990: ### Basic Configuration
1991: 
1992: In the frontmatter section of your markdown file, configure these essential parameters:
1993: 
1994: ```yaml
1995: chatConfig:
1996:   provider: openai           # AI provider
1997:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"      # Model to use
1998:   temperature: 0.7          # Response creativity (0-1)
1999:   maxTokens: 4000          # Maximum response length
2000: ```
2001: 
2002: ### Define the AI's Role
2003: 
2004: Create a clear system prompt that defines your AI's expertise:
2005: 
2006: ```yaml
2007: systemPrompt:
2008:   - type: text
2009:     text: "You are an expert in [your topic] focused on helping visitors understand [specific aspects]. You provide clear, accurate information about [key areas]."
2010: ```
2011: 
2012: Example from the license page:
2013: ```yaml
2014: systemPrompt:
2015:   - type: text
2016:     text: "You are a licensing expert focused on helping visitors understand the ONE License terms and benefits. You provide clear, accurate information about licensing terms, commercial rights, and usage requirements."
2017: ```
2018: 
2019: ### Set Up the Welcome Screen
2020: 
2021: Configure the initial interaction:
2022: 
2023: ```yaml
2024: welcome:
2025:   message: "👋 Your greeting message here"
2026:   avatar: "/path/to/icon.svg"
2027:   suggestions:
2028:     - label: "💡 First Option"
2029:       prompt: "What would you like to know about...?"
2030:     - label: "🚀 Second Option"
2031:       prompt: "Another suggested question..."
2032: ```
2033: 
2034: ## Step 3: Structure Your Content
2035: 
2036: Organize your markdown content to help the AI understand the topic:
2037: 
2038: 1. **Clear Headings**
2039:    ```markdown
2040:    # Main Title
2041:    
2042:    ## Key Section
2043:    
2044:    ### Subsection
2045:    ```
2046: 
2047: 2. **Structured Information**
2048:    ```markdown
2049:    ## Key Points
2050:    
2051:    - **First Point** - Detailed explanation
2052:    - **Second Point** - More details
2053:    ```
2054: 
2055: 3. **Organized Sections**
2056:    ```markdown
2057:    ## Topic Area
2058:    
2059:    1. **Main Concept**
2060:       - Detail one
2061:       - Detail two
2062:    
2063:    2. **Another Concept**
2064:       - More information
2065:       - Additional details
2066:    ```
2067: 
2068: ## Step 4: Add Interactive Elements
2069: 
2070: Include elements that enhance user interaction:
2071: 
2072: ### Quick Access Buttons
2073: 
2074: ```yaml
2075: suggestions:
2076:   - label: "💡 Key Feature"
2077:     prompt: "Tell me about this feature"
2078:   - label: "🚀 Getting Started"
2079:     prompt: "How do I begin?"
2080:   - label: "⚖️ Requirements"
2081:     prompt: "What are the requirements?"
2082: ```
2083: 
2084: ### Contact Information
2085: 
2086: ```markdown
2087: Contact [support@example.com](mailto:support@example.com) for assistance.
2088: ```
2089: 
2090: ## Real-World Example
2091: 
2092: Here's how the license page implements these concepts:
2093: 
2094: ```markdown
2095: ---
2096: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
2097: title: "ONE License"
2098: description: "Maximum Freedom. Zero Restrictions"
2099: chatConfig:
2100:   provider: openai
2101:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
2102:   apiEndpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v1"
2103:   temperature: 0.7
2104:   maxTokens: 4000
2105:   systemPrompt:
2106:     - type: text
2107:       text: "You are a licensing expert focused on helping visitors understand the ONE License terms and benefits. You provide clear, accurate information about licensing terms, commercial rights, and usage requirements."
2108:   welcome:
2109:     message: "👋 Hello! I can help explain the ONE License terms and how you can use them for your business."
2110:     avatar: "/icon.svg"
2111:     suggestions:
2112:       - label: "💡 Commercial Rights"
2113:         prompt: "What commercial rights do I get with the ONE License?"
2114:       - label: "🚀 Getting Started"
2115:         prompt: "What are the steps to start using the ONE License?"
2116: ---
2117: 
2118: # ONE License (Version 1.0)
2119:

2121:

2123: 
2124: ## Key Benefits
2125: 
2126: - **✨ 100% Commercial Rights** - Sell products and services at any price point
2127: - **🚀 Full Modification Rights** - Customize and adapt the software freely

2130: ## Best Practices
2131:

2133:    - Be specific about the AI's role

2193: 
2194: # Development FAQ
2195: 
2196: Common questions and answers about developing applications with ONE framework.
2197: 
2198: ## Getting Started
2199: 
2200: ### Q: What are the minimum requirements to run ONE?
2201: **A:** You need:
2202: - Node.js 18 or higher
2203: - pnpm package manager
2204: - An OpenAI API key
2205: - Basic knowledge of Astro and React
2206: 
2207: ### Q: How do I install ONE?
2208: **A:** Use the following commands:
2209: ```bash
2210: # Create new project
2211: pnpm create astro@latest my-one-app -- --template one
2212: 
2213: # Install dependencies
2214: cd my-one-app
2215: pnpm install
2216: ```
2217: 
2218: ### Q: How do I set up my OpenAI API key?
2219: **A:** Create a `.env` file in your project root and add:
2220: ```env
2221: OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
2222: ```
2223: 
2224: ## Chat System
2225: 
2226: ### Q: How do I add a chat interface to my page?
2227: **A:** Add chat configuration to your page's frontmatter:
2228: ```yaml
2229: ---
2230: layout: ../layouts/Layout.astro
2231: chatConfig:
2232:   provider: openai
2233:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
2234:   temperature: 0.7
2235:   maxTokens: 2000
2236:   systemPrompt:
2237:     - type: text
2238:       text: "Your system prompt here"
2239: ---
2240: ```
2241: 
2242: ### Q: How do I customize the chat panel position?
2243: **A:** Use the `rightPanelMode` prop in your Layout component:
2244: ```astro
2245: <Layout
2246:   title="Your Page"
2247:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
2248:   rightPanelMode="quarter" // or "half", "full", "floating", "icon"
2249: >
2250:   <!-- Your content -->
2251: </Layout>
2252: ```
2253: 
2254: ### Q: Can I customize the welcome message and suggestions?
2255: **A:** Yes, in your chat configuration:
2256: ```yaml
2257: chatConfig:
2258:   welcome:
2259:     message: "👋 Your welcome message"
2260:     avatar: "/path/to/icon.svg"
2261:     suggestions:
2262:       - label: "💡 First Option"
2263:         prompt: "Your prompt here"
2264: ```
2265: 
2266: ## Content Management
2267: 
2268: ### Q: How do I create a chatbot for my markdown content?
2269: **A:** Create a markdown file with chat configuration in the frontmatter:
2270: ```markdown
2271: ---
2272: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
2273: title: "Your Title"
2274: chatConfig:
2275:   systemPrompt:
2276:     - type: text
2277:       text: "Define your AI's expertise"
2278: ---
2279: 
2280: Your content here
2281: ```
2282: 
2283: ### Q: How do I organize my documentation?
2284: **A:** Use the following structure:
2285: ```
2286: src/content/docs/
2287: ├── index.md         # Main documentation page
2288: ├── getting-started/ # Getting started guides
2289: ├── features/       # Feature documentation
2290: └── api/           # API documentation
2291: ```
2292: 
2293: ### Q: How do I add images and assets?
2294: **A:** Place them in the `public` directory:
2295: ```
2296: public/
2297: ├── images/    # For images
2298: ├── icons/     # For icons
2299: └── assets/    # For other assets
2300: ```
2301: 
2302: ## Styling and Theming
2303: 
2304: ### Q: How do I customize the appearance?
2305: **A:** ONE uses Tailwind CSS. Customize in `tailwind.config.mjs`:
2306: ```javascript
2307: export default {
2308:   theme: {
2309:     extend: {
2310:       colors: {
2311:         primary: {...},
2312:         secondary: {...}
2313:       }
2314:     }
2315:   }
2316: }
2317: ```
2318: 
2319: ### Q: How do I switch between light and dark themes?
2320: **A:** Use the built-in theme system:
2321: ```typescript
2322: import { useTheme } from "@/hooks/use-theme";
2323: 
2324: const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();
2325: ```
2326: 
2327: ## Performance
2328: 
2329: ### Q: How do I optimize chat performance?
2330: **A:** Several ways:
2331: 1. Use edge runtime
2332: 2. Implement proper caching
2333: 3. Optimize response sizes
2334: 4. Use streaming responses
2335: 
2336: ### Q: How do I implement caching?
2337: **A:** Use edge caching for API responses:
2338: ```typescript
2339: export const config = {
2340:   runtime: 'edge',
2341:   regions: ['all'],
2342: };
2343: ```
2344: 
2345: ## Troubleshooting
2346: 
2347: ### Q: Why isn't my chat interface showing up?
2348: **A:** Check these common issues:
2349: 1. Verify chatConfig in frontmatter
2350: 2. Ensure OpenAI API key is set
2351: 3. Check for console errors
2352: 4. Verify rightPanelMode setting
2353: 
2354: ### Q: Why are my API calls failing?
2355: **A:** Common solutions:
2356: 1. Verify API key in .env
2357: 2. Check API endpoint configuration
2358: 3. Verify rate limits
2359: 4. Check network connectivity
2360: 
2361: ### Q: How do I debug streaming responses?
2362: **A:** Use the browser's network tab:
2363: 1. Open DevTools
2364: 2. Go to Network tab
2365: 3. Filter for 'Fetch/XHR'
2366: 4. Look for streaming responses
2367: 
2368: ## Deployment
2369: 
2370: ### Q: How do I deploy my ONE application?
2371: **A:** Several options:
2372: 1. Vercel (recommended)
2373: 2. Netlify
2374: 3. CloudFlare
2375: 4. Custom server
2376: 
2377: ### Q: How do I handle environment variables in production?
2378: **A:** Set them in your hosting platform:
2379: ```env
2380: OPENAI_API_KEY=production_key
2381: API_ENDPOINT=production_endpoint
2382: ```
2383: 
2384: ## Development Best Practices
2385: 
2386: ### Q: What's the recommended way to structure a large application?
2387: **A:** Follow this structure:
2388: ```
2389: src/
2390: ├── components/    # Reusable components
2391: ├── layouts/       # Page layouts
2392: ├── content/       # Markdown content
2393: ├── pages/         # Routes
2394: ├── styles/        # Global styles
2395: └── lib/          # Utilities
2396: ```
2397: 
2398: ### Q: How do I implement proper error handling?
2399: **A:** Use try-catch blocks and error boundaries:
2400: ```typescript
2401: try {
2402:   // API calls
2403: } catch (error) {
2404:   if (error.response?.status === 429) {
2405:     // Handle rate limiting
2406:   }
2407:   // Handle other errors
2408: }
2409: ```
2410: 
2411: ### Q: How do I test my AI interactions?
2412: **A:** Use test modes and mock responses:
2413: ```typescript
2414: const testConfig = {
2415:   ...chatConfig,
2416:   provider: 'test',
2417:   mockResponses: [...]
2418: };
2419: ```
2420: 
2421: ## Commercial Usage
2422: 
2423: ### Q: Can I use ONE in a commercial project?
2424: **A:** Yes, ONE License provides:
2425: - Full commercial rights
2426: - White-label options
2427: - No royalty fees
2428: - Enterprise support
2429: 
2430: ### Q: How do I remove ONE branding?
2431: **A:** Contact [agent@one.ie](mailto:agent@one.ie) for white-label rights.
2432: 
2433: ## Support and Resources
2434: 
2435: ### Q: Where can I get help?
2436: **A:** Several options:
2437: 1. [Documentation](/docs)
2438: 3. [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/one-ie/one/issues)
2439: 4. Email support@one.ie
2440: 
2441: ### Q: How do I report bugs?
2442: **A:** Open an issue on GitHub with:
2443: - Description of the problem
2444: - Steps to reproduce
2445: - Expected vs actual behavior
2446: - Environment details

2449: title: How it works
2450: description: Detailed explanation of ONE's architecture and operation
2451: date: 2024-02-02
2452: section: Introduction
2453: order: 2
2454: ---
2455: 
2456: # How ONE Works
2457: 
2458: ONE is a comprehensive framework for building AI-powered web applications with Astro. It combines high-performance static site generation with dynamic AI capabilities to create intelligent, responsive web experiences.
2459: 
2460: ## Core Architecture
2461: 
2462: ### Tech Stack
2463: - **Astro** - The core framework that enables high-performance static site generation
2464: - **React** - Used for interactive components and UI elements
2465: - **Assistant UI** - Provides the chat interface and AI interaction components
2466: - **Vercel AI SDK** - Handles AI model integration and streaming responses
2467: - **Tailwind CSS** - For responsive and customizable styling
2468: 
2469: ### Layout System
2470: 
2471: The framework uses a flexible layout system with three main components:
2472: 
2473: 1. **Main Grid**
2474:    - Configurable grid layout system
2475:    - Support for responsive design
2476:    - Dynamic panel sizing and positioning
2477: 
2478: 2. **Panel Modes**
2479:    ```typescript
2480:    type PanelMode = 'hidden' | 'full' | 'half' | 'quarter' | 'floating' | 'icon';
2481:    ```
2482:    - `quarter`: 25% width side panel
2483:    - `half`: 50% width side panel
2484:    - `full`: Full screen display
2485:    - `floating`: Detached floating window
2486:    - `icon`: Minimized chat button
2487:    - `hidden`: No chat interface
2488: 
2489: 3. **Responsive Behavior**
2490:    - Automatic adaptation to screen sizes
2491:    - Mobile-first design approach
2492:    - Smooth transitions between states
2493: 
2494: ### AI Agent Implementation
2495: 
2496: Every page in ONE can have its own AI Agent, with specific knowledge about the page content:
2497: 
2498: 1. **Configuration Layer**
2499: ```typescript
2500: {
2501:     "provider": "openai",
2502:     "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
2503:     "apiEndpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
2504:     "runtime": "edge",
2505:     "temperature": 0.7,
2506:     "maxTokens": 2000,
2507:     "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful AI assistant.",
2508:     "userPrompt": "main content of the markdown file below"
2509: }
2510: ```
2511: 
2512: 2. **Chat Interface Layer**
2513: - Real-time message streaming
2514: - Markdown rendering
2515: - Message history and branching
2516: - Text-to-speech capabilities
2517: - Code syntax highlighting
2518: - Copy/edit functionality
2519: 
2520: 3. **Edge Runtime Layer**
2521: - Edge-based processing
2522: - Efficient data streaming
2523: - Optimized response handling
2524: 
2525: ## Content Management
2526: 
2527: ### 1. Blog System
2528: - Markdown-based content
2529: - Multiple view modes (list, grid, magazine)
2530: - Automatic reading time calculation
2531: - Rich media support
2532: - Category and tag organization
2533: 
2534: ### 2. Documentation System
2535: - Hierarchical structure
2536: - Section-based organization
2537: - Automated navigation
2538: - Version control support
2539: 
2540: ### 3. Page-Specific AI Agents
2541: - Contextual awareness
2542: - Custom knowledge base
2543: - Tailored responses
2544: - Dynamic suggestions
2545: 
2546: ## Advanced Features
2547: 
2548: ### 1. Real-time Interaction
2549: - Streaming responses
2550: - Interactive components
2551: - Dynamic content updates
2552: - Branch navigation
2553: - Message history
2554: 
2555: ### 2. UI Components
2556: - Floating chat interface
2557: - Customizable welcome screen
2558: - Quick suggestion buttons
2559: - Progress indicators
2560: - Error states
2561: 
2562: ### 3. Performance Optimization
2563: - Edge computing
2564: - Asset optimization
2565: - Lazy loading
2566: - Caching strategies
2567: - Response streaming
2568: 
2569: ## Configuration Examples
2570: 
2571: ### 1. Basic Chat Setup
2572: ```typescript
2573: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
2574:   systemPrompt: [{
2575:     type: "text",
2576:     text: "You are a helpful AI assistant."
2577:   }],
2578:   welcome: {
2579:     message: "👋 How can I help you today?",
2580:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
2581:     suggestions: [
2582:       {
2583:         label: "Get Started",
2584:         prompt: "How do I get started with ONE?"
2585:       }
2586:     ]
2587:   }
2588: });
2589: ```
2590: 
2591: ### 2. Custom Layout Configuration
2592: ```typescript
2593: <Layout 
2594:   title="Your Page"
2595:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
2596:   rightPanelMode="quarter"
2597:   header={true}
2598:   footer={true}
2599: >
2600:   {/* Your content */}
2601: </Layout>
2602: ```
2603: 
2604: ### 3. Page-Specific Agent
2605: ```typescript
2606: const pageSpecificAgent = {
2607:   systemPrompt: `You are an expert on ${topic}...`,
2608:   contextData: pageContent,
2609:   parameters: {
2610:     temperature: 0.7,
2611:     maxTokens: 2000
2612:   }
2613: };
2614: ```
2615: # Content Collections
2616: 
2617: - **Schema Definitions**: Continue using `src/content/config.ts` with `zod` for type-safe content validation.
2618: - **Content Queries**: Utilize `getCollection()` for type-safe content retrieval.
2619: - **Frontmatter Schemas**: Define schemas using `defineCollection`.
2620: - **Single Entry Retrieval**: Employ `getEntryBySlug` for fetching individual entries.
2621: - **Content Relationships**: Leverage collection references to establish relationships between content items.
2622: 
2623: # View Transitions
2624: 
2625: - **Implementation**: Use `transition:name` and `transition:animate` directives to define view transitions.
2626: - **State Persistence**: Apply `transition:persist` to maintain component state during page transitions.
2627: - **Animation Configuration**: Set animations with `transition:animate="slide|fade|none"`.
2628: - **Event Handling**: Manage transition events using `document.addEventListener('astro:page-load')`.
2629: - **Prop Preservation**: Use `transition:persist-props` to retain specific props during transitions.
2630: 
2631: # Islands Architecture
2632: 
2633: - **Immediate Interactivity**: Apply `client:load` for components requiring immediate interactivity.
2634: - **Deferred Hydration**: Use `client:visible` for components that can delay hydration until visible.
2635: - **Client-Only Components**: Implement `client:only` when server-side rendering is unnecessary.
2636: - **Responsive Hydration**: Utilize `client:media` for components that hydrate based on media queries.
2637: - **Idle Hydration**: Leverage `client:idle` for non-critical interactive components.
2638: 
2639: # Server-Side Features
2640: 
2641: - **Cookies Management**: Use `Astro.cookies` to handle server-side cookies.
2642: - **Middleware**: Implement middleware with `defineMiddleware()` in `src/middleware`.
2643: - **Request Access**: Access request details via `Astro.request` in server endpoints.
2644: - **Dynamic Routes**: Handle dynamic routes using the `[...spread].astro` pattern.
2645: - **API Endpoints**: Create API endpoints in `src/pages/api` using `Response` objects.
2646: 
2647: # Image Optimization
2648: 
2649: - **Image Component**: Use the `Image` component with `src`, `alt`, and `width/height` props.
2650: - **Picture Component**: Implement the `Picture` component for art direction.
2651: - **Service Configuration**: Configure the image service in `astro.config.mjs`.
2652: - **Modern Formats**: Use `format="avif,webp"` for modern image formats.
2653: - **Responsive Images**: Apply the `densities` prop for responsive images.
2654: 
2655: # Integration System
2656: 
2657: - **Framework Integrations**: Configure integrations in `astro.config.mjs`.
2658: - **Deployment Adapters**: Use adapters like `adapter-vercel`, `adapter-netlify`, or `adapter-node` for deployment.
2659: - **Vite Plugins**: Implement Vite plugins through Astro integrations.
2660: - **UI Frameworks**: Configure renderers for UI frameworks as needed.
2661: - **Environment Variables**: Handle integration-specific environment variables appropriately.
2662: 
2663: # Routing and Pages
2664: 
2665: - **File-Based Routing**: Place pages in `src/pages` for automatic routing.
2666: - **Dynamic Parameters**: Use `[param].astro` for dynamic route parameters.
2667: - **Rest Parameters**: Implement `[...spread].astro` for rest parameters in routes.
2668: - **Redirects**: Handle redirects using `Astro.redirect`.
2669: - **Nested Layouts**: Implement nested layouts using slot patterns.
2670: 
2671: # Dos
2672: 
2673: - **Static Path Generation**: Use `getStaticPaths` for generating static paths.
2674: - **Hydration Strategies**: Implement appropriate island hydration strategies.
2675: - **Type-Safe Content**: Utilize content collections for type-safe content management.
2676: - **View Transitions**: Configure view transitions appropriately.
2677: - **SSR Capabilities**: Leverage server-side rendering capabilities effectively.
2678: 
2679: # Don'ts
2680: 
2681: - **Overusing `client:load`**: Avoid using `client:load` when `client:visible` suffices.
2682: - **Mixing SSR and `client:only`**: Never mix server-side rendering and `client:only` in the same component.
2683: - **Redundant Queries**: Avoid unnecessary content collection queries.
2684: - **Skipping Animations**: Don't skip view transition animations without reason.
2685: - **Bypassing Image Optimization**: Never bypass Astro's image optimization features.
2686: 
2687: By incorporating these practices, you can effectively leverage the features introduced in Astro 5.5 to enhance your project's performance and maintainability.
`````

 23: interface ChatInputProps extends Omit<ChatInputContextValue, "variant"> {
 24:   children: React.ReactNode;
 25:   className?: string;
 26:   variant?: "default" | "unstyled";
 27:   rows?: number;
 28: 
 29:   onImageChange?: (fileData: string | null) => void;
 30: }
 31: 
 32: const ChatInput = function ChatInput({
 33:   children,
 34:   className,
 35:   variant = "default",
 36:   value,
 37:   onChange,
 38:   onSubmit,
 39:   loading,
 40:   onStop,
 41:   rows = 1,
 42:   onImageChange
 43: }: ChatInputProps) {
 44: 
 45:     const [imagePreview, setImagePreview] = useState<string | null>(null);
 46:     const [imageData, setImageData] = useState<string | null>(null);
 47:     const fileInputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
 48: 
 49:     const handleFileChange = (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
 50:         const file = event.target.files?.[0];
 51:         if (file && file.type.startsWith('image/')) {
 52:             const reader = new FileReader();
 53:             reader.onloadend = () => {
 54:                 const base64String = reader.result as string;
 55:                 setImagePreview(base64String);
 56:                 setImageData(base64String);
 57:                 onImageChange?.(base64String);
 58:             };
 59:             reader.readAsDataURL(file);
 60:         }
 61: 
 62:         if (fileInputRef.current) {
 63:             fileInputRef.current.value = "";
 64:         }
 65:     };
 66: 
 67:     const triggerFileInput = () => {
 68:         fileInputRef.current?.click();
 69:     };
 70: 
 71:     const removeImage = () => {
 72:         setImagePreview(null);
 73:         setImageData(null);
 74:         onImageChange?.(null); // Signal image removal
 75:         if (fileInputRef.current) {
 76:             fileInputRef.current.value = "";
 77:         }
 78:     };
 79: 
 80:   const contextValue: ChatInputContextValue = {
 81:     value,
 82:     onChange,
 83:     onSubmit,
 84:     loading,
 85:     onStop,
 86:     variant,
 87:     rows,
 88:     // You might add imageData/setImageData to context if sub-components need it
 89:   };
 90: 
 91:   return (
 92:     <ChatInputContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
 93:       {/* Hidden file input */}
 94:       <input
 95:         type="file"
 96:         ref={fileInputRef}
 97:         onChange={handleFileChange}
 98:         className="hidden"
 99:         accept="image/*"
100:       />
101:       <div
102:         className={cn(
103:           variant === "default" &&
104:             "flex items-end gap-2 w-full p-3 rounded-lg bg-[#2a2a2a] focus-within:ring-1 focus-within:ring-blue-600/30 focus-within:outline-none transition-all duration-200 shadow-md hover:shadow-lg",
105:           variant === "unstyled" && "flex items-end gap-2 w-full",
106:           className,
107:         )}
108:       >
109:         {}
110:         {imagePreview && (
111:           <div className="relative mb-1 shrink-0">
112:             <img src={imagePreview} alt="Preview" className="h-12 w-12 rounded object-cover" />
113:             <Button
114:               variant="destructive"
115:               size="icon"
116:               className="absolute -top-2 -right-2 h-5 w-5 rounded-full"
117:               onClick={removeImage}
118:             >
119:               <XIcon className="h-3 w-3" />
120:             </Button>
121:           </div>
122:         )}
123: 
124:         {}
125:         <Button
126:           variant="ghost"
127:           size="icon"
128:           className="h-10 w-10 shrink-0 rounded-full"
129:           onClick={triggerFileInput}
130:         >
131:           <Paperclip className="h-5 w-5" />
132:         </Button>
133: 
134:         {}
135:         {children}
136:       </div>
137:     </ChatInputContext.Provider>
138:   );
139: };
140: 
141: ChatInput.displayName = "ChatInput";
142: 
143: interface ChatInputTextAreaProps extends React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof Textarea> {
144:   value?: string;
145:   onChange?: React.ChangeEventHandler<HTMLTextAreaElement>;
146:   onSubmit?: () => void;
147:   variant?: "default" | "unstyled";
148: }
149: 
150: const ChatInputTextArea = forwardRef<HTMLTextAreaElement, ChatInputTextAreaProps>(
151:   ({
152:     onSubmit: onSubmitProp,
153:     value: valueProp,
154:     onChange: onChangeProp,
155:     className,
156:     variant: variantProp,
157:     ...props
158:   }, forwardedRef) => {
159:     const context = useContext(ChatInputContext);
160:     const value = valueProp ?? context.value ?? "";
161:     const onChange = onChangeProp ?? context.onChange;
162:     const onSubmit = onSubmitProp ?? context.onSubmit;
163:     const rows = context.rows ?? 1;
164: 
165:     // Convert parent variant to textarea variant unless explicitly overridden
166:     const variant =
167:       variantProp ?? (context.variant === "default" ? "unstyled" : "default");
168: 
169: 
170:     const resizeRef = useTextareaResize(value, rows);
171: 
172: 
173:     useEffect(() => {
174:       if (!forwardedRef || !resizeRef.current) return;
175: 
176:       if (typeof forwardedRef === 'function') {
177:         forwardedRef(resizeRef.current);
178:       } else {
179:         forwardedRef.current = resizeRef.current;
180:       }
181:     }, [forwardedRef]);
182: 
183:     const handleKeyDown = (e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
184:       if (!onSubmit) return;
185:       if (e.key === "Enter" && !e.shiftKey) {
186:         if (typeof value !== "string" || value.trim().length === 0) return;
187:         e.preventDefault();
188:         onSubmit();
189:       }
190:     };
191: 
192:     return (
193:       <Textarea
194:         ref={resizeRef}
195:         {...props}
196:         value={value}
197:         onChange={onChange}
198:         onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
199:         className={cn(
200:           "flex-1 max-h-[80px] min-h-0 resize-none overflow-x-hidden text-base transition-all duration-200 text-white placeholder:text-gray-400 bg-transparent",
201:           variant === "unstyled" &&
202:             "border-none focus-visible:ring-0 focus-visible:ring-offset-0 shadow-none",
203:           className,
204:         )}
205:         rows={rows}
206:       />
207:     );
208:   }
209: );
210: 
211: ChatInputTextArea.displayName = "ChatInputTextArea";
212: 
213: interface ChatInputSubmitProps extends React.ComponentProps<typeof Button> {
214:   onSubmit?: () => void;
215:   loading?: boolean;
216:   onStop?: () => void;
217: }
218: 
219: const ChatInputSubmit = function ChatInputSubmit({
220:   onSubmit: onSubmitProp,
221:   loading: loadingProp,
222:   onStop: onStopProp,
223:   className,
224:   ...props
225: }: ChatInputSubmitProps) {
226:   const context = useContext(ChatInputContext);
227:   const loading = loadingProp ?? context.loading;
228:   const onStop = onStopProp ?? context.onStop;
229:   const onSubmit = onSubmitProp ?? context.onSubmit;
230: 
231:   if (loading && onStop) {
232:     return (
233:       <Button
234:         onClick={onStop}
235:         className={cn(
236:           "shrink-0 rounded-full w-10 h-10 flex items-center justify-center bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground hover:bg-destructive/90 transition-all duration-200 shadow-sm hover:shadow-md",
237:           className,
238:         )}
239:         {...props}
240:       >
241:         <StopCircleIcon className="h-5 w-5" />
242:       </Button>
243:     );
244:   }
245: 
246:   const isDisabled =
247:     typeof context.value !== "string" || context.value.trim().length === 0;
248: 
249:   return (
250:     <Button
251:       className={cn(
252:         "shrink-0 rounded-full w-10 h-10 flex items-center justify-center bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 text-white transition-all duration-200 shadow-sm hover:shadow-md",
253:         isDisabled ? "opacity-50" : "animate-subtle-bounce",
254:         className,
255:       )}
256:       disabled={isDisabled}
257:       onClick={(event) => {
258:         event.preventDefault();
259:         if (!isDisabled) {
260:           onSubmit?.();
261:         }
262:       }}
263:       {...props}
264:     >
265:       <SendIcon className="h-5 w-5" />
266:     </Button>
267:   );
268: };
269: 
270: ChatInputSubmit.displayName = "ChatInputSubmit";
271: 
272: export {
273:   ChatInput,
274:   ChatInputTextArea,
275:   ChatInputSubmit,
276:   type ChatInputProps,
277:   type ChatInputTextAreaProps,
278:   type ChatInputSubmitProps,
279: };
`````

  1: import { cn } from '../lib/utils';

  5: export function Breadcrumbs() {

  7:   const [isHome, setIsHome] = useState(false);
  8:   const [lastScrollY, setLastScrollY] = useState(0);
  9:   const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(true);
 10:

 12:     const updatePath = () => {
 13:       const currentPath = window.location.pathname;
 14:       setPathSegments(currentPath.split('/').filter(Boolean));
 15:       setIsHome(currentPath === '/');
 16:     };
 17: 
 18: 
 19:     updatePath();
 20: 
 21: 
 22:     window.addEventListener('popstate', updatePath);
 23: 
 24:     const handleClick = () => {
 25:       setTimeout(updatePath, 0);
 26:     };
 27:     document.addEventListener('click', handleClick);
 28: 
 29:     return () => {
 30:       window.removeEventListener('popstate', updatePath);
 31:       document.removeEventListener('click', handleClick);
 32:     };
 33:   }, []);
 34: 
 35:   useEffect(() => {
 36:     const handleScroll = () => {
 37:       const currentScrollY = window.scrollY;
 38:       setIsVisible(currentScrollY < lastScrollY || currentScrollY < 10);
 39:       setLastScrollY(currentScrollY);
 40:     };
 41: 
 42:     window.addEventListener('scroll', handleScroll, { passive: true });
 43:     return () => window.removeEventListener('scroll', handleScroll);
 44:   }, [lastScrollY]);
 45: 
 46:   interface Breadcrumb {
 47:     text: React.ReactNode;
 48:     href: string;
 49:     key?: string;
 50:   }
 51: 
 52:   const breadcrumbs: Breadcrumb[] = [
 53:     { text: <Home className="h-4 w-4" />, href: '/', key: 'home' }
 54:   ];
 55: 
 56: 
 57:   if (pathSegments[0]) {
 58:     const section = pathSegments[0];
 59:     if (section === 'blog' || section === 'docs') {
 60:       breadcrumbs.push({
 61:         text: section.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + section.slice(1),
 62:         href: `/${section}`,
 63:         key: section
 64:       });
 65:     }
 66:   }
 67: 
 68: 
 69:   for (let i = 1; i < pathSegments.length - 1; i++) {
 70:     const segment = pathSegments[i];
 71:     breadcrumbs.push({
 72:       key: segment,
 73:       text: segment
 74:         .split('-')
 75:         .map(word => word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1))
 76:         .join(' '),
 77:       href: '/' + pathSegments.slice(0, i + 1).join('/')
 78:     });
 79:   }
 80: 
 81: 
 82:   const currentPage = pathSegments[pathSegments.length - 1];
 83:   if (currentPage && pathSegments.length > 0) {
 84:     breadcrumbs.push({
 85:       key: currentPage,
 86:       text: currentPage
 87:         .split('-')
 88:         .map(word => word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1))
 89:         .join(' '),
 90:       href: '/' + pathSegments.join('/')
 91:     });
 92:   }
 93: 
 94: 
 95:   if (isHome) return null;
 96: 
 97: 
 98:   if (breadcrumbs.length <= 1) return null;
 99: 
100:   return (
101:     <div className={cn(
102:       "h-16",
103:       "flex items-center",
104:       "bg-transparent",
105:       "transition-opacity duration-300",
106:       isVisible ? "opacity-100" : "opacity-0"
107:     )}>
108:       <nav
109:         aria-label="Breadcrumb"
110:         className="flex items-center px-4 gap-2 text-sm text-muted-foreground"
111:       >
112:         {breadcrumbs.map((crumb, index) => (
113:           <div key={crumb.key || crumb.href} className="flex items-center">

117:             <a

123:               )}
124:               aria-current={index === breadcrumbs.length - 1 ? 'page' : undefined}
125:             >
126:               {crumb.text}
127:             </a>
128:           </div>
129:         ))}
130:       </nav>

133: }

105:     {
106:         outerStartAngles.map((angle, i) => (
107:             <OrbitingCircles

111:                 startAngle={angle}
112:                 path={false}

114:                 client:load

117:                     <div class="h-14 w-14 rounded-full hover:scale-110 transition-all duration-300 text-black dark:text-white">

## File: src/content/docs/content-types.md
`````markdown
  1: ---
  2: title: Content Types
  3: description: Complete guide to ONE's content collection system
  4: date: 2024-02-02
  5: section: Core Features
  6: order: 3
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Content Types System
 10: 
 11: ONE uses Astro's content collections with Zod validation to provide a powerful, type-safe content management system. This guide covers all content types, their schemas, and integration features.
 12: 
 13: ## Quick Start
 14: 
 15: ```typescript
 16: // src/content/config.ts
 17: import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content';
 18: 
 19: // Define collection with schema
 20: const blog = defineCollection({
 21:   type: 'content',
 22:   schema: z.object({
 23:     title: z.string(),
 24:     description: z.string(),
 25:     date: z.date(),
 26:     tags: z.array(z.string()).default([])
 27:   })
 28: });
 29: 
 30: // Export collections
 31: export const collections = {
 32:   blog
 33: };
 34: ```
 35: 
 36: ## Base Schema
 37: 
 38: All content types extend from common base fields:
 39: 
 40: ```typescript
 41: const CommonFields = {
 42:   // Required fields
 43:   title: z.string(),
 44:   
 45:   // Optional fields
 46:   description: z.string().optional(),
 47:   date: z.date().optional(),
 48:   draft: z.boolean().default(false),
 49:   tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
 50:   image: z.string().optional(),
 51:   
 52:   // SEO fields
 53:   seo: z.object({
 54:     title: z.string().optional(),
 55:     description: z.string().optional(),
 56:     keywords: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
 57:     ogImage: z.string().optional()
 58:   }).optional()
 59: };
 60: ```
 61: 
 62: ## Content Collections
 63: 
 64: ### 1. Pages
 65: General website pages with flexible layouts.
 66: 
 67: ```typescript
 68: const PagesSchema = z.object({
 69:   ...CommonFields,
 70:   layout: z.enum(['default', 'wide', 'landing']),
 71:   sections: z.array(z.object({
 72:     id: z.string(),
 73:     type: z.enum(['hero', 'features', 'cta', 'pricing']),
 74:     content: z.record(z.unknown())
 75:   })),
 76:   menu: z.object({
 77:     visible: z.boolean(),
 78:     order: z.number()
 79:   }).optional()
 80: });
 81: 
 82: // Example usage
 83: ---
 84: title: Home Page
 85: layout: landing
 86: sections:
 87:   - id: hero
 88:     type: hero
 89:     content:
 90:       heading: "Welcome to ONE"
 91:       subheading: "Build AI-powered applications"
 92: menu:
 93:   visible: true
 94:   order: 1
 95: ---
 96: ```
 97: 
 98: ### 2. Documentation
 99: Technical documentation and guides.
100: 
101: ```typescript
102: const DocsSchema = z.object({
103:   ...CommonFields,
104:   section: z.string(),
105:   order: z.number(),
106:   prev: z.string().optional(),
107:   next: z.string().optional(),
108:   aiConfig: z.object({
109:     systemPrompt: z.string(),
110:     suggestions: z.array(z.object({
111:       label: z.string(),
112:       prompt: z.string()
113:     }))
114:   }).optional()
115: });
116: 
117: // Example usage
118: ---
119: title: Getting Started
120: section: Introduction
121: order: 1
122: aiConfig:
123:   systemPrompt: "You are a documentation expert..."
124:   suggestions:
125:     - label: "🚀 Quick Start"
126:       prompt: "Show me how to get started"
127: ---
128: ```
129: 
130: ### 3. Blog Posts
131: Rich content articles with AI assistance.
132: 
133: ```typescript
134: const BlogSchema = z.object({
135:   ...CommonFields,
136:   author: z.object({
137:     name: z.string(),
138:     avatar: z.string().optional(),
139:     bio: z.string().optional()
140:   }),
141:   category: z.string(),
142:   featured: z.boolean().default(false),
143:   aiSummary: z.boolean().default(true),
144:   relatedContent: z.array(z.string()).optional()
145: });
146: 
147: // Example usage
148: ---
149: title: Building AI Agents
150: author:
151:   name: John Doe
152:   avatar: /authors/john.jpg
153: category: Tutorials
154: featured: true
155: aiSummary: true
156: ---
157: ```
158: 
159: ### 4. Courses
160: Educational content with structured lessons.
161: 
162: ```typescript
163: const CoursesSchema = z.object({
164:   ...CommonFields,
165:   duration: z.string(),
166:   level: z.enum(['beginner', 'intermediate', 'advanced']),
167:   prerequisites: z.array(z.string()),
168:   modules: z.array(z.object({
169:     title: z.string(),
170:     lessons: z.array(z.object({
171:       title: z.string(),
172:       duration: z.string(),
173:       type: z.enum(['video', 'text', 'quiz'])
174:     }))
175:   })),
176:   instructor: z.object({
177:     name: z.string(),
178:     bio: z.string(),
179:     avatar: z.string()
180:   })
181: });
182: ```
183: 
184: ### 5. AI Prompts
185: Reusable AI conversation templates.
186: 
187: ```typescript
188: const PromptsSchema = z.object({
189:   ...CommonFields,
190:   category: z.string(),
191:   systemPrompt: z.string(),
192:   examples: z.array(z.object({
193:     user: z.string(),
194:     assistant: z.string()
195:   })),
196:   parameters: z.object({
197:     temperature: z.number(),
198:     maxTokens: z.number()
199:   }).optional()
200: });
201: 
202: // Example usage
203: ---
204: title: Technical Interviewer
205: category: Interviews
206: systemPrompt: "You are an expert technical interviewer..."
207: examples:
208:   - user: "Tell me about your experience with TypeScript"
209:     assistant: "That's a great question..."
210: parameters:
211:   temperature: 0.7
212:   maxTokens: 2000
213: ---
214: ```
215: 
216: ## Stream Integration
217: 
218: The stream system unifies content from all collections:
219: 
220: ```typescript
221: // src/lib/stream.ts
222: import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';
223: 
224: export type StreamItem = {
225:   id: string;
226:   type: string;
227:   title: string;
228:   description?: string;
229:   date: Date;
230:   data: unknown;
231: };
232: 
233: export async function getStream(options?: {
234:   limit?: number;
235:   offset?: number;
236:   filter?: (item: StreamItem) => boolean;
237: }): Promise<StreamItem[]> {
238:   // Fetch from all collections
239:   const [blog, docs, courses] = await Promise.all([
240:     getCollection('blog'),
241:     getCollection('docs'),
242:     getCollection('courses')
243:   ]);
244: 
245:   // Combine and transform
246:   const items: StreamItem[] = [
247:     ...blog.map(post => ({
248:       id: post.id,
249:       type: 'blog',
250:       title: post.data.title,
251:       date: post.data.date,
252:       data: post.data
253:     })),
254:     // ... transform other collections
255:   ];
256: 
257:   // Sort by date
258:   items.sort((a, b) => b.date.getTime() - a.date.getTime());
259: 
260:   // Apply options
261:   let result = items;
262:   if (options?.filter) {
263:     result = result.filter(options.filter);
264:   }
265:   if (options?.offset) {
266:     result = result.slice(options.offset);
267:   }
268:   if (options?.limit) {
269:     result = result.slice(0, options.limit);
270:   }
271: 
272:   return result;
273: }
274: ```
275: 
276: ## AI Integration
277: 
278: Each content type can include AI-specific configuration:
279: 
280: ```typescript
281: const AIConfig = z.object({
282:   // System behavior
283:   systemPrompt: z.string(),
284:   
285:   // Quick suggestions
286:   suggestions: z.array(z.object({
287:     label: z.string(),
288:     prompt: z.string()
289:   })),
290:   
291:   // Content processing
292:   summarize: z.boolean().default(true),
293:   generateKeywords: z.boolean().default(true),
294:   
295:   // Response configuration
296:   temperature: z.number().default(0.7),
297:   maxTokens: z.number().default(2000)
298: });
299: ```
300: 
301: ## Best Practices
302: 
303: 1. **Schema Organization**
304:    - Keep schemas modular and reusable
305:    - Use common fields consistently
306:    - Document schema properties
307: 
308: 2. **Content Structure**
309:    - Organize content logically
310:    - Use clear, descriptive filenames
311:    - Follow naming conventions
312: 
313: 3. **Type Safety**
314:    - Always use Zod validation
315:    - Define explicit types
316:    - Handle optional fields properly
317: 
318: 4. **AI Integration**
319:    - Configure AI per content type
320:    - Provide clear system prompts
321:    - Include helpful suggestions
322: 
323: 5. **Performance**
324:    - Use appropriate collection types
325:    - Optimize image assets
326:    - Implement proper caching
327: 
328: ## Troubleshooting
329: 
330: 1. **Schema Validation**
331:    ```typescript
332:    try {
333:      const data = schema.parse(frontmatter);
334:    } catch (error) {
335:      console.error("Validation failed:", error.issues);
336:    }
337:    ```
338: 
339: 2. **Collection Issues**
340:    - Verify file organization
341:    - Check frontmatter format
342:    - Validate schema definitions
343: 
344: 3. **Stream Problems**
345:    - Monitor memory usage
346:    - Implement pagination
347:    - Cache results appropriately
348: 
349: For more help:
350: - [Content Collections Guide](/docs/content-collections)
351: - [AI Integration Guide](/docs/ai-integration)
352: - Support: support@one.ie
`````

  1: ---
  2: import Layout from "@layouts/1.left.astro";
  3: import { Chat as ChatComponent } from "@/components/Chat";
  4: import { normalizeConfig } from "@/schema/chat";
  5: 
  6: import type { ChatConfig } from "@/schema/chat"; // Import the type
  7: 
  8: interface Props {
  9:   frontmatter?: any; // Make frontmatter optional as config might come via chatConfig prop
 10:   chatConfig?: ChatConfig; // Add chatConfig prop
 11:   // For MDX files
 12:   Content?: any;
 13:   // Raw content
 14:   content?: string;
 15: }
 16: 
 17: // Destructure props, getting chatConfig directly if passed
 18: const { chatConfig: passedChatConfig, Content, content } = Astro.props;
 19: 
 20: // Get the raw content
 21: let rawContent = '';
 22: 
 23: try {
 24:   // First try: Direct content if provided
 25:   if (content && typeof content === 'string') {
 26:     rawContent = content;
 27:     console.log('[Direct content found]', {
 28:       length: content.length,
 29:       preview: content.substring(0, 100)
 30:     });
 31:   }
 32:   
 33:   // Second try: MDX/Markdown Content component
 34:   if (!rawContent && Content?.rawContent) {
 35:     rawContent = await Content.rawContent();
 36:     console.log('[Markdown content found]', {
 37:       length: rawContent.length,
 38:       preview: rawContent.substring(0, 100)
 39:     });
 40:   }
 41:   
 42:   // Last try: Render default slot
 43:   if (!rawContent) {
 44:     rawContent = await Astro.slots.render('default');
 45:     if (rawContent) {
 46:       console.log('[Slot content found]', {
 47:         length: rawContent.length,
 48:         preview: rawContent.substring(0, 100)
 49:       });
 50:     }
 51:   }
 52: } catch (error) {
 53:   console.error('[Content extraction failed]:', error);
 54: }
 55: 
 56: // Use the passed chatConfig prop directly, merging with potential rawContent

  1: import type { APIRoute } from 'astro';
  2: import 'dotenv/config';
  3: import { openai } from "@ai-sdk/openai";
  4: import { anthropic } from "@ai-sdk/anthropic";
  5: import { mistral } from "@ai-sdk/mistral";
  6: import { openrouter } from '@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider';
  7: import { createEdgeRuntimeAPI } from "@assistant-ui/react/edge";
  8: import { type ChatConfig } from '@/schema/chat';
  9: import type { Message } from 'ai';
 10: 
 11: interface ChatRequest {
 12:   id: string;
 13:   messages: Message[];
 14:   config?: ChatConfig;
 15:   provider?: string;
 16:   model?: string;
 17:   apiEndpoint?: string;
 18:   temperature?: number;
 19:   maxTokens?: number;
 20:   systemPrompt?: string;
 21:   addSystemPrompt?: boolean;
 22:   addBusinessPrompt?: boolean;
 23:   content?: string;
 24:   attachedImageData?: string;
 25: }
 26: 
 27: interface ExtendedMessage extends Message {
 28:   role: 'system' | 'user' | 'assistant';
 29: }
 30: 
 31: const getProvider = (config: ChatRequest) => {
 32: 
 33:   const provider = config.config?.provider || config.provider || 'mistral';
 34:   const model = config.config?.model || config.model || 'mistral-large-latest';
 35: 
 36:   switch (provider) {
 37:     case 'anthropic':
 38:       if (!process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) {
 39:         throw new Error('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not configured');
 40:       }
 41:       return anthropic(model);
 42: 
 43:     case 'mistral':
 44:       if (!process.env.MISTRAL_API_KEY) {
 45:         throw new Error('MISTRAL_API_KEY not configured');
 46:       }
 47:       return mistral(model);
 48: 
 49:     case 'openrouter':
 50:       if (!process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY) {
 51:         throw new Error('OPENROUTER_API_KEY not configured');
 52:       }
 53:       return openrouter(model);
 54: 
 55:     case 'openai':
 56:     default:
 57:       if (!process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY) {
 58:         throw new Error('OPENAI_API_KEY not configured');
 59:       }
 60:       return openai(model);
 61:   }
 62: };
 63: 
 64: 
 65: const loadSystemPrompt = async (addSystemPrompt: boolean = false) => {
 66:   if (!addSystemPrompt) return '';
 67:   try {
 68:     return "You are Agent ONE, an AI assistant focused on helping users with their tasks.";
 69:   } catch (error) {
 70:     console.error('Error loading system prompt:', error);
 71:     return '';
 72:   }
 73: };
 74: 
 75: // Function to load business prompts
 76: const loadBusinessPrompt = async (addBusinessPrompt: boolean = false) => {
 77:   if (!addBusinessPrompt) return '';
 78:   try {
 79:     return "You specialize in helping businesses with commercial applications, licensing, and enterprise solutions.";
 80:   } catch (error) {
 81:     console.error('Error loading business prompt:', error);
 82:     return '';
 83:   }
 84: };
 85: 
 86: // Process system prompt from various formats
 87: const processSystemPrompt = (systemPrompt: any): string => {
 88:   if (!systemPrompt) return '';
 89: 
 90:   if (typeof systemPrompt === 'string') {
 91:     return systemPrompt;
 92:   }
 93: 
 94:   if (Array.isArray(systemPrompt)) {
 95:     return systemPrompt.map(p => {
 96:       if (typeof p === 'string') return p;
 97:       if (p && typeof p === 'object' && p.text) return p.text;
 98:       return '';
 99:     }).filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');
100:   }
101: 
102:   return '';
103: };
104: 
105: export const POST: APIRoute = async ({ request }) => {
106:   try {
107:     const requestData = await request.json() as ChatRequest;
108: 
109:     // Get the config object with proper typing
110:     const config = requestData.config || {} as ChatConfig;
111: 
112:     // Merge configuration from different sources, prioritizing direct properties over config object
113:     const provider = requestData.provider || config.provider || 'mistral';
114:     const model = requestData.model || config.model || 'mistral-large-latest';
115:     const temperature = requestData.temperature || config.temperature || 0.7;
116:     const maxTokens = requestData.maxTokens || config.maxTokens || 12000;
117: 
118: 
119:     const userSystemPrompt = processSystemPrompt(requestData.systemPrompt || config.systemPrompt || '');
120:     const addSystemPrompt = requestData.addSystemPrompt || config.addSystemPrompt || false;
121:     const addBusinessPrompt = requestData.addBusinessPrompt || config.addBusinessPrompt || false;
122: 
123:     // Get content settings
124:     const includeContent = config.includeContent !== undefined ? config.includeContent : true;
125: 
126:     // Get content if available
127:     const content = requestData.content || '';
128: 
129:     // Check environment variables early
130:     const envKey = `${provider.toUpperCase()}_API_KEY`;
131:     if (!process.env[envKey]) {
132:       throw new Error(`Missing ${envKey} in environment variables`);
133:     }
134: 
135:     // Load system and business prompts if needed
136:     const baseSystemPrompt = await loadSystemPrompt(addSystemPrompt);
137:     const businessPrompt = await loadBusinessPrompt(addBusinessPrompt);
138: 
139:     // Combine prompts
140:     let fullSystemPrompt = [baseSystemPrompt, businessPrompt, userSystemPrompt]
141:       .filter(Boolean)
142:       .join('\n\n');
143: 
144: 
145:     if (content && includeContent) {
146:       console.log('Adding content to system prompt');
147:       let processedContent = content;
148: 
149:       try {
150: 
151:         if (typeof content === 'string' && content.trim().startsWith('{')) {
152:           try {
153:             const parsed = JSON.parse(content);
154:             if (typeof parsed === 'object' && parsed !== null) {
155:               processedContent = parsed.value || parsed.content || parsed.body ||
156:                               parsed.text || JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2);
157:             }
158:           } catch (e) {
159:             console.log('Content is not valid JSON, using as-is');
160:           }
161:         }
162: 
163: 
164:         if (processedContent === '[object Object]') {
165:           processedContent = 'Error: Content could not be properly extracted';
166:         }
167: 
168: 
169:         fullSystemPrompt = `${fullSystemPrompt}\n\nPage Content:\n${processedContent}`;
170:       } catch (e) {
171:         console.error('Error processing content:', e);
172:         fullSystemPrompt = `${fullSystemPrompt}\n\nError: Could not process page content`;
173:       }
174:     }
175: 
176: 
177:     let messages: ExtendedMessage[] = [...requestData.messages] as ExtendedMessage[];
178:     if (fullSystemPrompt) {
179:       messages.unshift({
180:         id: 'system-1',
181:         role: 'system',
182:         content: fullSystemPrompt
183:       });
184:     }
185: 
186: 
187:     const formattedMessages = messages.map(msg => {
188:       if (Array.isArray(msg.content) && msg.content[0]?.type === 'text') {
189:         return msg;
190:       }
191:       return {
192:         ...msg,
193:         content: [{
194:           type: 'text' as const,
195:           text: typeof msg.content === 'string' ? msg.content : JSON.stringify(msg.content)
196:         }]
197:       };
198:     });
199: 
200: 
201:     if (requestData.attachedImageData) {
202:       console.log('Including image data in the request');
203:       formattedMessages.push({
204:         id: 'image-1',
205:         role: 'user',
206:         content: [{
207:           type: 'text',
208:           text: `Image URL: ${requestData.attachedImageData}`
209:         }]
210:       });
211:     }
212: 
213:     const handler = createEdgeRuntimeAPI({
214:       model: getProvider(requestData),
215:       temperature,
216:       maxTokens
217:     });
218: 
219:     const response = await handler.POST({
220:       ...request,
221:       json: async () => ({
222:         messages: formattedMessages,
223:         functions: [],
224:         function_call: null
225:       })
226:     });
227: 
228:     if (!response.ok) {
229:       throw new Error(`Edge runtime error: ${response.statusText}`);
230:     }
231: 
232:     return response;
233: 
234:   } catch (error) {
235:     const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error occurred';
236:     console.error('Chat API error:', errorMessage);
237:     return new Response(
238:       JSON.stringify({
239:         error: errorMessage,
240:         timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
241:       }),
242:       {
243:         status: 500,
244:         headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
245:       }
246:     );
247:   }
248: };

318: function parseMarkdownIntoBlocks(markdown: string): string[] {
319: 	if (!markdown) {
320: 		return [];
321: 	}

323: 	return tokens.map((token) => token.raw);
324: }

331: const MemoizedMarkdownBlock = memo(
332: 	({ content, className }: MarkdownBlockProps) => {
333: 		return (
334: 		  <div className={className}>
335: 		    <ReactMarkdown
336: 		      remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}
337: 		      components={components}
338: 		    >
339: 		      {content}
340: 		    </ReactMarkdown>
341: 		  </div>
342: 		);
343: 	},
344: 	(prevProps, nextProps) => {
345: 		if (prevProps.content !== nextProps.content) {
346: 			return false;
347: 		}
348: 		return true;
349: 	},
350: );
351: 
352: MemoizedMarkdownBlock.displayName = "MemoizedMarkdownBlock";
353: 
354: interface MarkdownContentProps {
355: 	content: string;
356: 	id: string;
357: 	className?: string;
358: }

360: export const MarkdownContent = memo(
361: 	({ content, id, className }: MarkdownContentProps) => {
362: 		const blocks = useMemo(
363: 			() => parseMarkdownIntoBlocks(content || ""),
364: 			[content],
365: 		);
366: 
367: 		return blocks.map((block, index) => (
368: 			<MemoizedMarkdownBlock
369: 				content={block}
370: 				className={className}
371: 				key={`${id}-block_${
372: 					// biome-ignore lint/suspicious/noArrayIndexKey: <explanation>
373: 					index
374: 				}`}
375: 			/>
376: 		));
377: 	},
378: );

 96:   'bash': { color: '#d4d4d4' },

 99: };
100: 
101: export const CodeHighlighter = ({ language, children }: CodeProps) => {
102:   const customStyles = {
103:     margin: 0,
104:     width: "100%",
105:     background: "#1e1e1e",
106:     padding: "1rem",
107:     fontSize: "14px",
108:     lineHeight: "1.5",
109:     borderRadius: "0",
110:     fontFamily: "'Menlo', 'Monaco', 'Consolas', 'Courier New', monospace",
111:     overflow: "visible",
112:   };
113: 
114: 
115:   let processedCode = children;
116:   if (language === 'bash' && children.includes('npm')) {
117:     processedCode = children.replace(/npm/, '<span style="color: #9b37ff;">npm</span>');
118:   }
119: 
120:   return (
121:     <div className="relative group overflow-hidden bg-[#1e1e1e]">
122:       {}
123:       <div className="flex items-center justify-between h-8 bg-[#252526] border-b border-[#1e1e1e]">
124:         <span className="px-4 text-sm text-[#cccccc] font-mono lowercase">{language}</span>
125:         <CopyButton code={children} />
126:       </div>
127: 
128:       {}
129:       <div className="[&::-webkit-scrollbar]:hidden [-ms-overflow-style:none] [scrollbar-width:none] overflow-auto">
130:         {language === 'bash' && children.includes('npm') ? (
131:           <div
132:             style={{
133:               ...customStyles,
134:               padding: "1rem",
135:               fontFamily: "'Menlo', 'Monaco', 'Consolas', 'Courier New', monospace",
136:               fontSize: "14px",
137:             }}
138:             dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: processedCode }}
139:           />
140:         ) : (
141:           <SyntaxHighlighter
142:             language={language}
143:             style={customSyntaxTheme}
144:             customStyle={customStyles}
145:             PreTag="div"
146:             codeTagProps={{
147:               style: {
148:                 fontFamily: "'Menlo', 'Monaco', 'Consolas', 'Courier New', monospace",
149:                 fontSize: "14px",
150:               }
151:             }}
152:           >
153:             {children}
154:           </SyntaxHighlighter>
155:         )}
156:       </div>
157:       <CopyButton code={children} />
158:     </div>
159:   );
160: };
`````
